children.title: Variable-Copy Lifts
children.top_down_role: Replicated-variable formulations used to separate component dependence.

knowledge_statements.title: Variable-Copy Lifts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separable reformulation using constrained copies of a shared decision variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) be a finite-dimensional real vector space, let \(C\subseteq X\), and let \(f_i:X\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) for \(i=1,\ldots,m\). The composite problem
\[
\inf_{x\in C}\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x)
\]
has the variable-copy lift
\[
\inf_{x\in C,\ z_1,\ldots,z_m\in X}\left\{\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(z_i):z_i=x\text{ for all }i\right\}.
\]
The diagonal constraints force every copy to equal the shared variable, so feasible points correspond bijectively and preserve objective values. Consequently, both formulations have identical optimal values and corresponding minimizers, including in the extended-real setting.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Variable-copy lifting assigns each objective term its own variable and enforces equality with a shared variable, preserving feasible solutions, values, and minimizers.
assumptions_latex: All functions \(f_i\) have common domain space \(X\).
The same constraint \(x\in C\) is retained in both formulations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The original composite problem and its variable-copy lift are exactly equivalent.

notation.meaning: Copy used by the objective component \(f_i\).

children.title: Consensus-Coupling Constraints
children.top_down_role: Constraint structures that reconcile replicated variables within equivalent lifted models.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent linear and quadratic tests for agreement among graph-indexed variable copies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a finite undirected graph, let \(B\in\mathbb R^{|E|\times |V|}\) be an oriented incidence matrix, let \(L=B^{\mathsf T}B\), and stack \(x_i\in\mathbb R^d\) as \(\mathbf x\). Then
\[
(B\otimes I_d)\mathbf x=0
\iff (L\otimes I_d)\mathbf x=0
\iff \mathbf x^{\mathsf T}(L\otimes I_d)\mathbf x=0,
\]
and
\[
\mathbf x^{\mathsf T}(L\otimes I_d)\mathbf x=\sum_{\{i,j\}\in E}\|x_i-x_j\|_2^2.
\]
These conditions make \(x_i\) constant on each connected component. They give global consensus \(\mathbf x=\mathbf1\otimes z\) exactly when \(G\) is connected.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Incidence residual, Laplacian residual, and zero disagreement energy are equivalent consensus tests; connectedness is exactly what turns componentwise agreement into global agreement.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is a finite undirected graph with an arbitrary orientation.
Each local copy lies in \(\mathbb R^d\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \ker(B\otimes I_d)=\ker(L\otimes I_d),\text{ consisting of componentwise-constant vectors.}
knowledge_statements.title: Incidence and Laplacian Consensus Representations
Consensus-Coupling Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear constraints characterizing agreement among local variable copies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G=(V,E)\) be an undirected graph with an arbitrary orientation, let \(B\in\mathbb{R}^{|E|\times|V|}\) be its oriented incidence matrix, and let each \(x_i\in\mathbb{R}^d\). Stack the local variables as \(\mathbf{x}=(x_i)_{i\in V}\). The edgewise consensus-coupling condition is
\[
(B\otimes I_d)\mathbf{x}=0,
\]
equivalently \(x_i=x_j\) for every edge \(\{i,j\}\in E\). If \(G\) is connected, this condition is further equivalent to the existence of \(z\in\mathbb{R}^d\) such that \(x_i=z\) for every \(i\in V\). For disconnected graphs it enforces consensus only within each connected component.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Incidence-matrix coupling equates neighboring copies. It produces global consensus exactly when the coupling graph is connected, and componentwise consensus otherwise.
assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is an undirected graph with an arbitrary edge orientation.
Global consensus requires \(G\) to be connected.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((B\otimes I_d)\mathbf{x}=0\) characterizes edgewise consensus and, for connected \(G\), global consensus.

notation.meaning: Stacked vector of local variable copies.
Identity operator on each local variable space.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The incidence-matrix condition and connected-component qualification are correct, and condition is the appropriate content kind, but no inspectable source is supplied.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite Positive Minimum Away from the Origin
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existence, finiteness, and strict positivity for a degree-one positively homogeneous convex objective over a nonempty closed convex set excluding the origin.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathbb E\) be a finite-dimensional real vector space. Suppose \(f:\mathbb E\to\mathbb R\) is convex, \(\operatorname{dom}f=\mathbb E\), and \(f(\lambda x)=\lambda f(x)\) for every \(x\in\mathbb E\) and \(\lambda\ge0\). Let \(Q_1\subset\mathbb E\) be nonempty, closed, and convex with \(0\notin Q_1\), and assume \(0\in\operatorname{int}\partial f(0)\). Then \[f^*:=\min_{x\in Q_1}f(x)\] is well-defined and finite, and \(f^*>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An everywhere-finite, degree-one positively homogeneous convex function whose subdifferential at zero contains zero in its interior attains a finite, strictly positive minimum on every nonempty closed convex set that excludes the origin.
assumptions_latex: \mathbb E\text{ is a finite-dimensional real vector space}
\varnothing\ne Q_1\subset\mathbb E\text{ is closed and convex}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f^*:=\min_{x\in Q_1}f(x)\text{ is finite and attained, and }f^*>0

children.title: Symmetric Norm Regularizers
children.top_down_role: Regularizers generated by centrally symmetric convex unit balls.

knowledge_statements.title: Symmetric Norm Regularizers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Norm regularizer defined by a centrally symmetric convex unit ball.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) be a finite-dimensional real vector space and let \(B\subseteq X\) be compact, convex, centrally symmetric, and have \(0\) in its interior. Its Minkowski functional
\[
\|x\|_B=\inf\{t>0:x\in tB\}
\]
is a norm with unit ball \(B\). Conversely, the closed unit ball of every norm has these properties and recovers the norm by this formula. For \(\lambda>0\), the function \(R(x)=\lambda\|x\|_B\) is therefore a proper, finite, convex, positively homogeneous, and symmetric regularizer, satisfying \(R(-x)=R(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every centrally symmetric compact convex body containing zero in its interior generates a norm by its gauge, and scaling that norm gives a symmetric convex regularizer.
assumptions_latex: \(B\) is compact, convex, centrally symmetric, and contains \(0\) in its interior.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|\cdot\|_B\) is a norm with unit ball \(B\), and \(R=\lambda\|\cdot\|_B\) is a symmetric convex regularizer.

notation.meaning: Minkowski functional generated by the unit ball.

source_refs.locator: 2 Convex Analysis on Symmetric Matrices p. 13

source_witnesses.locator: 2 Convex Analysis on Symmetric Matrices p. 13

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact pointwise certificate for norm regularizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a norm \(\|\cdot\|\), \(z\in\partial\|x\|\) if and only if \(\|z\|_*\le1\) and \(\langle z,x\rangle=\|x\|\). If \(x\ne0\), then necessarily \(\|z\|_*=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A norm subgradient is a dual-feasible vector whose pairing with the point attains the norm.
knowledge_statements.title: Subgradient Certificate for a Norm

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Conjugate of a Scaled Norm Regularizer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fenchel conjugacy for a scaled norm penalty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\|\cdot\|\) be a norm with dual norm \(\|\cdot\|_*\), and let \(R(x)=\lambda\|x\|\) with \(\lambda>0\). Then \(R^*(z)=\delta_{\{z:\|z\|_*\le\lambda\}}(z)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The conjugate of a scaled norm is the indicator of the correspondingly scaled dual unit ball.
knowledge_statements.title: Conjugate of a Scaled Norm Regularizer

children.title: Gauge Regularizers
children.top_down_role: Possibly asymmetric positively homogeneous regularizers.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit failure of norm symmetry for a definite gauge.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(C=[-1,2]\subset\mathbb R\), \(\gamma_C(x)=x/2\) for \(x\ge0\) and \(\gamma_C(x)=-x\) for \(x<0\). Thus \(\gamma_C(1)=1/2\ne1=\gamma_C(-1)\), although \(C\) is compact, convex, absorbing, and contains \(0\) in its interior.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The interval [-1,2] generates a finite definite gauge that is asymmetric.
knowledge_statements.title: An Asymmetric One-Dimensional Gauge

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Polar Representation and Conjugate of a Gauge
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional polar duality for a closed convex gauge set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subset\mathbb R^n\) be closed, convex, absorbing, and contain \(0\), and define \(C^\circ=\{z:\langle z,c\rangle\le1\ \forall c\in C\}\). Then \(\gamma_C=\sigma_{C^\circ}\), \((\gamma_C)^*=\delta_{C^\circ}\), and \(z\in\partial\gamma_C(x)\) exactly when \(z\in C^\circ\) and \(\langle z,x\rangle=\gamma_C(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A closed gauge is the support function of its polar; its conjugate is the polar indicator, and tight polar vectors are exactly its subgradients.
assumptions_latex: C\subset\mathbb R^n\text{ is closed, convex, absorbing, and }0\in C

notation.meaning: support function of the polar set

knowledge_statements.title: Polar Representation and Conjugate of a Gauge

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates absorbing and line-free gauge geometries.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a closed convex set \(C\ni0\), \(\gamma_C\) is finite everywhere exactly when \(C\) is absorbing. Moreover, \(\{x:\gamma_C(x)=0\}=\operatorname{rec}C\). Hence the gauge is definite exactly when \(C\) has no nonzero recession direction; boundedness of \(C\) is sufficient but not necessary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Absorption controls finiteness, while recession directions are exactly the directions on which a gauge vanishes.
assumptions_latex: C\subset\mathbb R^n\text{ is closed and convex with }0\in C
knowledge_statements.title: Finiteness and Definiteness Boundaries

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent functional characterization of finite gauge regularizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A function \(g:\mathbb R^n\to[0,\infty)\) is the gauge of a closed convex absorbing set containing \(0\) if and only if it is finite, lower semicontinuous, subadditive, and positively homogeneous. In that case \(g=\gamma_C\) for \(C=\{x:g(x)\le1\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite closed nonnegative sublinear functions are exactly the gauges of their unit sublevel sets.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: g=\gamma_{\{g\le1\}}\iff g\text{ is lower semicontinuous and sublinear}
knowledge_statements.title: Sublinear Characterization of Finite Gauges
Gauge Regularizers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minkowski gauges used as convex, possibly asymmetric regularizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty, closed, convex, contain \(0\), and be absorbing. Its gauge is \[\gamma_C(x):=\inf\{t\ge 0:x\in tC\}.\] Then \(\gamma_C\) is convex, nonnegative, and positively homogeneous: \(\gamma_C(\alpha x)=\alpha\gamma_C(x)\) for every \(\alpha\ge0\). Moreover, \(C=\{x:\gamma_C(x)\le1\}\). Symmetry is not required, so generally \(\gamma_C(x)\ne\gamma_C(-x)\). If \(C\) is bounded and \(0\in\operatorname{int}C\), then \(\gamma_C(x)=0\) only for \(x=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A gauge is the scaling needed to place a point in a convex unit set. It is convex and positively homogeneous but may be asymmetric.
assumptions_latex: C\subset\mathbb{R}^n\text{ is closed, convex, absorbing, and }0\in C
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \gamma_C(x)=\inf\{t\ge0:x\in tC\}\text{ is a possibly asymmetric convex regularizer}

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition and stated gauge properties are mathematically precise and fit the leaf, but no inspectable authoritative source is supplied.

children.title: Finite-Dictionary Atomic Geometry
children.top_down_role: Atomic regularizer geometry generated by a finite collection of atoms.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Dictionary Atomic Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coefficient representation of the gauge generated by finitely many atoms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A=\{a_1,\ldots,a_m\}\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) and let \(C=\operatorname{conv}(A\cup\{0\})\). For every \(x\in\operatorname{cone}(A)\), the atomic gauge has the representation \[\gamma_C(x)=\min\left\{\sum_{i=1}^m c_i:c_i\ge0,\ \sum_{i=1}^m c_i a_i=x\right\}.\] It equals \(+\infty\) outside \(\operatorname{cone}(A)\). If \(A=-A\) and \(\operatorname{span}(A)=\mathbb{R}^n\), the resulting atomic norm is \[\|x\|_A=\min\{\|c\|_1:Ac=x\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite atomic gauge is the minimum total nonnegative atom weight representing a point; a centrally symmetric spanning dictionary yields an ℓ1 coefficient representation.

notation.meaning: finite atomic dictionary or its column matrix

source_refs.locator: 2.3.2. Structure of Polyhedral Sets p. 104

source_witnesses.locator: 2.3.2. Structure of Polyhedral Sets p. 104

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact invariance criterion for deleting a generator from a finite atomic dictionary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C=\operatorname{conv}(\{0,a_1,\ldots,a_m\})\). Removing \(a_j\) leaves \(C\), and hence its gauge, unchanged if and only if \[a_j\in\operatorname{conv}(\{0\}\cup\{a_i:i\ne j\}).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An atom is redundant exactly when it lies in the convex hull of zero and the remaining atoms.
knowledge_statements.title: Redundant-Atom Deletion Criterion

knowledge_statements.scope_note: LP dual and complementary-slackness certificate for a directed finite dictionary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A=[a_1\ \cdots\ a_m]\) and let \(x\in\operatorname{cone}(A)\). Then \[\min\{\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}c:Ac=x,\ c\ge0\}=\max\{\langle y,x\rangle:A^{\mathsf T}y\le\mathbf1\}.\] A primal-dual feasible pair \((c,y)\) is optimal exactly when \[c_i(1-a_i^{\mathsf T}y)=0\qquad(i=1,\ldots,m).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite atomic gauge is an LP whose dual bounds every atom by one; complementary slackness identifies active atoms.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Atomic Gauge Linear-Programming Dual

children.title: Polyhedral Atomic Unit Balls
children.top_down_role: Polyhedral unit sets arising from finitely generated atomic models.

knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral Atomic Unit Balls
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polyhedrality of unit balls generated by finite atomic dictionaries.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite set \(A=\{a_1,\ldots,a_m\}\subset\mathbb{R}^n\), the unit sublevel set of the gauge generated by \(C=\operatorname{conv}(A\cup\{0\})\) is exactly \[\{x:\gamma_C(x)\le1\}=C.\] Hence the atomic unit ball is a polytope. Conversely, every polytope \(P\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) containing \(0\) is the unit sublevel set of its gauge and admits a finite atomic description using its vertices. If \(P=-P\) and \(0\in\operatorname{int}P\), its gauge is a polyhedral norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite atomic dictionary generates a polyhedral unit ball, and every polytope containing the origin can be represented as a finite atomic gauge ball.

source_refs.locator: 2.3.2. Structure of Polyhedral Sets p. 104

source_witnesses.locator: 2.3.2. Structure of Polyhedral Sets p. 104

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Linear Epigraph Form of a Polyhedral Atomic Penalty
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact LP-ready epigraph of the facet representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\gamma_P(x)=\max_{1\le j\le q}b_j^{\mathsf T}x\), then \[\operatorname{epi}\gamma_P=\{(x,t):b_j^{\mathsf T}x\le t,\ j=1,\ldots,q\}.\] Thus the gauge term has an exact finite linear epigraph formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A facet-described polyhedral atomic gauge has an exact finite linear epigraph.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(t\ge\gamma_P(x)\) if and only if \(b_j^{\mathsf T}x\le t\) for every \(j\).
knowledge_statements.title: Linear Epigraph Form of a Polyhedral Atomic Penalty

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Facet Representation of a Polyhedral Atomic Gauge
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Max-linear gauge formula from a normalized halfspace description.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subset\mathbb R^n\) be a full-dimensional polytope with \(0\in\operatorname{int}P\), written as \[P=\{x:b_j^{\mathsf T}x\le1,\ j=1,\ldots,q\}.\] Then \[\gamma_P(x)=\max_{1\le j\le q}b_j^{\mathsf T}x.\] Consequently, every full-dimensional polyhedral atomic norm admits a finite maximum-of-linear-forms representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A normalized facet description of a polyhedral atomic ball turns its gauge into the maximum of finitely many linear forms.
knowledge_statements.title: Facet Representation of a Polyhedral Atomic Gauge

children.title: Vertex-Facet Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Structural links between atomic generators, extreme points, faces, and polar descriptions.

knowledge_statements.title: Vertex-Facet Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polar correspondence between vertices and facets of full-dimensional atomic polytopes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be a full-dimensional polytope with \(0\in\operatorname{int}P\), and define \(P^\circ=\{y:\langle y,x\rangle\le1\ \forall x\in P\}\). Polarity gives an inclusion-reversing bijection between nonempty proper faces: \[F\longmapsto F^*:=\{y\in P^\circ:\langle y,x\rangle=1\ \forall x\in F\},\qquad \dim F+\dim F^*=n-1.\] Consequently, each vertex of \(P\) corresponds to a facet of \(P^\circ\), and each facet of \(P\) corresponds to a vertex of \(P^\circ\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Polarity reverses the face lattice: vertices of an atomic polytope correspond to facets of its polar, and facets correspond to polar vertices.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F\leftrightarrow F^*\text{ reverses inclusion and }\dim F+\dim F^*=n-1

children.title: Continuous Atomic Geometries
children.top_down_role: Atomic models indexed by continuous parameter spaces.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between compact continuous atomic balls and exact finite LP descriptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Theta\) be compact, let \(a:\Theta\to\mathbb R^n\) be continuous, and set \(C=\operatorname{conv}(a(\Theta)\cup\{0\})\). If \(C\) has an exact finite linear extended formulation, then \(C\) is a polytope. Consequently, a nonpolyhedral continuous atomic ball has no exact finite LP representation, even though each point of positive finite gauge has a finite-support optimal decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pointwise finite optimal decompositions do not imply a finite global LP description; genuinely nonpolyhedral continuous atomic balls have none.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) has an exact finite linear extended formulation.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Linear-Programming Representation Boundary

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite-Support Attainment of Continuous Atomic Gauges
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Carathéodory sparsification of continuous atomic representations in finite dimensions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Theta\) be compact, let \(a:\Theta\to\mathbb R^n\) be continuous, and set \(C=\operatorname{conv}(a(\Theta)\cup\{0\})\). For every \(x\) with \(0<\gamma_C(x)<\infty\), the minimum-mass measure representation is attained. Moreover, there are \(r\le n\), parameters \(\theta_1,\ldots,\theta_r\in\Theta\), and coefficients \(c_j>0\) such that \[x=\sum_{j=1}^r c_j a(\theta_j),\qquad \sum_{j=1}^r c_j=\gamma_C(x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Although the dictionary is continuous, every finite-dimensional point of positive finite gauge has an optimal decomposition supported on at most n atoms.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\) has a gauge-minimizing representation using at most \(n\) atoms.

notation.meaning: support size of the finite optimal atomic measure

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Support Attainment of Continuous Atomic Gauges
Continuous Atomic Geometries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Atomic gauges generated by compact continuously parameterized atom sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Theta\) be a compact topological space and let \(a:\Theta\to\mathbb{R}^n\) be continuous. With \(\mathcal A=a(\Theta)\) and \(C=\operatorname{conv}(\mathcal A\cup\{0\})\), the continuous atomic gauge is \[\gamma_C(x)=\inf\left\{\mu(\Theta):\mu\in\mathcal M_+(\Theta),\ x=\int_\Theta a(\theta)\,d\mu(\theta)\right\},\] with value \(+\infty\) when no representing finite positive measure exists. If \(\mathcal A=-\mathcal A\) and spans \(\mathbb{R}^n\), the gauge is a norm; its unit ball need not be polyhedral.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A continuous atomic gauge minimizes the mass of a positive measure representing the point as a superposition of continuously indexed atoms.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The measure representation is precise and fits continuous atomic geometry, but its nontrivial equivalence with the gauge and the norm assertion have no cited source.

children.title: Atomic Polar Geometry
children.top_down_role: Polar and facial structures supporting dual certification.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identification of atoms allowed in a gauge-minimizing finite decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C=\operatorname{conv}(\mathcal A\cup\{0\})\), let \(x\ne0\), and suppose \(z\in C^\circ\) satisfies \(\langle z,x\rangle=\gamma_C(x)\). If \[x=\sum_i c_i a_i,\qquad c_i\ge0,\quad a_i\in\mathcal A,\quad \sum_i c_i=\gamma_C(x),\] then every atom with \(c_i>0\) satisfies \(\langle z,a_i\rangle=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A tight polar certificate forces every active atom in an optimal finite decomposition onto the exposed atomic face.
assumptions_latex: The displayed atomic decomposition attains the gauge.
knowledge_statements.title: Exposed-Atom Support Certificate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Atomic Gauge Conjugate and Polar-Ball Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fenchel representation of a closed atomic gauge through its polar unit set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subset\mathbb R^n\) be closed and convex with \(0\in C\), and assume its gauge \(\gamma_C\) is closed. Then \[\gamma_C^*(z)=\delta_{C^\circ}(z),\qquad C^\circ=\{z:\langle z,a\rangle\le1\ \forall a\in C\}.\] Hence polar feasibility together with \(\langle z,x\rangle=\gamma_C(x)\) certifies the gauge value at \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The conjugate of a closed atomic gauge is the indicator of its polar ball, so polar feasibility plus equality certifies the gauge value.

notation.meaning: indicator function of the polar set

knowledge_statements.title: Atomic Gauge Conjugate and Polar-Ball Certificate
Atomic Polar Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polar gauge and exposed-face geometry used in atomic dual certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be closed, convex, contain \(0\), and be absorbing, and let \(C^\circ=\{z:\langle z,x\rangle\le1\ \forall x\in C\}\). The polar gauge is the support function \[\gamma_C^\circ(z):=\sup_{x\in C}\langle z,x\rangle=\sigma_C(z).\] For every \(x,z\), \(\langle z,x\rangle\le\gamma_C(x)\gamma_C^\circ(z)\). When \(\gamma_C(x)>0\), equality with \(\gamma_C^\circ(z)=1\) holds exactly when \(z\in\partial\gamma_C(x)\); then \(x/\gamma_C(x)\) lies in the exposed face \(\{u\in C:\langle z,u\rangle=1\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The polar atomic gauge is the unit ball’s support function. Equality in the gauge inequality exposes a face and supplies a subgradient certificate.
assumptions_latex: C\subset\mathbb{R}^n\text{ is closed, convex, absorbing, and }0\in C

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The polar-gauge inequality, equality characterization, and exposed-face statement are mathematically coherent and fit the duality container, but no inspectable source is supplied.

children.title: Structured Sparsity Regularizer Family
children.top_down_role: Convex regularizers promoting sparse coordinates or prescribed collections of variables.

children.title: Elementwise Sparsity Regularizers
children.top_down_role: Coordinate-level sparsity through unweighted or weighted polyhedral geometry.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact proximal evaluation for weighted elementwise sparsity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\lambda\ge0\), \[\bigl(\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda R_w}(y)\bigr)_i=\operatorname{sign}(y_i)(|y_i|-\lambda w_i)_+.\] Thus coordinate \(i\) vanishes exactly when \(|y_i|\le\lambda w_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The proximal operator is coordinatewise soft thresholding with coordinate-dependent thresholds.
knowledge_statements.title: Weighted Soft-Thresholding Proximal Map

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Weighted Coordinate Subdifferential and Optimality Test
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinatewise first-order characterization for weighted l1 regularization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(R_w(x)=\sum_iw_i|x_i|\), \[z_i\in(\partial R_w(x))_i\iff z_i=\begin{cases}w_i\operatorname{sign}(x_i),&x_i\ne0,\\q_i,\ |q_i|\le w_i,&x_i=0.\end{cases}\] Hence, for differentiable convex \(f\) and \(\lambda>0\), \(x^\star\) minimizes \(f+\lambda R_w\) exactly when \(-\nabla f(x^\star)\in\lambda\partial R_w(x^\star)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weighted l1 optimality is checked coordinatewise; a zero coordinate requires a gradient magnitude no larger than its weighted threshold.
knowledge_statements.title: Weighted Coordinate Subdifferential and Optimality Test

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Support-function and Fenchel representation of weighted l1 geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(B_w:=\{z\in\mathbb R^n:|z_i|\le w_i\ \forall i\}\), \[R_w(x)=\sigma_{B_w}(x),\qquad R_w^*(z)=\delta_{B_w}(z).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weighted l1 is the support function of a coordinate box, and its conjugate is the box indicator.
knowledge_statements.title: Weighted Box Conjugacy

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp boundary between a weighted l1 norm and a seminorm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(w_i\ge0\), then \(R_w\) is a norm if and only if every \(w_i>0\). If \(w_j=0\), then \(R_w(te_j)=0\) for all \(t\), so positive definiteness, coercivity, and penalization in direction \(e_j\) fail.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A zero weight makes the regularizer blind to that coordinate and destroys normhood.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: R_w\text{ is a norm}\iff w_i>0\ \forall i
knowledge_statements.title: Zero-Weight Degeneracy
Elementwise Sparsity Regularizers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted coordinatewise sparsity regularization on finite-dimensional vectors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\) and weights \(w_i>0\), the weighted elementwise sparsity regularizer is \[R_w(x):=\sum_{i=1}^n w_i|x_i|.\] It is a norm whose unit ball is a centrally symmetric polytope with vertices \(\{\pm e_i/w_i:i=1,\ldots,n\}\). Its dual norm is \[R_w^\circ(z)=\max_{1\le i\le n}\frac{|z_i|}{w_i}.\] Setting every \(w_i=1\) gives the usual \(\ell_1\) regularizer and dual \(\ell_\infty\) norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weighted ℓ1 regularization penalizes coordinates separately, has a cross-polytope unit ball, and is dual to a weighted ℓ∞ norm.

notation.meaning: dual norm of the weighted ℓ1 norm

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The weighted ℓ1 definition, unit-ball vertices, and dual norm are correct and locally appropriate, but the record has no authoritative citation.

children.title: Disjoint Group Regularizers
children.top_down_role: Group-selection geometry over a partition of the variables.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact proximal evaluation for disjoint Euclidean groups.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\lambda\ge0\), \[\bigl(\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda R}(y)\bigr)_g=\begin{cases}\left(1-\dfrac{\lambda w_g}{\|y_g\|_2}\right)_+y_g,&y_g\ne0,\\0,&y_g=0.\end{cases}\] Hence block \(g\) vanishes exactly when \(\|y_g\|_2\le\lambda w_g\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The proximal operator independently applies Euclidean soft thresholding to each disjoint block.
knowledge_statements.title: Block Soft-Thresholding Proximal Map

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Blockwise first-order characterization for the weighted disjoint-group norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(R(x)=\sum_gw_g\|x_g\|_2\), \[z\in\partial R(x)\iff z_g= egin{cases}w_gx_g/\|x_g\|_2,&x_g
e0,\q_g,\ \|q_g\|_2\le w_g,&x_g=0.\end{cases}\] If \(f\) is differentiable and convex and \(\lambda>0\), then \(x^\star\) minimizes \(f+\lambda R\) exactly when \(-
abla f(x^\star)\in\lambda\partial R(x^\star)\); in particular, a zero block satisfies \(\|
abla_gf(x^\star)\|_2\le\lambda w_g\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The subgradient separates by blocks, and a block-gradient norm inequality certifies a zero block at an optimum.
knowledge_statements.title: Block Subdifferential and Optimality Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fenchel representation of the disjoint group norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(B_*:=\{z:\|z_g\|_2\le w_g\ \forall g\}\), \[R(x)=\sigma_{B_*}(x),\qquad R^*(z)=\delta_{B_*}(z).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The group norm is the support function of its product dual ball, and its conjugate is that ball's indicator.

notation.meaning: product of weighted Euclidean dual balls

knowledge_statements.title: Conjugate and Dual-Ball Representation
Disjoint Group Regularizers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mixed-norm regularization over a partition of the coordinate indices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal G\) be a partition of \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\), let \(w_g>0\), and let \(x_g\) denote the subvector indexed by \(g\). The disjoint group regularizer is \[R_{\mathcal G}(x):=\sum_{g\in\mathcal G}w_g\|x_g\|_2.\] It is a norm on \(\mathbb{R}^n\), and its dual norm is \[R_{\mathcal G}^\circ(z)=\max_{g\in\mathcal G}\frac{\|z_g\|_2}{w_g}.\] Thus the primal penalty is block-separable and promotes solutions in which entire subvectors \(x_g\) vanish.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The disjoint group norm sums weighted Euclidean norms over a partition; its dual is the maximum weighted block norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: R_{\mathcal G}(x)=\sum_{g\in\mathcal G}w_g\|x_g\|_2,\quad R_{\mathcal G}^\circ(z)=\max_{g\in\mathcal G}\|z_g\|_2/w_g

notation.meaning: subvector of x indexed by group g

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The disjoint-group norm and its dual are correctly stated for a partition with positive weights, but no source supports the formula or modeling interpretation.

children.title: Overlap-Latent Group Representation Pair
children.top_down_role: Group geometries involving shared variables or latent decompositions.

children.title: Overlapping Group Geometry
children.top_down_role: Group regularizers in which variables participate directly in multiple prescribed groups.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact projection characterization of direct-overlap proximal evaluation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the set \(C\) in Minkowski-Sum Dual Ball and \(\lambda>0\), \[\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda R_{\mathrm{ov}}}(y)=y-\Pi_{\lambda C}(y).\] Projection onto \(C\) generally couples group components, so independently thresholding the original overlapping subvectors is not valid in general.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The direct-overlap proximal map is the residual from projection onto the scaled Minkowski-sum dual ball.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal G\text{ is a finite coordinate cover}

notation.meaning: Euclidean projection onto the scaled dual ball

knowledge_statements.title: Proximal Map as Dual-Ball Projection

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual and conjugate geometry of the direct overlapping-group norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E_g\) embed group coordinates and define \[C:=\sum_{g\in\mathcal G}E_g\{q:\|q\|_2\le w_g\}.\] Then \[R_{\mathrm{ov}}=\sigma_C,\qquad R_{\mathrm{ov}}^*=\delta_C,\qquad R_{\mathrm{ov}}^\circ(z)=\inf_{z=\sum_gE_gq_g}\max_g\frac{\|q_g\|_2}{w_g}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The dual unit ball is a Minkowski sum of embedded group balls, and the dual norm optimizes a decomposition across overlapping groups.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal G\text{ is a finite coordinate cover}

notation.meaning: Minkowski sum of weighted embedded group balls

knowledge_statements.title: Minkowski-Sum Dual Ball
Overlapping Group Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct mixed-norm penalty for a covering family of possibly intersecting groups.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal G\) be a finite family of nonempty subsets whose union is \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\), and let \(w_g>0\). The direct overlapping-group regularizer is \[R_{\mathrm{ov}}(x):=\sum_{g\in\mathcal G}w_g\|x_g\|_2.\] It is a norm, although coordinates belonging to several groups enter several summands. For \(x_g\ne0\), the contribution of group \(g\) to a subgradient on its coordinates is \(w_gx_g/\|x_g\|_2\); at \(x_g=0\), it may be any vector of Euclidean norm at most \(w_g\), embedded on \(g\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The direct overlapping-group norm sums block norms even when groups intersect, so multiply covered coordinates participate in several coupled penalty terms.

notation.meaning: restriction of x to group g

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The direct overlapping-group norm is correctly distinguished from the latent norm, and the groupwise subgradient contributions are stated consistently, but an authoritative source is absent.

children.title: Latent Group Decompositions
children.top_down_role: Group regularizers represented through latent components assigned to prescribed groups.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual feasibility and saturation for the latent group norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(x\), \[z\in\partial\Omega_{\mathrm{lat}}(x)\iff \|z_g\|_2\le w_g\ \forall g\in\mathcal G\quad\text{and}\quad\langle z,x\rangle=\Omega_{\mathrm{lat}}(x).\] At \(x=0\), the equality is automatic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A latent-norm subgradient is dual feasible on every group and saturates the norm pairing.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal G\text{ is a finite coordinate cover}

notation.meaning: restriction of z to group g

knowledge_statements.title: Latent-Norm Subgradient Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometric representation of the latent group norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B_g:=\{v\in\mathbb R^n:\operatorname{supp}(v)\subseteq g,\ \|v\|_2\le1\}\). Then \[\{x:\Omega_{\mathrm{lat}}(x)\le1\}=\operatorname{conv}\!\left(\bigcup_{g\in\mathcal G}w_g^{-1}B_g\right),\] so \(\Omega_{\mathrm{lat}}\) is the gauge of this convex hull.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The latent norm is the atomic gauge generated by inverse-weighted Euclidean atoms supported on individual groups.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal G\text{ is a finite coordinate cover}

notation.meaning: Euclidean unit ball supported on group g

knowledge_statements.title: Atomic Convex-Hull Unit Ball
Latent Group Decompositions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Infimal-convolution representation assigning separate latent vectors to overlapping groups.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal G\) cover \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\), with weights \(w_g>0\). For each \(g\), let \(v^g\in\mathbb{R}^n\) satisfy \(\operatorname{supp}(v^g)\subseteq g\). The latent group regularizer is \[\Omega_{\mathrm{lat}}(x):=\inf\left\{\sum_{g\in\mathcal G}w_g\|v^g\|_2:x=\sum_{g\in\mathcal G}v^g,\ \operatorname{supp}(v^g)\subseteq g\right\}.\] The infimum is attained in finite dimensions. Its dual norm is \[\Omega_{\mathrm{lat}}^\circ(z)=\max_{g\in\mathcal G}\frac{\|z_g\|_2}{w_g}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The latent group norm decomposes a vector into group-supported components and minimizes their weighted block norms; its dual is a maximum over groups.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal G\text{ is a finite cover of }\{1,\ldots,n\}

notation.meaning: latent vector supported on group g
restriction of z to group g

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The latent decomposition and dual norm are mathematically plausible and appropriately classified as a representation, but the attainment and duality claims require an inspectable source.

children.title: Variable-Duplication Equivalence
children.top_down_role: Lifted relationships between overlapping formulations and latent group representations.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Adjoint Recovery of the Latent Dual Ball
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual consequence of the aggregation lift.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(h(u)=\sum_gw_g\|u^g\|_2\), \(D(u)=\sum_gE_gu^g\), and \(\Omega(x)=\inf_{Du=x}h(u)\), \[\Omega^*(z)=h^*(D^*z)=\delta_{\{z:\|(D^*z)^g\|_2\le w_g\ \forall g\}}(z).\] Since \((D^*z)^g=z_g\), this is \(\delta_{\cap_g\{z:\|z_g\|_2\le w_g\}}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The adjoint of the aggregation map converts the separable lifted conjugate into the latent norm's groupwise dual constraints.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal G\text{ is a finite coordinate cover}

notation.meaning: separable block penalty in duplicated variables

knowledge_statements.title: Adjoint Recovery of the Latent Dual Ball

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp distinction between duplicated latent and direct-overlap formulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Aggregation \(x=\sum_gE_gu^g\) and minimization of \(\sum_gw_g\|u^g\|_2\) yield the latent penalty. Consensus constraints \(u^g=x_g\) yield the direct penalty \(\sum_gw_g\|x_g\|_2\). They are generally inequivalent: for \(\mathcal G=\{\{1\},\{1,2\}\}\), unit weights, and \(x=e_1\), the latent value is \(1\) and the direct value is \(2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Aggregation represents the latent norm, whereas consensus copies represent the direct overlap norm; the two need not agree.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal G\text{ is a finite coordinate cover}
knowledge_statements.title: Aggregation versus Consensus Duplication
Variable-Duplication Equivalence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lifted disjoint-block formulation of the latent overlapping-group norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each \(g\in\mathcal G\), let \(E_g:\mathbb{R}^{|g|}\to\mathbb{R}^n\) embed group coordinates, define \(u=(u^g)_{g\in\mathcal G}\), and set \(Du:=\sum_{g\in\mathcal G}E_gu^g\). Then \[\Omega_{\mathrm{lat}}(x)=\min_{u:Du=x}\sum_{g\in\mathcal G}w_g\|u^g\|_2.\] Thus duplicating every coordinate once for each group containing it converts the latent overlapping-group penalty into a separable disjoint-block penalty in the lifted variable, coupled only by the linear consistency equation \(Du=x\). The lifted and latent formulations have identical optimal values and corresponding minimizers under \(v^g=E_gu^g\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Duplicating shared coordinates yields disjoint latent blocks; a linear aggregation constraint makes the lifted block penalty exactly equal to the latent group norm.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal G\text{ is a finite coordinate-group cover}

notation.meaning: duplicated block associated with group g

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The duplication map gives the stated latent formulation and fits the equivalence leaf, but the equivalence and minimizer correspondence have no cited evidence.

children.title: Hierarchical Graph Sparsity Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: Nested, tree-structured, or graph-organized selection patterns.

children.title: Hierarchical Sparsity Patterns
children.top_down_role: Selection geometries governed by nested inclusion or ancestry constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Hierarchical Sparsity Patterns
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Support sets closed under ancestry in a directed acyclic hierarchy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a directed acyclic graph whose edge \((u,v)\in E\) means that \(u\) is a parent of \(v\). A support set \(S\subseteq V\) is hierarchical when it is ancestor-closed: \[v\in S\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\operatorname{Anc}(v)\subseteq S.\] Equivalently, its complement is descendant-closed: if \(u\notin S\), then every descendant of \(u\) is absent from \(S\). For coefficients \(x=(x_v)_{v\in V}\), the hierarchical sparsity condition requires \(S=\operatorname{supp}(x)\) to satisfy this predicate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A hierarchical support may contain a node only when it also contains every ancestor; equivalently, excluding a node excludes all descendants.
assumptions_latex: G=(V,E)\text{ is a directed acyclic graph}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S\text{ is hierarchical}\iff\forall v\in S,\ \operatorname{Anc}(v)\subseteq S

notation.meaning: set of ancestors of vertex v, optionally including v

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The ancestor-closed condition and its descendant-closed complement formulation are consistent, and `condition` fits the leaf. A source is required to establish the intended hierarchy convention, including whether ancestry includes the vertex itself.

children.title: Tree-Structured Sparsity
children.top_down_role: Hierarchical selection patterns indexed by rooted tree structures.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Ordered Composition of Nested Group Thresholds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact proximal evaluation for laminar tree groups with Euclidean norms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose the groups are laminar. For each \(v\), let \(S_v\) apply \(z_{G_v}\mapsto(1-\lambda w_v/\|z_{G_v}\|_2)_+z_{G_v}\) and leave other coordinates unchanged, with zero mapped to zero. If \(v_1,\ldots,v_m\) is ordered so that \(G_{v_i}\subsetneq G_{v_j}\) implies \(i<j\), then \[\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda\Omega_T}=S_{v_m}\circ\cdots\circ S_{v_1}.\] Thus the shrinkages are applied from descendants toward ancestors.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For laminar tree groups, sequential Euclidean shrinkage from leaves to root computes the exact proximal map.
knowledge_statements.title: Ordered Composition of Nested Group Thresholds
Tree-Structured Sparsity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Overlapping group penalty associated with a rooted tree of coefficient groups.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(T=(V,E)\) be a rooted tree and let \(G_v\subseteq\{1,\ldots,p\}\) be the coefficients in the subtree rooted at \(v\), so that descendants satisfy \(G_u\subseteq G_v\). For weights \(w_v>0\), the tree-structured sparsity regularizer is
\[\Omega_T(x)=\sum_{v\in V}w_v\lVert x_{G_v}\rVert_2,\qquad x\in\mathbb R^p.\]
It is a convex, positively homogeneous function. Vanishing of a subtree group sets all coordinates in that subtree to zero, thereby coupling selected supports according to the tree hierarchy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A tree penalty sums weighted norms over nested subtree groups, encouraging coefficient supports that respect the prescribed hierarchy.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) is a finite rooted tree with nested subtree groups \(G_v\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Omega_T\) is convex and promotes supports organized by the tree.

notation.meaning: coordinate group associated with the subtree rooted at node v
restriction of x to coordinates in the group G_v

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard overlapping subtree-group norm definition

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition and content kind fit the leaf, but no cited source supports the claimed hierarchy-induced support behavior.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Builder complexity claim deferred because its strengthened linear-time implementation lacks sufficient structural and computational assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Direct evaluation of every group norm and rescaling has arithmetic cost \(O(\sum_v|G_v|)\). The stronger claimed \(O(p+|V|)\) bound does not follow from laminarity alone and requires a precisely specified coefficient-tree representation, cached aggregates, and update scheme.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The direct incidence bound is sound, but the claimed representation-linear implementation needs additional algorithmic assumptions.

notation.meaning: number of coefficients in group G_v

knowledge_statements.title: Linear Incidence-Cost Tree Proximal Pass

intermediate_metadata.reason: The leaf owns the nested subtree penalty and its distinctive descendant-to-ancestor proximal computation, with direct cost linear in total group incidence. The stronger cached linear-time claim was deferred. General DAG support predicates, arbitrary graph groups, and generic overlap duality were excluded as sibling scopes.

children.title: Graph-Structured Sparsity
children.top_down_role: Selection patterns organized by general adjacency or incidence structures.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Graph Alone Does Not Determine a Penalty
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonuniqueness without a declared graph-derived group construction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the path \(1-2-3\), let \(\mathcal G_E=\{\{1,2\},\{2,3\}\}\) and \(\mathcal G_N=\{\{1,2\},\{1,2,3\},\{2,3\}\}\), with unit weights. At \(x=e_3\), \[\sum_{H\in\mathcal G_E}\|x_H\|_2=1,\qquad \sum_{H\in\mathcal G_N}\|x_H\|_2=2.\] Thus \(G\) alone, without \(\mathcal G(G)\) and weights, does not define a unique graph-structured regularizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The same graph can induce different penalties, so the graph-derived groups and weights are essential data.
knowledge_statements.title: Graph Alone Does Not Determine a Penalty
Graph-Structured Sparsity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Overlapping group sparsity induced by a prescribed graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a finite graph with \(V=\{1,\ldots,p\}\), and let \(\mathcal G(G)\) be a specified family of vertex sets derived from \(G\), such as edges, neighborhoods, or connected subgraphs. Given weights \(w_H>0\), define
\[\Omega_G(x)=\sum_{H\in\mathcal G(G)}w_H\lVert x_H\rVert_2,
\qquad x\in\mathbb R^p.\]
This overlapping-group penalty is convex and promotes joint deletion or retention of graph-related coordinates. The chosen family \(\mathcal G(G)\), rather than the graph alone, determines the admissible structural bias.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Graph-structured sparsity uses norms of graph-derived coordinate groups to favor supports compatible with edges, neighborhoods, or other specified graph structures.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is finite and \(\mathcal G(G)\) is a fixed nonempty group family.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Omega_G\) is a convex graph-structured sparsity penalty.

notation.meaning: specified family of coordinate groups derived from G
restriction of x to vertices in H

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard overlapping graph-group norm construction
graph-derived group convention must be source-certified

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The construction is mathematically plausible and appropriately a definition, but graph-structured sparsity depends materially on the chosen graph-derived group family, for which no source is supplied.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Builder claim rejected because it overinterprets a tautological vanishing identity as optimizer support geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The identity \((x_H=0\ \forall H\in\mathcal H)\iff x_{\cup_{H\in\mathcal H}H}=0\) is valid, but it does not by itself characterize the zero patterns selected by minimizing the overlapping penalty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Simultaneous group vanishing zeros a union of groups, but that tautology is not a characterization of optimizer support patterns.
knowledge_statements.title: Representable Group-Zero Patterns

children.title: Sparsity-Shrinkage Synthesis
children.top_down_role: Regularizers combining sparse selection with additional curvature or multiple sparsity scales.

children.title: Elastic-Net Regularization
children.top_down_role: Combined coordinate sparsity and quadratic shrinkage.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinatewise exact proximal operation for the canonical elastic-net normalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(R_{\mathrm{EN}}(x)=\lambda_1\|x\|_1+\tfrac{\lambda_2}{2}\|x\|_2^2\) and \(\gamma>0\), \[\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma R_{\mathrm{EN}}}(z)=\frac{1}{1+\gamma\lambda_2}S_{\gamma\lambda_1}(z),\] where \((S_\tau(z))_j=\operatorname{sign}(z_j)(|z_j|-\tau)_+\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Elastic-net proximal evaluation is soft thresholding followed by uniform quadratic shrinkage.
knowledge_statements.title: Elastic-Net Proximal Map

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact first-order certificate for a differentiable convex loss plus elastic-net regularization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A vector \(x^*\) minimizes \(f+R_{\mathrm{EN}}\) if and only if, for every coordinate \(j\), \[x_j^*
eq0\Rightarrow 
abla_jf(x^*)+\lambda_2x_j^*+\lambda_1\operatorname{sign}(x_j^*)=0,\] and \[x_j^*=0\Rightarrow |
abla_jf(x^*)|\leq\lambda_1.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Elastic-net optimality is certified by equality on nonzero coordinates and an l1 threshold inequality on zero coordinates.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^p\to\mathbb R\) is differentiable and convex.
knowledge_statements.title: Coordinatewise Subgradient Test

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separable conjugate, including the pure-l1 boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\lambda_2>0\), then \[R_{\mathrm{EN}}^*(y)=\sum_{j=1}^p\frac{(|y_j|-\lambda_1)_+^2}{2\lambda_2}.\] If \(\lambda_2=0\), then \[R_{\mathrm{EN}}^*(y)=\delta_{\{y:\|y\|_\infty\leq\lambda_1\}}(y),\] including the convention that \(\lambda_1=0\) gives the indicator of \(\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The conjugate is a squared excess above the l1 threshold, degenerating to an infinity-ball indicator without quadratic curvature.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_{\mathrm{EN}}^*(y)=\sum_j(|y_j|-\lambda_1)_+^2/(2\lambda_2)\) for \(\lambda_2>0\), with the stated indicator limit at \(\lambda_2=0\).
knowledge_statements.title: Elastic-Net Fenchel Conjugate
Elastic-Net Regularization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional elastic-net penalty combining coordinate sparsity with isotropic quadratic shrinkage.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(x\in\mathbb R^p\) and parameters \(\lambda_1,\lambda_2\geq0\), the elastic-net regularizer is
\[R_{\mathrm{EN}}(x)=\lambda_1\lVert x\rVert_1+\frac{\lambda_2}{2}\lVert x\rVert_2^2.\]
The first term promotes coordinatewise sparsity, while the second shrinks coefficients and supplies quadratic curvature. The function is proper, finite, and convex. If \(\lambda_2>0\), it is \(\lambda_2\)-strongly convex with respect to the Euclidean norm; if \(\lambda_1>0\), it is nonsmooth at points having a zero coordinate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Elastic net adds an l1 sparsity penalty to squared Euclidean shrinkage; a positive quadratic coefficient makes the regularizer strongly convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_{\mathrm{EN}}\) is convex, and it is \(\lambda_2\)-strongly convex when \(\lambda_2>0\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: canonical elastic-net formula and strong-convexity modulus

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The elastic-net formula and strong-convexity statement are correct under the stated normalization, but the record has no inspectable citation.

children.title: Sparse-Group Regularization
children.top_down_role: Combined elementwise and group sparsity.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact groupwise proximal operation for a partition of coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(R(x)=\lambda_1\|x\|_1+\lambda_G\sum_{g\in\mathcal G}w_g\|x_g\|_2\), set \(z_g=S_{\gamma\lambda_1}(x_g)\). Then \[\big(\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma R}(x)\big)_g=\left(1-\frac{\gamma\lambda_Gw_g}{\|z_g\|_2}\right)_+z_g,\] with value zero when \(z_g=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sparse-group proximal evaluation applies coordinate soft thresholding followed by group Euclidean shrinkage.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The proximal map is group shrinkage applied to coordinatewise soft-thresholded blocks.
knowledge_statements.title: Sparse-Group Proximal Map

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact group-zero stationarity test for a differentiable convex loss.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a candidate minimizer \(x^*\) of \(f+R\), the stationarity condition on a group with \(x_g^*=0\) is equivalent to \[\|S_{\lambda_1}(\nabla_gf(x^*))\|_2\leq\lambda_Gw_g.\] Together with stationarity on nonzero groups, these conditions certify global optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A zero group satisfies stationarity exactly when its soft-thresholded loss gradient lies below the group threshold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For \(x_g^*=0\), group stationarity is equivalent to \(\|S_{\lambda_1}(\nabla_gf(x^*))\|_2\leq\lambda_Gw_g\).
knowledge_statements.title: Zero-Group Optimality Test

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fenchel representation of the sparse-group penalty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B_\infty=\{u:\|u\|_\infty\leq1\}\) and \[B_{2,\mathcal G}(w)=\{v:\|v_g\|_2\leq w_g\text{ for every }g\in\mathcal G\}.\] Then \[R=\sigma_{\lambda_1B_\infty+\lambda_GB_{2,\mathcal G}(w)},\qquad R^*=\delta_{\lambda_1B_\infty+\lambda_GB_{2,\mathcal G}(w)}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The sparse-group penalty is the support function of the Minkowski sum of an infinity ball and a product of group Euclidean balls.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal G\) is a finite coordinate partition.
knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Ball Minkowski-Sum Representation
Sparse-Group Regularization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Penalty combining coordinatewise sparsity and predefined group sparsity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal G\) be a partition of \(\{1,\ldots,p\}\), let \(w_g>0\), and choose \(\lambda_1,\lambda_G\geq0\). The sparse-group regularizer is
\[R_{\mathrm{SG}}(x)=\lambda_1\lVert x\rVert_1+\lambda_G\sum_{g\in\mathcal G}w_g\lVert x_g\rVert_2,
\qquad x\in\mathbb R^p.\]
It is convex. The coordinate term permits zeros within an active group, whereas the group term encourages entire groups to vanish. If every coordinate belongs to at least one positively weighted term and at least one of the two coefficients is positive, the penalty is a norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sparse-group regularization combines l1 sparsity within groups with group-l2 penalties that can remove whole groups.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_{\mathrm{SG}}\) is convex and combines elementwise with groupwise sparsity.

notation.meaning: coefficient subvector indexed by group g

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The sparse-group penalty is correctly formulated for a partition and the definition kind fits, but no authoritative source with a locator is provided.

children.title: Ordered Adaptive Sparsity Regimes
children.top_down_role: Convex sparsity geometries with ordered or data-adapted coordinate weights.

children.title: Ordered-Weight Sparsity
children.top_down_role: Sparsity geometries governed by weights attached to ranked coefficient magnitudes.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Proximal Map by Sorting and Isotonic Regression
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact proximal algorithm for the ordered weighted absolute-value functional.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\gamma>0\), sort \(|x|\) as \(s_1\geq\cdots\geq s_p\), and project \(s-\gamma w\) onto \[K=\{u\in\mathbb R^p:u_1\geq\cdots\geq u_p\geq0\}.\] Restoring the original order and signs yields \(\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma J_w}(x)\). Projection onto \(K\) is computable by nonnegative isotonic regression.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The proximal map is computed by sorting magnitudes, monotone nonnegative isotonic regression, and restoration of signs and order.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma J_w}\) reduces to sorting and projection onto the monotone nonnegative cone.
knowledge_statements.title: Proximal Map by Sorting and Isotonic Regression

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact finite inequality certificate for membership in the dual unit ball.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under \(w_1>0\), \[J_w^{\circ}(y)\leq1\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \sum_{i=1}^k|y|_{(i)}\leq\sum_{i=1}^kw_i\quad(k=1,\ldots,p).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dual-unit-ball membership is exactly certified by all leading partial-sum inequalities after sorting absolute coordinates.
knowledge_statements.title: Leading-Partial-Sum Dual-Ball Test

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed-form polar norm for nonincreasing nonnegative rank weights.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(W_k=\sum_{i=1}^k w_i\). If \(w_1\geq\cdots\geq w_p\geq0\) and \(w_1>0\), the dual norm is \[J_w^{\circ}(y)=\max_{1\leq k\leq p}\frac{\sum_{i=1}^k|y|_{(i)}}{W_k}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The dual norm is the largest ratio of a leading sorted-magnitude sum to the corresponding cumulative weight.

notation.meaning: sum of the first k ordered weights

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Norm of Ordered-Weight Sparsity
Ordered-Weight Sparsity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sorted absolute-value penalty with rank-dependent weights.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(x\in\mathbb R^p\), let \(|x|_{(1)}\geq\cdots\geq|x|_{(p)}\) denote the absolute coordinates sorted in nonincreasing order. Given weights \(w_1\geq\cdots\geq w_p\geq0\), define the ordered-weight sparsity penalty
\[J_w(x)=\sum_{i=1}^p w_i|x|_{(i)}.\]
The penalty is convex and permutation- and sign-invariant. If \(w_1>0\), it is a norm. Unequal weights impose shrinkage according to coefficient rank rather than a coordinate's fixed identity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Ordered-weight sparsity penalizes sorted coefficient magnitudes with decreasing nonnegative weights, producing a convex rank-dependent sparsity penalty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(J_w\) is convex; when \(w_1>0\), \(J_w\) is a norm.

notation.meaning: i-th largest absolute coordinate of x
weight assigned to the i-th order statistic

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: sorted l1 or SLOPE norm definition

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The ordered weighted absolute-value formula, convexity condition, and norm condition are mathematically consistent, but they lack a cited source.

children.title: Data-Adaptive Weighting
children.top_down_role: Convex sparsity penalties whose fixed weights reflect external data or preliminary estimates.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit boundary between fixed data-derived weights and weights depending on the current optimization variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\varepsilon>0\), the variable-dependent weighted penalty \[Q(x)=\frac{|x|}{|x|+\varepsilon}\] has the form \(a(x)|x|\) with \(a(x)=(|x|+\varepsilon)^{-1}>0\), but \(Q\) is not convex on \(\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive weights do not preserve convexity when they are functions of the current optimization variable.
knowledge_statements.title: Variable-Dependent Reweighting Can Be Nonconvex

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Kernel and Coercivity of Fixed Adaptive Weights
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural effect of zero versus positive realized weights.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For fixed realized weights \(a_j\geq0\), let \(R(x)=\sum_j a_j|x_j|\). Then \[\ker R=\{x:x_j=0\text{ whenever }a_j>0\}.\] The functional is coercive on \(\mathbb R^p\), and hence a norm, if and only if every \(a_j>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Zero adaptive weights create unpenalized coordinate directions; strict positivity is exactly the condition for a coercive weighted l1 norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R\) is coercive if and only if \(a_j>0\) for every \(j\).
knowledge_statements.title: Kernel and Coercivity of Fixed Adaptive Weights
Data-Adaptive Weighting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted sparsity penalty whose weights are estimated before solving the penalized problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(D\) denote observed data, and let \(a(D)=(a_1(D),\ldots,a_p(D))\) be nonnegative weights computed without reference to the optimization variable \(x\). The data-adaptively weighted sparsity regularizer is
\[R_D(x)=\sum_{j=1}^p a_j(D)|x_j|,
\qquad x\in\mathbb R^p.\]
Conditional on the realized data, the weights are constants, so \(R_D\) is convex. If every \(a_j(D)>0\), it is a norm; zero weights leave the corresponding directions unpenalized. Convexity need not persist if the weights are recomputed as functions of the current variable inside the same objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Data-adaptive weighting estimates nonnegative coordinate penalties from data and then holds them fixed, preserving convexity of the weighted l1 problem.
assumptions_latex: The realized weights are fixed while optimizing over \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_D\) is convex, and it is a norm if all \(a_j(D)>0\).

notation.meaning: observed data used to construct the weights

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: fixed nonnegative weighted l1 penalty
specific adaptive-weighting convention and source required

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Holding realized nonnegative weights fixed does preserve convexity, but the intended data-adaptive weighting convention and the warning about variable-dependent reweighting require source support.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Majorization by Iteratively Reweighted l1 Penalties
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proposed optimization-iterate-dependent reweighting scheme.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a concave nondecreasing scalar penalty \(\rho\), iteratively choose weights \(a_j^k=\rho'(|x_j^k|)\) and solve a weighted-l1 majorization subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Iteratively reweighted l1 can majorize a nonconvex concave sparsity penalty.
assumptions_latex: The stated majorization subproblems are well defined and attain minimizers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The majorized objective is nonincreasing under exact minimization.

notation.meaning: weight computed from the preceding optimization iterate

review_flags: This leaf is scoped to weights derived externally from data or preliminary estimates and held fixed; optimization-iterate-dependent MM is a different algorithmic family.
knowledge_statements.title: Majorization by Iteratively Reweighted l1 Penalties

intermediate_metadata.reason: The local inventory covers externally data-derived weights held fixed during optimization, conditional convexity, the kernel and coercivity boundary, and an explicit failure for current-variable-dependent weights. The proposed iteratively reweighted MM scheme is deferred as a different nonconvex algorithmic family. Rank-dependent sorting remains in Ordered-Weight Sparsity.

children.title: Convexity-Preserving Weight Regimes
children.top_down_role: Weight configurations that preserve or compromise the intended convex regularizer structure.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp two-dimensional witness outside the ordered-weight convexity regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Giving the second rank greater weight than the first produces an immediate midpoint violation of convexity.
knowledge_statements.title: Increasing Rank Weights Destroy Convexity
Convexity-Preserving Weight Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact convexity condition for a sorted absolute-value penalty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(w\in\mathbb R^p\) and define \(J_w(x)=\sum_{i=1}^p w_i|x|_{(i)}\), where \(|x|_{(1)}\geq\cdots\geq|x|_{(p)}\). Then \(J_w\) is convex on \(\mathbb R^p\) if and only if
\[w_1\geq w_2\geq\cdots\geq w_p\geq0.\]
Under this regime, \(J_w\) is positively homogeneous and permutation- and sign-invariant. It is a norm exactly when \(w_1>0\). Thus weights must decrease as sorted magnitudes decrease; reversing this order generally destroys convexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sorted l1 penalty is convex exactly when its rank weights are nonnegative and nonincreasing; it is a norm when the largest weight is positive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(J_w\) is convex if and only if \(w_1\geq\cdots\geq w_p\geq0\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: exact convexity criterion for ordered weighted l1 functionals
the if-and-only-if claim requires authoritative source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits the leaf and the stated criterion is standard, but the exact if-and-only-if convexity claim requires an authoritative citation.

children.title: Curvature-Inducing Regularizer Family
children.top_down_role: Regularizers supplying shrinkage, metric structure, stability, or quantitative curvature.

children.title: Ridge Regularization
children.top_down_role: Canonical isotropic quadratic shrinkage.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed-form proximal map of the isotropic squared Euclidean penalty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(R(x)=\tfrac\lambda2\|x\|_2^2\), \(\lambda\ge0\), and \(\tau>0\), \[\operatorname{prox}_{\tau R}(v)=\frac{1}{1+\tau\lambda}v.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The ridge proximal map uniformly contracts every direction by 1/(1+τλ).
knowledge_statements.title: Ridge Proximal Shrinkage

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fenchel conjugacy for a positive ridge coefficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\lambda>0\) and \(R(x)=\tfrac\lambda2\|x\|_2^2\), then \[R^*(z)=\frac{1}{2\lambda}\|z\|_2^2,\qquad \nabla R^*(z)=\lambda^{-1}z.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fenchel conjugacy reciprocates the positive ridge coefficient.
knowledge_statements.title: Ridge Conjugate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convexity and curvature regimes determined by the ridge coefficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(R_\lambda(x)=\tfrac\lambda2\|x\|_2^2\), \(\lambda=0\) gives the zero regularizer and supplies neither shrinkage nor strong convexity. If \(\lambda<0\), then \(R_\lambda\) is concave and unbounded below as \(\|x\|_2\to\infty\), so it is not a convex regularizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Zero removes ridge curvature, while a negative coefficient destroys convexity and makes the quadratic unbounded below.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lambda=0\) yields zero curvature, whereas \(\lambda<0\) is not convex.
knowledge_statements.title: Ridge-Coefficient Boundary

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Existence and Uniqueness Induced by Ridge Curvature
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Effect of positive ridge regularization on a finite-dimensional closed convex objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^p\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper, closed, and convex, and let \(\lambda>0\). Then \[F(x)=f(x)+\frac\lambda2\|x\|_2^2\] is proper, closed, coercive, and \(\lambda\)-strongly convex. Consequently, \(F\) has a unique minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding a positive ridge term to a proper closed convex objective makes the problem coercive and uniquely solvable.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, closed, and convex on \(\mathbb R^p\).
knowledge_statements.title: Existence and Uniqueness Induced by Ridge Curvature
Ridge Regularization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical Euclidean quadratic penalty in finite dimensions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(x\in\mathbb R^p\) and \(\lambda\geq0\), the ridge regularizer is
\[R_{\mathrm{ridge}}(x)=\frac{\lambda}{2}\lVert x\rVert_2^2.\]
It is differentiable with \(\nabla R_{\mathrm{ridge}}(x)=\lambda x\) and convex. When \(\lambda>0\), it is \(\lambda\)-strongly convex in the Euclidean norm and has the unique minimizer \(x=0\). Its isotropy means that equal Euclidean lengths receive equal penalties, independently of coordinate orientation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Ridge regularization penalizes squared Euclidean length, giving isotropic shrinkage and strong convexity whenever its coefficient is positive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_{\mathrm{ridge}}\) is convex and is \(\lambda\)-strongly convex when \(\lambda>0\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The ridge formula, gradient, isotropy, and strong-convexity modulus are correct, but no source with a specific locator is supplied.

children.title: Anisotropic Quadratic Geometry
children.top_down_role: Anisotropic quadratic geometry induced by weights or linear operators.

children.title: Weighted Quadratic Geometry
children.top_down_role: Anisotropic quadratic regularization specified through coordinate or block weights.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed-form Euclidean proximal evaluation of a positive diagonal quadratic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\tau>0\) and \(R_D(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Dx\), where \(D=\operatorname{diag}(d_i)\succ0\), \[\operatorname{prox}_{\tau R_D}(v)=(I+\tau D)^{-1}v,\qquad (\operatorname{prox}_{\tau R_D}(v))_i=\frac{v_i}{1+\tau d_i}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The proximal map independently shrinks coordinate i by the factor 1/(1+τd_i).

notation.meaning: Euclidean proximal map of the scaled weighted quadratic

knowledge_statements.title: Coordinatewise Weighted-Quadratic Proximal Map

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dual Weighted Geometry and Quadratic Conjugate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual norm and Fenchel conjugate of a positive diagonal quadratic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(D\succ0\) diagonal, the dual of \(\|x\|_D=(x^{\mathsf T}Dx)^{1/2}\) is \[\|z\|_{D^{-1}}=(z^{\mathsf T}D^{-1}z)^{1/2},\qquad \langle z,x\rangle\le\|z\|_{D^{-1}}\|x\|_D.\] Moreover, \(R_D(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Dx\) has conjugate \[R_D^*(z)=\tfrac12z^{\mathsf T}D^{-1}z.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Inverting the weights gives both the dual norm and the Fenchel-conjugate quadratic.

notation.meaning: Fenchel conjugate of the weighted quadratic

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Weighted Geometry and Quadratic Conjugate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp spectral bounds for positive diagonal quadratic geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=\operatorname{diag}(d_1,\ldots,d_p)\) with \(0<d_{\min}\le d_i\le d_{\max}\). Then \[\sqrt{d_{\min}}\|x\|_2\le\|x\|_D\le\sqrt{d_{\max}}\|x\|_2.\] For \(R_D(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Dx\), \[\|\nabla R_D(x)-\nabla R_D(y)\|_2\le d_{\max}\|x-y\|_2.\] The Euclidean strong-convexity and gradient-Lipschitz moduli \(d_{\min}\) and \(d_{\max}\) are sharp.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The smallest and largest weights give the sharp Euclidean norm-equivalence, strong-convexity, and smoothness constants.
knowledge_statements.title: Weighted Norm Equivalence and Smoothness
Weighted Quadratic Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinate-weighted positive-definite quadratic regularization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(d_1,\ldots,d_p>0\), and set \(D=\operatorname{diag}(d_1,\ldots,d_p)\). The weighted quadratic regularizer is
\[R_D(x)=\frac12x^{\mathsf T}Dx=\frac12\sum_{i=1}^p d_i x_i^2,
\qquad x\in\mathbb R^p.\]
It induces the norm \(\lVert x\rVert_D=(x^{\mathsf T}Dx)^{1/2}\), has gradient \(Dx\), and is \(\min_i d_i\)-strongly convex in the Euclidean norm. Different weights impose direction-dependent shrinkage while retaining separability across coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive diagonal matrix defines a coordinate-weighted quadratic norm, with curvature equal to its smallest diagonal weight.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_D\) is positive definite and \(\min_i d_i\)-strongly convex.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: spectral characterization of diagonal quadratic curvature

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The positive diagonal quadratic geometry and Euclidean strong-convexity modulus are correct, but the record lacks an inspectable citation.

children.title: Operator-Induced Quadratic Geometry
children.top_down_role: Quadratic regularization generated by applying a linear operator before measuring magnitude.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fenchel conjugate represented through minimum-norm adjoint preimages.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(R_A(x)=\tfrac12\|Ax\|_2^2\),
\[
R_A^*(s)=
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle\tfrac12\min\{\|y\|_2^2:A^{\mathsf T}y=s\},&s\in\operatorname{range}A^{\mathsf T},\\
+\infty,&s\notin\operatorname{range}A^{\mathsf T}.
\end{cases}
\]
Equivalently, for \(s\in\operatorname{range}A^{\mathsf T}\),
\[
R_A^*(s)=\tfrac12s^{\mathsf T}(A^{\mathsf T}A)^\dagger s.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The conjugate is the least squared energy of an adjoint preimage and is finite exactly on the adjoint range.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) is linear between finite-dimensional Euclidean spaces.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{dom}R_A^*=\operatorname{range}A^{\mathsf T}\text{ with the displayed minimum-energy value.}
knowledge_statements.title: Dual Minimum-Energy Representation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Squared-output, Gram, differential, and spectral representations of a quadratic induced by a linear operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A:\mathbb R^p\to\mathbb R^m\) be linear and define
\[
R_A(x)=\tfrac12\|Ax\|_2^2=\tfrac12\langle x,A^{\mathsf T}Ax\rangle.
\]
Then \(R_A\) is convex and differentiable with
\[
\nabla R_A(x)=A^{\mathsf T}Ax,\qquad \nabla^2R_A=A^{\mathsf T}A.
\]
Its smallest global gradient-Lipschitz constant is \(\|A\|_2^2\). It is strongly convex exactly when \(A\) is injective, in which case its largest valid modulus is \(\sigma_{\min}(A)^2\); otherwise it is constant along \(\ker A\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A squared operator norm is the quadratic generated by the Gram operator; its extreme singular values give exact smoothness and strong-convexity constants.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) is linear between finite-dimensional Euclidean spaces.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{Lip}(\nabla R_A)=\|A\|_2^2,\qquad R_A\text{ is strongly convex }\iff\ker A=\{0\}.
knowledge_statements.title: Operator-Induced Quadratic Geometry and Spectrum
Operator-Induced Quadratic Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic regularization represented through a linear operator and its Gram operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A:\mathbb R^p\to\mathbb R^m\) be linear. The operator-induced quadratic regularizer has the equivalent representations
\[R_A(x)=\frac12\lVert Ax\rVert_2^2
=\frac12\langle x,A^{\mathsf T}Ax\rangle.\]
It is convex, differentiable, and satisfies \(\nabla R_A(x)=A^{\mathsf T}Ax\). It is strongly convex in the Euclidean norm exactly when \(A\) is injective; in that case its strong-convexity modulus is \(\sigma_{\min}(A)^2\). Otherwise it penalizes only components outside \(\ker A\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A linear operator induces a quadratic penalty through its squared output norm, with strong convexity exactly when the operator is injective.
assumptions_latex: Both spaces carry their Euclidean inner products.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_A(x)=\frac12\langle x,A^{\mathsf T}Ax\rangle\), and \(R_A\) is strongly convex exactly when \(\ker A=\{0\}\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Gram-operator identity and singular-value curvature criterion

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind matches the leaf, and the Gram representation and injectivity criterion are correct in finite-dimensional Euclidean spaces, but no source is cited.

children.title: Degenerate Metric Regimes
children.top_down_role: Semidefinite or rank-deficient settings where the induced quadratic form lacks full metric control.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pseudoinverse conjugate and effective dual domain of a singular positive-semidefinite quadratic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(q(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx\) with \(Q=Q^{\mathsf T}\succeq0\),
\[
q^*(s)=
\begin{cases}
\tfrac12s^{\mathsf T}Q^\dagger s,&s\in\operatorname{range}Q,\\
+\infty,&s\notin\operatorname{range}Q.
\end{cases}
\]
Hence \(\operatorname{dom}q^*=\operatorname{range}Q=(\ker Q)^\perp\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The conjugate of a singular quadratic is the pseudoinverse quadratic on the matrix range and is infinite outside that range.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{dom}q^*=\operatorname{range}Q,\quad q^*(s)=\tfrac12s^{\mathsf T}Q^\dagger s\text{ on that domain.}
knowledge_statements.title: Conjugate of a Degenerate Quadratic

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Kernel Flatness and Restricted Metric Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact loss and recovery of norm and strong-convexity geometry for singular positive-semidefinite quadratics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Q=Q^{\mathsf T}\succeq0\) be singular and let \(q(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx\). For every \(z\in\ker Q\),
\[
q(x+tz)=q(x)\quad(x\in\mathbb R^p,\ t\in\mathbb R).
\]
Thus \((x^{\mathsf T}Qx)^{1/2}\) is only a seminorm and \(q\) is not strongly convex or coercive on \(\mathbb R^p\). For a linear subspace \(S\), define
\[
\mu_S=\min\{z^{\mathsf T}Qz:z\in S,\ \|z\|_2=1\}.
\]
The restriction of \(q\) to any affine translate of \(S\) is strongly convex exactly when \(S\cap\ker Q=\{0\}\), equivalently \(\mu_S>0\). The induced form is positive definite on \(\mathbb R^p/\ker Q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A singular quadratic is flat along its kernel, but regains positive-definite and strongly convex geometry after quotienting out the kernel or restricting to directions that avoid it.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\) is symmetric positive semidefinite and singular.
\(S\) is a finite-dimensional linear subspace for the restricted statement.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: q\text{ lacks global metric control, while }q|_{x_0+S}\text{ is strongly convex }\iff S\cap\ker Q=\{0\}.

notation.meaning: Null space of the quadratic metric.

knowledge_statements.title: Kernel Flatness and Restricted Metric Recovery
Degenerate Metric Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of norm geometry and strong convexity for singular quadratic weights.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Q\in\mathbb R^{p\times p}\) be symmetric positive semidefinite and singular, and define \(R_Q(x)=\frac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx\). For every nonzero \(z\in\ker Q\),
\[R_Q(x+t z)=R_Q(x)\qquad\text{for all }x\in\mathbb R^p\text{ and }t\in\mathbb R.\]
