Consequently, \((x^{\mathsf T}Qx)^{1/2}\) is only a seminorm, and \(R_Q\) is not strongly convex on \(\mathbb R^p\). It becomes positive definite on the quotient \(\mathbb R^p/\ker Q\), or on any subspace intersecting \(\ker Q\) only at zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A singular positive-semidefinite quadratic is flat along its kernel, so it defines only a seminorm and cannot be globally strongly convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_Q\) is constant along \(\ker Q\) and is not strongly convex on \(\mathbb R^p\).

notation.meaning: null space of the quadratic weight matrix

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: null-space characterization of singular quadratic forms

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind is appropriate and the kernel-flatness conclusions are correct, but the record provides no authoritative source locator.

children.title: Uniformly Convex Regularization
children.top_down_role: Nonquadratic regularizers carrying quantitative curvature.

knowledge_statements.title: Uniformly Convex Regularization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Power-type uniform convexity relative to a specified norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) be a finite-dimensional normed space, let \(C\subseteq X\) be convex, and let \(p\geq2\) and \(\mu>0\). A proper convex regularizer \(R:C\to\mathbb R\) is uniformly convex of degree \(p\) with modulus \(\mu\) if, for every \(x,y\in C\), every \(g\in\partial R(x)\),
\[R(y)\geq R(x)+\langle g,y-x\rangle+\frac{\mu}{p}\lVert y-x\rVert^p.\]
For \(p=2\), this is strong convexity. The positive remainder supplies quantitative curvature and implies strict convexity on \(C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A uniformly convex regularizer exceeds every subgradient affine model by a positive power of the displacement; degree two recovers strong convexity.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is convex in a finite-dimensional normed space \(X\).

notation.meaning: convex subdifferential of R at x
uniform-convexity modulus under the stated normalization

source_refs.locator: 4.2.2 Uniformly Convex Functions p. 274

review_flags: normalization of the modulus should be checked against the cited section

source_witnesses.locator: 4.2.2 Uniformly Convex Functions p. 274

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual regularity generated by global power-type uniform convexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R:X\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper, closed, and globally uniformly convex of degree \(p\ge2\) with modulus \(\mu\) on a finite-dimensional normed space. Then \(R^*\) is differentiable on \(X^*\), and \[\|\nabla R^*(u)-\nabla R^*(v)\|\le\left(\frac{p}{2\mu}\right)^{1/(p-1)}\|u-v\|_*^{1/(p-1)}.\] For \(p=2\), the conjugate gradient is Lipschitz.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Global power-type uniform convexity becomes Hölder continuity of the conjugate gradient; degree two gives Lipschitz smoothness.
assumptions_latex: \(R\) is globally uniformly convex of degree \(p\ge2\) with modulus \(\mu>0\).
knowledge_statements.title: Hölder Smoothness of the Conjugate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Subdifferential consequence of power-type uniform convexity under the seed normalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(R\) is uniformly convex of degree \(p\ge2\) with modulus \(\mu>0\), then for \(g\in\partial R(x)\) and \(h\in\partial R(y)\), \[\langle g-h,x-y\rangle\ge\frac{2\mu}{p}\|x-y\|^p.\] Thus \(\partial R\) is quantitatively strictly monotone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Power-type uniform convexity makes the subdifferential uniformly monotone with a quantitative power bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Uniform Monotonicity of the Subdifferential

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Existence and Uniqueness from Global Uniform Convexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Well-posedness supplied by a globally power-uniformly convex regularizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be finite-dimensional. Let \(R:X\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper, closed, and globally uniformly convex of degree \(p\ge2\), and let \(f\) be proper, closed, and convex with \(\operatorname{dom}f\cap\operatorname{dom}R\ne\varnothing\). Then \(f+R\) is coercive and strictly convex and therefore has a unique minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A globally power-uniformly convex regularizer makes every compatible closed convex composite objective coercive and uniquely solvable.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(R\) are proper, closed, and convex.
\(R\) is globally uniformly convex of degree \(p\ge2\).
knowledge_statements.title: Existence and Uniqueness from Global Uniform Convexity

children.title: Information-Geometric Regularizer Family
children.top_down_role: Regularizers adapted to probability, positivity, and non-Euclidean geometries.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Mirror descent and non-Euclidean composite models

children.title: Negative-Entropy Regularization
children.top_down_role: Probability-simplex and positive-coordinate regularization.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Relative Smoothness and Boundary Steepness of Negative Entropy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correctly distinguishes the smooth simplex interior from the extended-valued ambient regularizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the smooth representative \(h(p)=\sum_i p_i\log p_i\) on the positive orthant, \(\nabla h(p)_i=1+\log p_i\) and \(\nabla^2h(p)=\operatorname{diag}(1/p_i)\). Restricted to \(\operatorname{ri}\Delta_n\), these formulas describe the relative differential and tangent-space Hessian; the gradient representative is defined only up to addition of a multiple of \(\mathbf1\). As \(p_i\downarrow0\), its \(i\)-th component tends to \(-\infty\). Thus the closed simplex extension remains finite at the boundary but loses relative differentiability there, and it is not ambient-differentiable because its domain lies in an affine hyperplane.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Negative entropy is relatively smooth and strictly curved on the positive simplex, but is steep at zero coordinates; the extended simplex regularizer has no ordinary ambient gradient.

notation.meaning: all-ones vector, normal to the simplex affine hull

knowledge_statements.title: Relative Smoothness and Boundary Steepness of Negative Entropy

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Range and Extremizers of Negative Entropy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extremal values on the probability simplex.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(\Delta_n\), \[-\log n\le\sum_{i=1}^n p_i\log p_i\le0.\] The unique minimum \(-\log n\) occurs at \(p_i=1/n\) for every \(i\), while the maximum \(0\) occurs exactly at the vertices of \(\Delta_n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Negative entropy is uniquely minimized by the uniform distribution and maximized by deterministic distributions.
knowledge_statements.title: Range and Extremizers of Negative Entropy

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(H_-(p)=\sum_{i=1}^n p_i\log p_i\) is a proper convex regularizer on \(\Delta_n\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional negative entropy on the closed probability simplex.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(p\in\mathbb{R}^n\), define the extended-valued negative-entropy regularizer by
\[
H_-(p)=
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^n p_i\log p_i, & p\in\Delta_n,\\
+\infty, & p\notin\Delta_n.
\end{cases}
\]
Here \(0\log 0=0\). The function \(H_-\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex; it is strictly convex on \(\Delta_n\) and differentiable on the relative interior \(\{p\in\Delta_n:p_i>0\text{ for every }i\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Negative entropy sums p log p on the probability simplex and is infinite outside it; it is convex, strictly convex on the simplex, and smooth where every coordinate is positive.
knowledge_statements.title: Negative-Entropy Regularization

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-dimensional definition and stated convexity properties are standard and fit the leaf, but no source or inspectable locator is supplied.

children.title: Relative-Entropy Regularization
children.top_down_role: Reference-distribution regularization through entropy divergence.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit failure of metric symmetry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(p=(1/2,1/2)\) and \(q=(3/4,1/4)\), \(D_{\mathrm{KL}}(p\|q)=\tfrac12\log(4/3)\), whereas \(D_{\mathrm{KL}}(q\|p)=\tfrac34\log(3/2)+\tfrac14\log(1/2)\); these values are unequal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reversing the candidate and reference distributions generally changes KL divergence.
knowledge_statements.title: Relative Entropy Is Not Symmetric

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extends the full-support seed to arbitrary reference distributions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(p,q\in\Delta_n\), define \(D_{\mathrm{KL}}(p\|q)=\sum_{i:p_i>0}p_i\log(p_i/q_i)\), with value \(+\infty\) if some \(p_i>0=q_i\). For fixed \(q\), its effective domain is \(\{p\in\Delta_n:\operatorname{supp}p\subseteq\operatorname{supp}q\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relative entropy is finite exactly when the candidate assigns mass only where the reference does.

notation.meaning: indices assigned positive mass by p

knowledge_statements.title: Support-Sensitive Relative Entropy

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fenchel conjugate of KL regularization with fixed reference distribution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For fixed \(q\in\Delta_n\), let \(R_q(p)=D_{\mathrm{KL}}(p\|q)\) on \(\Delta_n\) and \(+\infty\) otherwise. Then \[R_q^*(u)=\log\!\left(\sum_{i=1}^nq_i e^{u_i}\right).\] Its gradient, on the coordinates with \(q_i>0\), is the exponentially tilted distribution \(p_i=q_i e^{u_i}/\sum_jq_j e^{u_j}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The conjugate of KL from q is weighted log-sum-exp, and its gradient exponentially tilts q.

notation.meaning: extended-valued KL regularizer relative to q

knowledge_statements.title: Conjugate of Relative Entropy

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantitative definiteness for finite-dimensional relative entropy using natural logarithms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(p,q\in\Delta_n\), \[D_{\mathrm{KL}}(p\|q)\ge\frac12\|p-q\|_1^2=2\operatorname{TV}(p,q)^2,\qquad \operatorname{TV}(p,q)=\frac12\|p-q\|_1.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: KL divergence controls squared total-variation distance.
knowledge_statements.title: Pinsker Inequality

assumptions_latex: The conventions \(0\log(0/q_i)=0\) and \(+\infty\) outside \(\Delta_n\) are used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D_{\mathrm{KL}}(p\|q)=\sum_i p_i\log(p_i/q_i)\) is a nonnegative convex regularizer vanishing exactly at \(p=q\).

notation.meaning: reference probability vector with positive coordinates

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional relative entropy with a fixed full-support reference distribution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a fixed \(q\in\Delta_n\) with \(q_i>0\), define
\[
D_{\mathrm{KL}}(p\|q)=
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^n p_i\log\!\left(\frac{p_i}{q_i}\right), & p\in\Delta_n,\\
+\infty, & p\notin\Delta_n.
\end{cases}
\]
This regularizer is proper, lower semicontinuous, and strictly convex on \(\Delta_n\). Moreover, \(D_{\mathrm{KL}}(p\|q)\ge 0\) for every \(p\in\Delta_n\), with equality if and only if \(p=q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relative entropy penalizes departure from a fixed positive reference distribution. It is strictly convex and nonnegative on the simplex, and it vanishes only at the reference distribution.
knowledge_statements.title: Relative-Entropy Regularization

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The full-support finite-dimensional KL regularizer is mathematically precise and fits the leaf, but the record has no cited source or locator.

children.title: General Bregman Regularization
children.top_down_role: Reference-geometric regularization beyond Euclidean distance.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relates generator curvature to squared norm displacement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\phi\) is \(\mu\)-strongly convex with respect to \(\|\cdot\|\), then \(D_\phi(x,y)\ge(\mu/2)\|x-y\|^2\). If additionally \(\nabla\phi\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz from that norm to its dual norm, then \(D_\phi(x,y)\le(L/2)\|x-y\|^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong convexity lower-bounds Bregman divergence by squared displacement, while gradient smoothness upper-bounds it.
assumptions_latex: x,y\text{ lie in a convex region on which the stated curvature assumptions hold}
knowledge_statements.title: Curvature Bounds for Bregman Divergence

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Bregman Divergences Need Not Be Metrics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit examples of asymmetry and triangle-inequality failure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\phi(t)=e^t\), \(D_\phi(1,0)=e-2\) while \(D_\phi(0,1)=1\), so symmetry fails. For \(\phi(t)=t^2/2\), \(D_\phi(x,y)=(x-y)^2/2\), and \(D_\phi(2,0)=2>D_\phi(2,1)+D_\phi(1,0)=1\), so the triangle inequality fails.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exponential geometry gives an asymmetric Bregman divergence, while squared Euclidean divergence violates the triangle inequality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: D_\phi(x,y)\text{ need not be symmetric or satisfy the triangle inequality}
knowledge_statements.title: Bregman Divergences Need Not Be Metrics

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Legendre conjugacy of primal and dual Bregman divergences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\phi\) is Legendre and \(x,y\in\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}\phi)\), then \[D_\phi(x,y)=D_{\phi^*}(\nabla\phi(y),\nabla\phi(x)).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under Legendre regularity, gradient coordinates reverse the arguments and preserve Bregman divergence.
knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Coordinate Bregman Identity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fundamental identity for differentiable Bregman generators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x,y,z\) in a convex domain where \(\phi\) is differentiable, \[D_\phi(x,y)-D_\phi(x,z)-D_\phi(z,y)=\langle\nabla\phi(z)-\nabla\phi(y),x-z\rangle.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The difference between one Bregman divergence and two successive divergences is an explicit gradient pairing.
knowledge_statements.title: Bregman Three-Point Identity

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Bregman Projection and Generalized Pythagorean Inequality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional best-approximation theorem in Bregman geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\) be convex and suppose \(z\in K\) minimizes \(D_\phi(\cdot,y)\) over \(K\), with the displayed gradients defined. Then \(\langle\nabla\phi(z)-\nabla\phi(y),x-z\rangle\ge0\) for every \(x\in K\), and hence \[D_\phi(x,y)\ge D_\phi(x,z)+D_\phi(z,y)\quad(x\in K).\] If \(\phi\) is strictly convex, such a minimizer is unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An existing Bregman projection satisfies a variational inequality and a generalized Pythagorean inequality.
assumptions_latex: \phi\text{ is differentiable at the displayed points}
knowledge_statements.title: Bregman Projection and Generalized Pythagorean Inequality
General Bregman Regularization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional Bregman regularization on an open convex domain with a differentiable strictly convex generator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\) be a nonempty open convex subset of a finite-dimensional real inner-product space, and let \(\phi:C\to\mathbb{R}\) be differentiable and strictly convex. For \(x,y\in C\), define
\[
D_\phi(x,y)=\phi(x)-\phi(y)-\langle\nabla\phi(y),x-y\rangle.
\]
For each fixed \(y\in C\), the mapping \(x\mapsto D_\phi(x,y)\) is convex and nonnegative, and \(D_\phi(x,y)=0\) if and only if \(x=y\). In general, \(D_\phi\) need not be symmetric and need not satisfy the triangle inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On an open convex finite-dimensional domain, a differentiable strictly convex generator defines a Bregman divergence as the gap from its affine approximation at a reference point. The divergence is nonnegative and convex in its first argument, vanishes only when its arguments coincide, and generally is not a metric.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is a nonempty open convex subset of a finite-dimensional real inner-product space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D_\phi(x,y)=\phi(x)-\phi(y)-\langle\nabla\phi(y),x-y\rangle\ge 0\), with equality if and only if \(x=y\), and \(x\mapsto D_\phi(x,y)\) is convex.

children.title: Transform-Difference Regularizer Family
children.top_down_role: Regularizers promoting simplicity after application of a transform or difference operator.

children.title: Analysis-Synthesis Representation Pair
children.top_down_role: Distinct transformed-coefficient and latent-coefficient sparsity models.

children.title: Analysis-Form Regularization
children.top_down_role: Regularization imposed directly on coefficients produced by an analysis transform.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Conjugate and Subdifferential of an Analysis Composite
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fenchel formulas for a qualified closed convex analysis penalty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(R(x)=\psi(Ax)\), where \(\psi\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex. If \(\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}\psi)\cap\operatorname{range}A\ne\varnothing\), then
\[R^*(u)=\min\{\psi^*(y):A^Ty=u\},\]
with value \(+\infty\) when the constraint is infeasible, and
\[\partial R(x)=A^T\partial\psi(Ax).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the relative-interior qualification, conjugation minimizes the coefficient conjugate over adjoint-compatible variables, and subgradients pull back through the adjoint.
assumptions_latex: \(\psi\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.

notation.meaning: Fenchel conjugate of the coefficient penalty

knowledge_statements.title: Conjugate and Subdifferential of an Analysis Composite

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural properties intrinsic to finite-dimensional analysis penalties.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) be linear and \(R=\psi\circ A\). Then \(\operatorname{dom}R=A^{-1}(\operatorname{dom}\psi)\). If \(\psi\) is lower semicontinuous, then so is \(R\). If \(\psi\) is a norm, then \(R\) is a seminorm with \(\ker R=\ker A\), and \(R\) is a norm exactly when \(A\) is injective.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An analysis penalty is finite where the analyzed coefficients lie in the penalty domain. A norm composed with the analysis map is a seminorm, becoming a norm exactly for an injective map.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dom}(\psi\circ A)=A^{-1}(\operatorname{dom}\psi)\); for norm \(\psi\), \(\ker(\psi\circ A)=\ker A\) and normhood is equivalent to injectivity of \(A\).
knowledge_statements.title: Domain, Kernel, and Norm Conditions

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Support and Subgradient Representation of Analysis L1
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual representation specific to the analysis l1 seminorm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For linear \(A:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\),
\[\|Ax\|_1=\max_{\|y\|_\infty\le1}\langle A^Ty,x\rangle.\]
Moreover, \(u\in\partial\|A\cdot\|_1(x)\) exactly when \(u=A^Ty\) for some \(y\) with \(\|y\|_\infty\le1\), where \(y_i=\operatorname{sign}((Ax)_i)\) whenever \((Ax)_i\ne0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Analysis l1 is the support function of the adjoint image of the infinity ball, with an explicit bounded-sign subgradient certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|Ax\|_1=\max_{\|y\|_\infty\le1}\langle A^Ty,x\rangle\), with the stated subgradient characterization.
knowledge_statements.title: Support and Subgradient Representation of Analysis L1

assumptions_latex: \(\psi:\mathbb{R}^m\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_{\mathrm{an}}(x)=\psi(Ax)\) is a convex extended-valued regularizer on \(\mathbb{R}^n\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex penalties applied directly to analyzed coefficients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The analysis-form regularizer induced by \(A\) and \(\psi\) is the composition
\[
R_{\mathrm{an}}(x)=\psi(Ax),\qquad x\in\mathbb{R}^n.
\]
It penalizes the transform coefficients \(Ax\) without introducing an independent representation variable. Because \(A\) is linear and \(\psi\) is convex, \(R_{\mathrm{an}}\) is convex. A standard sparsity-promoting instance is \(R_{\mathrm{an}}(x)=\|Ax\|_1\); finite-difference analysis operators yield total-variation-type regularizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Analysis-form regularization applies a convex penalty directly to coefficients produced by a linear transform, as in the l1 norm of analysis or finite-difference coefficients.
knowledge_statements.title: Analysis-Form Regularization

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The analysis-form definition and convexity claim are correct and fit the leaf, but no source or specific locator supports the record.

children.title: Synthesis-Form Regularization
children.top_down_role: Regularization imposed on latent coefficients used to synthesize the modeled object.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditions separating convex projection from a closed, attained synthesis regularizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(R(x)=\inf_{Dz=x}\psi(z)\), with \(\psi\) proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex. Linear projection preserves convexity but need not preserve closedness. If \(\psi\) is level-bounded on every affine fiber \(\{z:Dz=x\}\), every finite fiber infimum is attained. Under attainment,
\[\operatorname{epi}R=\{(Dz,t):(z,t)\in\operatorname{epi}\psi\}.\]
If this projected epigraph is also closed, then \(R\) is lower semicontinuous. Neither attainment nor closedness follows from closed convexity of \(\psi\) alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fiberwise level-boundedness gives coefficient attainment, while closedness of the projected epigraph gives lower semicontinuity; neither property is automatic.
assumptions_latex: \(\psi\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Fiberwise level-boundedness ensures finite infima are attained, and closedness of the projected epigraph ensures \(R\) is lower semicontinuous.
knowledge_statements.title: Closedness and Attainment Boundary

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Domain and Conjugate of a Synthesis Value Function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact domain and Fenchel conjugate of the coefficient infimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(R(x)=\inf_{Dz=x}\psi(z)\), with value \(+\infty\) on infeasible fibers,
\[\operatorname{dom}R=D(\operatorname{dom}\psi),\qquad R^*(y)=\psi^*(D^Ty).\]
The conjugate identity does not require attainment of the fiber infimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The finite domain is the dictionary image of the coefficient domain, and the conjugate is the coefficient conjugate composed with the adjoint dictionary.
knowledge_statements.title: Domain and Conjugate of a Synthesis Value Function

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometry and dual feasibility for a surjective finite dictionary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(D=[d_1\ \cdots\ d_m]\) be surjective and
\[R(x)=\min_{Dz=x}\|z\|_1.\]
Then
\[\{x:R(x)\le1\}=DB_1=\operatorname{conv}\{\pm d_1,\ldots,\pm d_m\}.\]
Thus \(R\) is the atomic norm generated by the signed dictionary columns, and
\[R^*(y)=\delta_{\{y:\|D^Ty\|_\infty\le1\}}(y).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Synthesis l1 is the atomic norm generated by the signed dictionary columns, and its conjugate is the indicator of the corresponding dual-feasible set.
knowledge_statements.title: Atomic-Norm Representation of Synthesis L1
Synthesis-Form Regularization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonnegative convex coefficient penalties minimized over exact finite-dimensional synthesis representations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(D:\mathbb{R}^m\to\mathbb{R}^n\) be linear and let \(\psi:\mathbb{R}^m\to[0,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex. Define
\[
R_{\mathrm{syn}}(x)=\inf\{\psi(z):z\in\mathbb{R}^m,\ Dz=x\},
\]
using the value \(+\infty\) when the feasible set is empty. This synthesis-form value function is a proper convex extended-valued regularizer. For \(\psi(z)=\|z\|_1\), it gives the minimum \(\ell_1\)-cost among exact representations of \(x\) through \(D\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Synthesis-form regularization assigns a signal the infimum of a nonnegative convex coefficient penalty over all exact representations through a linear dictionary. With the l1 penalty, this infimum is the minimum l1 cost of an exact representation.
assumptions_latex: \(\psi:\mathbb{R}^m\to[0,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
The infimum is \(+\infty\) when \(\{z\in\mathbb{R}^m:Dz=x\}\) is empty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_{\mathrm{syn}}(x)=\inf\{\psi(z):Dz=x\}\) is a proper convex extended-valued regularizer on \(\mathbb{R}^n\).

notation.meaning: nonnegative convex penalty on representation coefficients

children.title: Representation Equivalence Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Transform and dictionary regimes governing agreement or divergence between the two representations.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometric equivalence criterion with the closed-image qualification needed for exact synthesis unit balls.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(p\) and \(q\) be closed gauges, let \(A:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^k\), and let surjective \(D:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R^n\). Suppose \(D\{z:q(z)\le1\}\) is closed. For \(R_{\rm an}=p\circ A\) and \(R_{\rm syn}(x)=\inf_{Dz=x}q(z)\),
\[R_{\rm an}=R_{\rm syn}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \{x:p(Ax)\le1\}=D\{z:q(z)\le1\}.\]
Without the closed-image or an equivalent attainment condition, replacing the synthesis unit ball by the displayed linear image can omit boundary points; its closure instead describes the lower-semicontinuous gauge hull.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For closed gauges with a closed synthesis ball image, equivalence is exactly equality of induced unit balls. Without closedness or attainment, a closure may be required and exact equality is not automatic.
knowledge_statements.title: Closed-Gauge Equivalence Criterion

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact agreement for mutually inverse analysis and synthesis transforms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\) be invertible, set \(D=A^{-1}\), and let \(\psi:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\). The constraint \(Dz=x\) has the unique solution \(z=Ax\), and hence
\[\inf_{Dz=x}\psi(z)=\psi(Ax)\qquad\text{for every }x.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Analysis and synthesis penalties coincide for mutually inverse transforms because every signal has a unique coefficient representation.
knowledge_statements.title: Bijective Transform Equivalence

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_{\mathrm{an}}=R_{\mathrm{syn}}\) exactly when \(\{x:\|Ax\|_1\le1\}=D\{z:\|z\|_1\le1\}\); this equality is not automatic.

notation.meaning: unit ball of the l1 norm

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact equality criterion and a finite-dimensional failure example for analysis and synthesis penalties.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The two regularizers agree for every \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\) if and only if their unit balls agree:
\[
\{x:\|Ax\|_1\le1\}=D(B_1),\qquad B_1=\{z:\|z\|_1\le1\}.
\]
Thus analysis-synthesis equivalence requires geometric compatibility between \(A\) and \(D\), not merely linearity. For example, with \(n=1\), \(D(z_1,z_2)=z_1+z_2\), and \(Ax=(x,x)\), one has \(R_{\mathrm{syn}}(x)=|x|\) but \(R_{\mathrm{an}}(x)=2|x|\), so the representations are inequivalent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Analysis and synthesis l1 penalties coincide exactly when their unit balls coincide. Redundant transforms need not satisfy this condition; a two-coefficient representation of a scalar already gives unequal penalties.
knowledge_statements.title: Representation Equivalence Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The unit-ball equality criterion and scalar counterexample correctly describe an analysis–synthesis equivalence boundary, and failure_boundary is the appropriate kind, but no source or locator is supplied.

children.title: Total-Variation Regularization
children.top_down_role: Variation geometry in discrete, continuous, anisotropic, isotropic, and graph settings.

children.title: Grid-Based Total Variation
children.top_down_role: Anisotropic and isotropic variation on regular grids.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dual Flux Forms of Anisotropic and Isotropic Grid TV
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A fixed finite-difference operator including its boundary convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For anisotropic TV, \[\|Du\|_{1,1}=\max_{\|q\|_\infty\le1}\langle D^Tq,u\rangle.\] For isotropic TV, \[\|Du\|_{2,1}=\max_{\|q_{i,j}\|_2\le1\ \forall(i,j)}\langle D^Tq,u\rangle.\] Subgradients are \(D^Tq\), with nonzero gradient components or blocks aligned with their dual variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Anisotropic and isotropic grid TV are support functions of box-constrained and pixelwise Euclidean-bounded fluxes.
assumptions_latex: \(D\) is a fixed linear finite-difference operator.
\(u\) is a finite real grid array.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The two TV variants have the displayed exact flux duals and subgradient forms.
knowledge_statements.title: Dual Flux Forms of Anisotropic and Isotropic Grid TV

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-grid TV defined through discrete differences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The expressions \(\|Du\|_{1,1}\) and \(\|Du\|_{2,1}\) determine a penalty only after \(D\) is fixed. Omitted, periodic, reflected, and zero-padded boundary operators can give different values and nullspaces. In particular, zero padding can penalize a nonzero constant array, whereas omitted and periodic differences do not.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Grid TV is ambiguous without a boundary convention, and zero padding can destroy the usual constant nullspace.
assumptions_latex: The boundary-difference operator has not been specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Different boundary operators can define distinct TV penalties; zero padding need not annihilate constants.
knowledge_statements.title: Boundary Convention Dependence

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-dimensional forward differences with missing-neighbor differences set to zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On an \(M\times N\) grid set \((D_xu)_{i,j}=u_{i+1,j}-u_{i,j}\) for \(i<M\) and zero for \(i=M\), and set \((D_yu)_{i,j}=u_{i,j+1}-u_{i,j}\) for \(j<N\) and zero for \(j=N\). Then \[\operatorname{TV}_{\rm aniso}(u)=\sum_{i,j}(|D_xu_{i,j}|+|D_yu_{i,j}|)=\|Du\|_{1,1},\] \[\operatorname{TV}_{\rm iso}(u)=\sum_{i,j}\sqrt{(D_xu_{i,j})^2+(D_yu_{i,j})^2}=\|Du\|_{2,1}.\] Both vanish exactly on constant arrays when the grid is connected.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With a fixed omitted-boundary convention, anisotropic and isotropic grid TV are mixed norms of the forward-difference field.
assumptions_latex: Missing-neighbor forward differences are set to zero.
knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Boundary Mixed-Norm Grid TV

assumptions_latex: \(u=(u_{i,j})\) is a real array on a rectangular grid.
Forward differences crossing the grid boundary are omitted.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-dimensional unweighted forward-difference total variation on rectangular grids.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define \(D_xu_{i,j}=u_{i+1,j}-u_{i,j}\) and \(D_yu_{i,j}=u_{i,j+1}-u_{i,j}\) wherever the corresponding neighbors exist. The anisotropic and isotropic grid total variations are respectively
\[
\operatorname{TV}_{\mathrm{aniso}}(u)=\sum_{i,j}\bigl(|D_xu_{i,j}|+|D_yu_{i,j}|\bigr)
\]
and
\[
\operatorname{TV}_{\mathrm{iso}}(u)=\sum_{i,j}\sqrt{(D_xu_{i,j})^2+(D_yu_{i,j})^2},
\]
where unavailable boundary differences are omitted. Both are convex seminorms and vanish exactly on arrays constant over the connected grid.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Grid total variation sums neighboring differences. The anisotropic version sums their absolute coordinate components, while the isotropic version sums the Euclidean lengths of local discrete gradients.
knowledge_statements.title: Grid-Based Total Variation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The grid-TV variants fit the leaf, but the summation sets and treatment of a local isotropic gradient when only one forward neighbor exists are not fully specified. A source is needed to fix the intended boundary convention.

children.title: Graph Total Variation
children.top_down_role: Variation measured over graph edges.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted anisotropic TV for scalar signals on a finite graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(J(x)=\|WBx\|_1\). Then \[J(x)=\max_{\|p\|_\infty\le1}\langle B^TWp,x\rangle,\qquad \partial J(x)=\{B^TWp:p_e\in\operatorname{Sign}(w_e(Bx)_e)\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Graph TV is the support function of bounded edge fluxes, and its subgradients are weighted flux divergences aligned with weighted edge differences.
assumptions_latex: \(B\) is an oriented incidence matrix and \(W=\operatorname{diag}(w_e)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Graph-TV Flux Dual and Subdifferential

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Discrete Coarea Formula for Graph TV
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted scalar graph TV represented through superlevel-set cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\operatorname{cut}_w(S)=\sum_{\{u,v\}\in E}w_{uv}|\mathbf1_S(u)-\mathbf1_S(v)|\), \[\operatorname{TV}_G(x)=\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}\operatorname{cut}_w(\{v:x_v>t\})\,dt.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Graph TV equals the integral of the weighted cut sizes of all superlevel sets.
knowledge_statements.title: Discrete Coarea Formula for Graph TV

assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is a finite undirected graph with weights \(w_e\ge0\).
An arbitrary orientation assigns each edge \(e\) a head \(e^+\) and tail \(e^-\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{TV}_G(x)=\sum_{e\in E}w_e|x_{e^+}-x_{e^-}|\) is an orientation-independent convex seminorm.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted anisotropic total variation for scalar signals on finite undirected graphs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a vertex signal \(x\in\mathbb{R}^{V}\), define
\[
\operatorname{TV}_G(x)=\sum_{e\in E}w_e\,|x_{e^+}-x_{e^-}|.
\]
Equivalently, if \(B\) is the oriented incidence matrix and \(W=\operatorname{diag}(w_e)\), then \(\operatorname{TV}_G(x)=\|WBx\|_1\). The value is independent of the chosen orientation. It is a convex seminorm; its nullspace consists of signals constant on every connected component of the positive-weight subgraph.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Graph total variation sums weighted absolute differences across edges. It is independent of edge orientation and vanishes precisely on signals constant within each positive-weight connected component.
knowledge_statements.title: Graph Total Variation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The weighted graph-TV definition, orientation independence, and positive-weight-component nullspace are precise and fit the leaf, but no supporting source or locator is supplied.

children.title: Continuum Total-Variation Regimes
children.top_down_role: Variation regularization in function and measure spaces.

children.title: Function-Space Total Variation
children.top_down_role: Total-variation regularization for functions over continuous domains.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality certificate consistent with the sign convention in the divergence-supremum definition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(u\in BV(\Omega)\). Every \(\varphi\in C_c^1(\Omega;\mathbb R^d)\) with \(\|\varphi\|_\infty\le1\) satisfies
\[\int_\Omega u\,\operatorname{div}\varphi\,dx\le |Du|(\Omega).\]
If equality holds, \(\varphi\) is a maximizing calibration. With the convention \(\int u\,\operatorname{div}\varphi=-\int\varphi\cdot dDu\), equality requires
\[\varphi\cdot\frac{dDu}{d|Du|}=-1\quad |Du|\text{-almost everywhere}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bounded test field gives a lower bound on TV through the divergence pairing; equality, with the correct sign, certifies a maximizing calibration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\int u\,\operatorname{div}\varphi\le|Du|(\Omega)\), and equality is a dual calibration certificate with polar pairing \(-1\).

notation.meaning: polar density of the derivative measure

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Calibration Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Basic functional-analytic properties of scalar BV total variation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The extended functional \(u\mapsto\operatorname{TV}(u;\Omega)\) on \(L^1(\Omega)\) is convex, positively one-homogeneous, and lower semicontinuous for strong \(L^1\) convergence. If \(\Omega\) is connected, \(\operatorname{TV}(u;\Omega)=0\) exactly when \(u\) is almost everywhere constant.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Function-space TV is a lower-semicontinuous convex extended seminorm; on a connected domain its nullspace consists of constants.
assumptions_latex: For the nullspace statement, \(\Omega\) is connected.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{TV}\) is convex, one-homogeneous, and \(L^1\)-lower-semicontinuous, with constants as its kernel on connected \(\Omega\).
knowledge_statements.title: Convexity, Lower Semicontinuity, and Nullspace

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Agreement with the classical gradient and the boundary of that formula.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If \(u\in W^{1,1}(\Omega)\), then
\[\operatorname{TV}(u;\Omega)=\int_\Omega|\nabla u(x)|_2\,dx.\]
For general \(u\in BV(\Omega)\), the distributional derivative can also have jump and Cantor parts, all of which contribute to \(|Du|(\Omega)\); the integral of the density of the absolutely continuous part alone need not equal total variation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: TV is the integral of gradient magnitude for Sobolev functions, while general BV functions may also carry jump and singular continuous variation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{TV}(u;\Omega)=\int_\Omega|\nabla u|_2\,dx\) for \(u\in W^{1,1}(\Omega)\), with additional singular contributions possible in \(BV\).
knowledge_statements.title: Sobolev and BV Derivative Representations

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compactness and liminf principle for bounded BV sequences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\Omega\) be a bounded Lipschitz domain. If \((u_j)\subset BV(\Omega)\) satisfies
\[\sup_j\bigl(\|u_j\|_{L^1(\Omega)}+|Du_j|(\Omega)\bigr)<\infty,\]
then a subsequence converges strongly in \(L^1(\Omega)\) to some \(u\in BV(\Omega)\), and
\[|Du|(\Omega)\le\liminf_{j\to\infty}|Du_j|(\Omega).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform L1 and TV bounds on a bounded Lipschitz domain give subsequential L1 compactness and a variation liminf inequality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A subsequence converges in \(L^1\) to a BV function satisfying the variation liminf inequality.
knowledge_statements.title: BV Compactness

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Level-set decomposition of scalar BV variation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every \(u\in BV(\Omega)\),
\[|Du|(\Omega)=\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}P(\{u>t\};\Omega)\,dt,\]
where \(P(E;\Omega)=|D\mathbf1_E|(\Omega)\). In particular, almost every superlevel set \(\{u>t\}\) has finite perimeter.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The total variation of a scalar BV function is the integral of the perimeters of its superlevel sets.

notation.meaning: relative perimeter of a measurable set

knowledge_statements.title: Coarea Formula

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{TV}(u;\Omega)=\sup\{\int_\Omega u\,\operatorname{div}\varphi\,dx:\varphi\in C_c^1(\Omega;\mathbb{R}^d),\ \|\varphi\|_\infty\le1\}\), and it is finite exactly when \(u\in BV(\Omega)\).

notation.meaning: space of integrable functions of bounded variation
total variation of u on Omega

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distributional total variation for integrable scalar functions on an open Euclidean domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The function-space total variation of \(u\) is
\[
\operatorname{TV}(u;\Omega)=\sup\left\{\int_\Omega u(x)\,\operatorname{div}\varphi(x)\,dx:\varphi\in C_c^1(\Omega;\mathbb{R}^d),\ \|\varphi\|_\infty\le1\right\}.
\]
The function belongs to \(BV(\Omega)\) exactly when this supremum is finite. In that case its distributional derivative \(Du\) is a finite \(\mathbb{R}^d\)-valued Radon measure and \(\operatorname{TV}(u;\Omega)=|Du|(\Omega)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Function-space total variation is the dual supremum against divergences of compactly supported bounded vector fields. Its finiteness defines bounded-variation functions and equals the mass of the distributional derivative.
knowledge_statements.title: Function-Space Total Variation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The dual definition of function-space total variation and its BV characterization are standard and fit the leaf, but the record lacks a source and specific locator.

children.title: Measure-Space Total Variation
children.top_down_role: Total-variation regularization for signed, vector-valued, or Radon measures.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Subdifferential of measure total variation in the dual pairing with C0(X).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\mu\ne0\), \[f\in\partial\|\cdot\|_{\mathrm{TV}}(\mu)\iff f\in C_0(X),\ \|f\|_\infty\le1,\ \int_Xf\,d\mu=\|\mu\|_{\mathrm{TV}}.\] At \(\mu=0\), the subdifferential is the closed unit ball of \(C_0(X)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A continuous test function is a TV subgradient exactly when it is sup-norm bounded by one and norms the measure.
knowledge_statements.title: Norming-Function Subgradient Certificate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Conjugate of the Measure TV Penalty
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fenchel conjugacy for finite signed Radon measures paired with continuous functions vanishing at infinity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(J(\mu)=\lambda\|\mu\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\), \(\lambda>0\), under \(\langle f,\mu\rangle=\int_Xf\,d\mu\), \[J^*(f)=\delta_{\{g\in C_0(X):\|g\|_\infty\le\lambda\}}(f).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The conjugate of scaled measure total variation is the indicator of the corresponding sup-norm ball.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal M(X)=C_0(X)^*\) is the space of finite real signed Radon measures.
knowledge_statements.title: Conjugate of the Measure TV Penalty

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Weak-Star Lower Semicontinuity and Compact TV Balls
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weak-star geometry of finite signed Radon measures.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\mu_\alpha\to\mu\) in \(\sigma(\mathcal M(X),C_0(X))\), then \[\|\mu\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\le\liminf_\alpha\|\mu_\alpha\|_{\mathrm{TV}}.\] Every norm ball \(\{\mu:\|\mu\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\le r\}\) is weak-star compact.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Measure TV is weak-star lower semicontinuous, and its bounded balls are weak-star compact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mu_\alpha\overset{*}{\rightharpoonup}\mu\Rightarrow\|\mu\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\le\liminf_\alpha\|\mu_\alpha\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\), and TV balls are weak-star compact.
knowledge_statements.title: Weak-Star Lower Semicontinuity and Compact TV Balls

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Extreme Points of the Measure TV Unit Ball
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Real Radon measures on a compact Hausdorff space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(X\) is compact Hausdorff, then \[\operatorname{ext}\{\mu:\|\mu\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\le1\}=\{\pm\delta_x:x\in X\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The extreme points of the real measure-TV unit ball are signed point masses.
assumptions_latex: Measures are finite and real signed.
knowledge_statements.title: Extreme Points of the Measure TV Unit Ball

assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a locally compact Hausdorff space.
\(\mu\) is a finite signed Radon measure on \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|\mu\|_{\mathrm{TV}}=|\mu|(X)=\mu^+(X)+\mu^-(X)\), equivalently the dual supremum over \(C_0(X)\) functions bounded by one.

notation.meaning: positive and negative measures in the Jordan decomposition

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Total-variation norm for finite signed Radon measures.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mu=\mu^+-\mu^-\) be the Jordan decomposition into mutually singular positive measures. Its variation measure is \(|\mu|=\mu^++\mu^-\), and its total-variation norm is
\[
\|\mu\|_{\mathrm{TV}}=|\mu|(X)=\mu^+(X)+\mu^-(X).
\]
Equivalently,
\[
\|\mu\|_{\mathrm{TV}}=\sup\left\{\left|\int_X f\,d\mu\right|:f\in C_0(X),\ \|f\|_\infty\le1\right\}.
\]
This is a norm on the vector space of finite signed Radon measures.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A signed measure's total variation is the combined mass of its positive and negative Jordan parts, equivalently its largest action on a continuous test function bounded by one.
knowledge_statements.title: Measure-Space Total Variation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Jordan-decomposition and dual formulations of the total-variation norm fit the measure-space leaf, but no source or inspectable locator is supplied.

children.title: Discrete-to-Continuum Regimes
children.top_down_role: Structural relationships between discretized variation penalties and their continuum counterparts.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of axis-aligned nearest-neighbor TV to recover Euclidean-isotropic variation automatically.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For standard surface-scaled, axis-aligned nearest-neighbor differences on Cartesian grids in dimensions greater than one, the continuum density is generally anisotropic:
\[\sum_{j=1}^d|D_ju|(\Omega)=\int_\Omega\left\|\frac{dDu}{d|Du|}\right\|_1d|Du|,\]
rather than the Euclidean-isotropic variation \(|Du|(\Omega)\). Thus nearest-neighbor consistency alone does not imply an isotropic Gamma limit; stencil directions and weights must encode the intended surface tension.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Axis-aligned nearest-neighbor differences generally yield anisotropic l1 variation, not Euclidean-isotropic TV.
assumptions_latex: Only axis-aligned nearest-neighbor absolute differences are used with the corresponding surface scaling.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The limiting surface density is generally the \(\ell_1\) norm of the derivative polar rather than its Euclidean norm.
knowledge_statements.title: Cartesian Anisotropy Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fully specified one-dimensional discrete-to-continuum TV regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(h=1/N\) and identify \(x\in\mathbb R^N\) with the piecewise-constant function \(I_hx=x_i\) on \(((i-1)h,ih)\). Define
\[F_h(I_hx)=\sum_{i=1}^{N-1}|x_{i+1}-x_i|,\qquad F_h(u)=+\infty\text{ off }I_h\mathbb R^N.\]
Then, as \(h\to0\),
\[F_h\xrightarrow{\Gamma(L^1(0,1))}F,\qquad F(u)=\begin{cases}|Du|(0,1),&u\in BV(0,1),\\+\infty,&u\notin BV(0,1).\end{cases}\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Piecewise-constant interpolation of the unscaled sum of adjacent jumps on a uniform one-dimensional grid Gamma-converges in L1 to continuum total variation.
assumptions_latex: Interpolation is piecewise constant on uniform cells.
The energy is the unscaled sum of adjacent absolute jumps.
knowledge_statements.title: One-Dimensional Exact-Stencil Gamma Limit

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convergence of TV-Regularized Minima and Minimizers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fundamental consequence of a specified TV Gamma limit.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(F_h\) Gamma-converges to \(F\) in \(L^1(\Omega)\), \(G_h\) converges continuously to \(G\), and \((F_h+G_h)\) is equicoercive. Then \(F_h+G_h\) Gamma-converges to \(F+G\), its minimum values converge to the minimum of \(F+G\), and every cluster point of minimizers is a minimizer of \(F+G\). If the continuum minimizer is unique, every relatively compact minimizing sequence converges to it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under continuous convergence of data terms and equicoercivity, a TV Gamma limit transfers minimum values and minimizers to the continuum problem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Minimum values converge and minimizer cluster points solve the continuum problem; uniqueness identifies the full limit.
knowledge_statements.title: Convergence of TV-Regularized Minima and Minimizers

assumptions_latex: \((\mathcal{T}_h)\) is a shape-regular grid family with mesh size \(h\to0\).
\(F_h\) is a consistently scaled nearest-neighbor discrete total variation, extended by \(+\infty\) off its interpolation space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Under isotropically consistent stencils, \(F_h\) \(\Gamma\)-converges in \(L^1(\Omega)\) to \(u\mapsto |Du|(\Omega)\).

notation.meaning: discrete total-variation functional at mesh size h
Gamma convergence in the L1 topology

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A standard Gamma-convergence regime; the precise stencil assumptions require source confirmation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose the grid stencils and weights are normalized so that their discrete surface energy is isotropically consistent. Then
\[
F_h\xrightarrow{\Gamma(L^1(\Omega))}F,
\qquad
F(u)=
\begin{cases}
|Du|(\Omega), & u\in BV(\Omega),\\
+\infty, & u\notin BV(\Omega).
\end{cases}
\]
Thus every sequence \(u_h\to u\) in \(L^1(\Omega)\) satisfies \(F(u)\le\liminf_{h\to0}F_h(u_h)\), and every \(u\in L^1(\Omega)\) admits a recovery sequence satisfying \(F(u)\ge\limsup_{h\to0}F_h(u_h)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With suitable scaling and isotropically consistent stencils, discrete grid total variation Gamma-converges in L1 to continuum BV total variation, comprising both a lower bound and recovery sequences.
knowledge_statements.title: Discrete-to-Continuum Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem kind fits this convergence-regime leaf, but “isotropically consistent” does not specify the stencil, weights, interpolation, or normalization needed to determine the Gamma-limit. The exact theorem cannot be validated without a source.

children.title: Difference-Regularization Order Family
children.top_down_role: First- and higher-order difference regularizers promoting piecewise-simple structure.

children.title: Fused-Difference Regularization
children.top_down_role: Difference penalties promoting locally constant coordinate or signal segments.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact intrinsic first-order certificate for the fused regularizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A vector \(g\) belongs to \(\partial R(x)\) exactly when there exist \(s\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(t\in\mathbb R^{n-1}\) such that
\[g=\lambda_1s+\lambda_2D_1^Tt,\]
where \(s_i=\operatorname{sign}(x_i)\) for \(x_i\ne0\) and \(|s_i|\le1\) otherwise, while \(t_i=\operatorname{sign}((D_1x)_i)\) for \((D_1x)_i\ne0\) and \(|t_i|\le1\) otherwise.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fused-penalty subgradient is a level-sign vector plus the adjoint of a bounded difference-sign vector.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g\in\partial R(x)\iff g=\lambda_1s+\lambda_2D_1^Tt\) with the stated sign constraints.
knowledge_statements.title: Subgradient Certificate for Fused Differences

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp parameter regimes for the one-dimensional fused penalty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(R(x)=\lambda_1\|x\|_1+\lambda_2\|D_1x\|_1\): if \(\lambda_1>0\), then \(R\) is a coercive norm. If \(\lambda_1=0<\lambda_2\), then \(R\) is a seminorm with kernel \(\operatorname{span}\{\mathbf1\}\). If \(\lambda_1=\lambda_2=0\), then \(R\) vanishes identically.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive level penalty makes the fused penalty a coercive norm. Pure first differences leave constants unpenalized, while zero weights give the zero functional.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lambda_1>0\) gives a coercive norm; \(\lambda_1=0<\lambda_2\) gives kernel \(\operatorname{span}\{\mathbf1\}\); both weights zero give the zero functional.
knowledge_statements.title: Coercivity and Nullspace Regimes

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact polyhedral lift of the one-dimensional fused penalty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The condition \(R(x)\le t\) is equivalent to the existence of \(u\in\mathbb R_+^n\) and \(v\in\mathbb R_+^{n-1}\) such that
\[-u\le x\le u,\qquad -v\le D_1x\le v,\qquad \lambda_1\mathbf1^Tu+\lambda_2\mathbf1^Tv\le t.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Auxiliary variables for absolute levels and differences give the fused regularizer a finite linear epigraph representation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{epi}R\) has the displayed finite linear lift.
knowledge_statements.title: Linear-Programming Epigraph

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_{\mathrm{fused}}(x)=\lambda_1\|x\|_1+\lambda_2\|D_1x\|_1\) is a convex regularizer promoting sparsity and piecewise constancy.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-dimensional first-order fused regularization with separate level and difference penalties.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The fused-difference regularizer is
\[
R_{\mathrm{fused}}(x)=\lambda_1\sum_{i=1}^n|x_i|+\lambda_2\sum_{i=1}^{n-1}|x_{i+1}-x_i|
=\lambda_1\|x\|_1+\lambda_2\|D_1x\|_1.
\]
It is convex for \(\lambda_1,\lambda_2\ge0\). The first term penalizes nonzero coordinate levels, while the second penalizes changes between adjacent coordinates. When both weights are positive, the regularizer jointly favors sparse coordinate values and sequences composed of constant segments separated by relatively few jumps.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fused-difference regularization combines an l1 penalty on coordinate values with an l1 penalty on adjacent differences, jointly encouraging sparsity and piecewise-constant structure.
knowledge_statements.title: Fused-Difference Regularization

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The one-dimensional fused-difference definition is precise and fits the leaf; its structural interpretation is standard, but no source or specific locator is supplied.

children.title: Trend-Filtering Regularization
children.top_down_role: Higher-order difference penalties promoting piecewise-polynomial structure.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Intrinsic bounded-sign representation and its use with a differentiable convex loss.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(R(\beta)=\lambda\|D_n^{(k+1)}\beta\|_1\),
\[g\in\partial R(\beta)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad g=\lambda(D_n^{(k+1)})^Tz,\]
where \(z_i=\operatorname{sign}((D_n^{(k+1)}\beta)_i)\) at nonzero differences and \(|z_i|\le1\) at zero differences. Consequently, for a convex differentiable loss \(f\), \(\widehat\beta\) minimizes \(f+R\) exactly when
\[0=\nabla f(\widehat\beta)+\lambda(D_n^{(k+1)})^Tz\]
for such a vector \(z\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The trend-filtering subgradient is the adjoint image of a bounded difference-sign vector; balancing it against the loss gradient exactly certifies optimality.
assumptions_latex: For the optimization statement, \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) is convex and differentiable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed bounded-sign representation characterizes \(\partial R\) and gives a necessary and sufficient optimality condition for \(f+R\).
knowledge_statements.title: Trend-Filtering Subgradient and Optimality Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limits of uniqueness supplied by the trend-filtering penalty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The seminorm \(\|D_n^{(k+1)}\beta\|_1\) vanishes on the degree-at-most-\(k\) polynomial nullspace and is not strictly convex. It therefore does not by itself ensure uniqueness. If an attached loss \(f\) is strictly convex, then \(f+\lambda\|D_n^{(k+1)}\cdot\|_1\) has at most one minimizer; without strict convexity or other identifying restrictions, multiple minimizers can occur.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Trend-filtering regularization alone is non-strictly convex and leaves polynomial directions unpenalized; uniqueness must come from the loss or constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The penalty alone does not imply uniqueness; strict convexity of the loss implies uniqueness whenever a minimizer exists.
knowledge_statements.title: Nullspace and Uniqueness Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural meaning of sparse higher-order differences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an equally spaced sequence \(\beta\), nonzero entries of \(D_n^{(k+1)}\beta\) mark discrete knots. On every consecutive region on which the relevant entries of \(D_n^{(k+1)}\beta\) vanish, \(\beta\) agrees with a discrete polynomial of degree at most \(k\). Thus sparsity of \(D_n^{(k+1)}\beta\) yields a small collection of transitions between discrete polynomial pieces.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonzero differences of order k+1 mark knots; between knots the sequence is a discrete polynomial of degree at most k.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Vanishing order-\((k+1)\) differences characterize degree-at-most-\(k\) discrete polynomial pieces.
knowledge_statements.title: Discrete-Knot Characterization

assumptions_latex: The sampling grid is equally spaced.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_{k,\lambda}(\beta)=\lambda\lVert D_n^{(k+1)}\beta\rVert_1\) is convex, and \(\ker R_{k,\lambda}=\ker D_n^{(k+1)}\) when \(\lambda>0\).

notation.meaning: Conformable forward-difference operator of order r on n coordinates.
Vector of fitted values on the ordered grid.

review_flags: Exact trend-filtering source and indexing convention require certification.
All TeX commands in statement_latex were placed inside explicit math delimiters.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses the convention that degree-k piecewise-polynomial trends are penalized by differences of order k+1.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(n\ge k+2\), let \(D_n^{(1)}\in\mathbb R^{(n-1)\times n}\) be the first-difference operator defined by \((D_n^{(1)}\beta)_i=\beta_{i+1}-\beta_i\), and recursively define \(D_n^{(r+1)}=D_{n-r}^{(1)}D_n^{(r)}\). The order-\(k\) trend-filtering regularizer with weight \(\lambda\ge0\) is
\[
R_{k,\lambda}(\beta)=\lambda\lVert D_n^{(k+1)}\beta\rVert_1,\qquad \beta\in\mathbb R^n.
\]
It is a convex seminorm. When \(\lambda>0\), its nullspace is \(\ker D_n^{(k+1)}\), consisting on an equally spaced grid of sequences sampled from polynomials of degree at most \(k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Trend filtering penalizes the l1 norm of discrete differences of order k+1, leaving sampled polynomials of degree at most k unpenalized when the weight is positive.
knowledge_statements.title: Trend-Filtering Regularization

children.title: Difference-Order Regimes
children.top_down_role: Structural effects associated with the selected order of the difference operator.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes algebraic difference penalties from derivative-consistent discretizations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
On a uniform grid of spacing \(h\), if \(x_i=u(ih)\) for a sufficiently smooth function, then away from boundaries
\[(D_n^{(r)}x)_i=h^r u^{(r)}(ih)+o(h^r).\]
Thus the difference order alone does not determine a continuum normalization. Derivative or integral approximations require explicit powers of \(h\), and changing them can change the limiting functional.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An unscaled rth difference is of order h to the rth power on smooth sampled data, so continuum scaling must be specified separately.
knowledge_statements.title: Grid-Scaling Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear-algebraic structure common to every positive difference order.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(1\le r<n\), \(D_n^{(r)}\) has rank \(n-r\) and an \(r\)-dimensional kernel consisting of sequences generated by discrete polynomials of degree at most \(r-1\). Hence \(x\mapsto\|D_n^{(r)}x\|_1\) is a seminorm on \(\mathbb R^n\) and a norm on \(\mathbb R^n/\ker D_n^{(r)}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An order-r difference matrix has full row rank and an r-dimensional polynomial kernel, so its l1 penalty is a quotient norm rather than a norm on the original space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{rank}D_n^{(r)}=n-r\), \(\dim\ker D_n^{(r)}=r\), and \(\|D_n^{(r)}\cdot\|_1\) is a norm on the quotient by its kernel.
knowledge_statements.title: Rank, Kernel, and Quotient-Norm Structure

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact algebraic descriptions of equally spaced forward differences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(1\le r<n\), define \((D_n^{(1)}x)_i=x_{i+1}-x_i\) and \(D_n^{(r+1)}=D_{n-r}^{(1)}D_n^{(r)}\). Then
\[(D_n^{(r)}x)_i=\sum_{j=0}^r(-1)^{r-j}\binom rj x_{i+j},\qquad i=1,\ldots,n-r.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Higher forward differences are recursive first differences and have the alternating binomial stencil.
assumptions_latex: Coordinates lie on an equally spaced ordered grid.
knowledge_statements.title: Recursive and Binomial Difference Formulas

assumptions_latex: Coordinates correspond to an equally spaced ordered grid.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The order-\(r\) penalty favors discrete polynomial pieces of degree at most \(r-1\) and has nullspace \(\ker D_n^{(r)}\).

notation.meaning: Forward-difference operator of order r on n coordinates.

review_flags: A source explicitly supporting the order convention and piecewise-polynomial interpretation is required.
The promotion language is qualitative and does not assert that every optimizer has the stated structure.
All TeX commands in statement_latex were placed inside explicit math delimiters.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classifies discrete difference penalties by difference order on an equally spaced one-dimensional grid.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(D_n^{(r)}\) denote the order-\(r\) forward-difference operator on \(\mathbb R^n\), and set \(R_r(\beta)=\lambda\lVert D_n^{(r)}\beta\rVert_1\) for \(r\ge1\) and \(\lambda>0\). The regime \(r=1\) penalizes changes between adjacent coordinates and favors piecewise-constant sequences. For \(r\ge2\), sparsity of \(D_n^{(r)}\beta\) means that the order-\((r-1)\) discrete difference changes only at selected indices, favoring discrete polynomial pieces of degree at most \(r-1\). In every regime,
\[
\ker R_r=\ker D_n^{(r)},
\]
and, on an equally spaced grid, this nullspace consists of sequences sampled from polynomials of degree at most \(r-1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: First differences favor constant segments; higher differences favor discrete polynomial pieces, with degree one below the difference order. These are regularization tendencies rather than unconditional descriptions of every optimizer.
knowledge_statements.title: Difference-Order Regimes

children.title: Spectral Matrix Regularizer Family
children.top_down_role: Regularizers acting through eigenvalues, singular values, rank surrogates, or matrix cones.

children.title: Nuclear-Norm Regularization
children.top_down_role: Convex low-rank regularization for rectangular or symmetric matrices.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact proximal evaluation of the nuclear norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(Z=U\operatorname{diag}(\sigma_i)V^\top\) is a singular-value decomposition and \(\tau\ge0\), then \[\operatorname{prox}_{\tau\|\cdot\|_*}(Z)=U\operatorname{diag}((\sigma_i-\tau)_+)V^\top.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The nuclear-norm proximal map soft-thresholds singular values while preserving singular vectors.
knowledge_statements.title: Singular-Value Thresholding Proximal Map

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact first-order certificate at a matrix of arbitrary rank.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=U_r\Sigma_rV_r^\top\) be a compact singular-value decomposition with rank \(r\). Then \[\partial\|X\|_* =\{U_rV_r^\top+W:U_r^\top W=0,\ WV_r=0,\ \|W\|_2\le1\}.\] In particular, \(\partial\|0\|_*=\{W:\|W\|_2\le1\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nuclear-norm subgradient is the polar factor on the active singular spaces plus a spectrally bounded orthogonal component.
knowledge_statements.title: Nuclear-Norm Subdifferential

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual representation of the nuclear norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(X\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \[\|X\|_*=\max_{\|Y\|_2\le1}\langle Y,X\rangle.\] Consequently, for \(\lambda>0\), \[(\lambda\|\cdot\|_*)^*(Y)=\delta_{\{Y:\|Y\|_2\le\lambda\}}(Y).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The nuclear and spectral norms are dual, and the conjugate of a weighted nuclear norm is the indicator of a spectral-norm ball.
knowledge_statements.title: Spectral-Norm Duality and Conjugacy

notation.meaning: The i-th singular value of X.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard matrix convex-analysis definition and convex-envelope characterization; exact source locator pending.
All TeX commands in statement_latex were placed inside explicit math delimiters.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical convex spectral penalty for low-rank rectangular matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a matrix \(X\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) with singular values \(\sigma_1(X),\ldots,\sigma_q(X)\), where \(q=\min\{m,n\}\), its nuclear norm is
\[
\lVert X\rVert_*:=\sum_{i=1}^{q}\sigma_i(X).
\]
Nuclear-norm regularization uses \(R_\lambda(X)=\lambda\lVert X\rVert_*\) with \(\lambda\ge0\). This function is convex and unitarily invariant. Moreover, \(\lVert X\rVert_*\) is the convex envelope of \(\operatorname{rank}(X)\) on the spectral-norm unit ball \(\{X:\lVert X\rVert_2\le1\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The nuclear norm sums a matrix's singular values and supplies the convex envelope of rank on the spectral-norm unit ball.
knowledge_statements.title: Nuclear-Norm Regularization

children.title: General Spectral-Function Regularization
children.top_down_role: Eigenvalue- and singular-value-based convex regularizers.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduction of matrix proximal evaluation to the vector generator's proximal map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R(X)=\phi(\sigma(X))\). If \(X=U\operatorname{Diag}(s)V^{\mathsf T}\) is a singular value decomposition, then \[\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma R}(X)=U\operatorname{Diag}(\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma\phi}(s))V^{\mathsf T}.\] The analogous eigenvalue formula holds for \(F(X)=\phi(\lambda(X))\) on \(\mathbb S^n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex spectral regularizer preserves singular or eigenvectors under its proximal map and applies the vector proximal map to the spectrum.
assumptions_latex: \(\phi\) is proper, lower-semicontinuous, convex, and absolutely symmetric for singular values or permutation invariant for eigenvalues.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Matrix proximal evaluation reduces to spectral decomposition followed by \(\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma\phi}\).
knowledge_statements.title: Spectral Transfer of Proximal Maps

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conjugacy rule for convex spectral regularizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the singular-value construction, \[R^*(Y)=\phi^*(\sigma(Y)).\] For the symmetric eigenvalue construction, \[F^*(Y)=\phi^*(\lambda(Y)).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Fenchel conjugate of a convex spectral function is obtained by conjugating its vector spectral generator.
assumptions_latex: The generator is proper, lower-semicontinuous, convex, and appropriately symmetric.
knowledge_statements.title: Spectral Transfer of Fenchel Conjugacy

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Eigenvalue counterpart of the seed's rectangular singular-value construction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\phi:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper, lower-semicontinuous, convex, and invariant under coordinate permutations. For \(X\in\mathbb S^n\), define \[F(X)=\phi(\lambda(X)).\] Then \(F\) is proper, lower-semicontinuous, convex, and orthogonally invariant.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A symmetric closed convex function of eigenvalues induces a closed convex orthogonally invariant regularizer on symmetric matrices.
assumptions_latex: \(\phi\) is proper, lower-semicontinuous, convex, and permutation invariant.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F=\phi\circ\lambda\) is proper, lower-semicontinuous, convex, and orthogonally invariant.

notation.meaning: eigenvalue vector of a symmetric matrix

knowledge_statements.title: Symmetric-Matrix Eigenvalue Spectral Functions

assumptions_latex: \(\phi:\mathbb R^q\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) is proper, lower-semicontinuous, convex, and absolutely symmetric.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R=\phi\circ\sigma\) is proper, lower-semicontinuous, convex, and unitarily invariant.

notation.meaning: Vector of singular values of X.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard characterization of convex unitarily invariant matrix functions; exact source locator pending.
All TeX commands in statement_latex were placed inside explicit math delimiters.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rectangular-matrix spectral regularizers induced by absolutely symmetric convex functions of singular values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(q=\min\{m,n\}\), and let \(\phi:\mathbb R^q\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper, lower-semicontinuous, convex, and absolutely symmetric, meaning invariant under coordinate permutations and sign changes. The associated spectral regularizer is
\[
R(X)=\phi(\sigma(X)),\qquad X\in\mathbb R^{m\times n},
\]
where \(\sigma(X)=(\sigma_1(X),\ldots,\sigma_q(X))\). Then \(R\) is proper, lower-semicontinuous, convex, and unitarily invariant: \(R(UXV^{\mathsf T})=R(X)\) for every conformable pair of orthogonal matrices \(U,V\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Applying an absolutely symmetric proper lower-semicontinuous convex function to singular values produces a proper lower-semicontinuous convex regularizer invariant under orthogonal changes of matrix coordinates.
knowledge_statements.title: General Spectral-Function Regularization

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proposed counterexample showing that spectral dependence alone does not imply convexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(\mathbb R^{2\times2}\), \(X\mapsto\sigma_{\min}(X)\) violates midpoint convexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The smallest singular value is not a convex matrix function.

knowledge_statements.title: Smallest-Singular-Value Convexity Failure

children.title: Positive-Semidefinite Trace Regularization
children.top_down_role: Trace-based regularization restricted to the positive-semidefinite cone.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_\lambda\) is proper, closed, and convex, and \(R_\lambda(X)=\lambda\lVert X\rVert_*\) whenever \(X\succeq0\).

notation.meaning: Cone of real symmetric positive-semidefinite matrices.
Extended-valued indicator of the positive-semidefinite cone.

review_flags: The cited semidefinite-optimization section should be checked for direct support of the trace/nuclear-norm identity.
All TeX commands in statement_latex were placed inside explicit math delimiters.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extended-valued trace penalty enforcing positive semidefiniteness.

source_refs.locator: 2.1 From Linear to Semidefinite Optimization p. 3
source_refs.source_title: Semidefinite Optimization and Convex Algebraic Geometry

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
On the space \(\mathbb S^n\) of real symmetric matrices, define the positive-semidefinite trace regularizer with \(\lambda\ge0\) by
\[
R_\lambda(X)=\lambda\operatorname{tr}(X)+\delta_{\mathbb S_+^n}(X),
\qquad
\delta_{\mathbb S_+^n}(X)=
\begin{cases}
0,&X\succeq0,\\
+\infty,&X\not\succeq0.
\end{cases}
\]
This function is proper, closed, and convex. For \(X\succeq0\), all eigenvalues are nonnegative, so \(\operatorname{tr}(X)=\sum_i\lambda_i(X)=\lVert X\rVert_*\). Hence trace regularization on the positive-semidefinite cone coincides with nuclear-norm regularization there.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On positive-semidefinite matrices, trace equals nuclear norm; adding the cone indicator yields a proper closed convex low-rank regularizer.
knowledge_statements.title: Positive-Semidefinite Trace Regularization

source_witnesses.locator: 2.1 From Linear to Semidefinite Optimization p. 3
source_witnesses.source_title: Semidefinite Optimization and Convex Algebraic Geometry

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The proximal map shifts eigenvalues by the trace weight and clips them at zero.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Conjugate and Subdifferential of PSD Trace Regularization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual geometry and first-order certificate for the extended-valued trace penalty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R(X)=\lambda\operatorname{tr}(X)+\delta_{\mathbb S_+^n}(X)\) with \(\lambda\ge0\). Under the trace pairing, \[R^*(Y)=\delta_{\{Y\in\mathbb S^n:Y\preceq\lambda I\}}(Y).\] For \(X\succeq0\), \[\partial R(X)=\{\lambda I+Z:Z\preceq0,\ ZX=0\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The conjugate is an upper spectral-order constraint, while subgradients are the trace gradient plus complementary negative-semidefinite normals.
knowledge_statements.title: Conjugate and Subdifferential of PSD Trace Regularization

children.title: Entrywise-Sparse Matrix Penalties
children.top_down_role: Matrix regularizers promoting sparsity among individual entries.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_{\mathrm{ent}}(X)=\lambda\sum_{i,j}|X_{ij}|\) is convex and has the stated coordinatewise subdifferential.

notation.meaning: Sum of the absolute values of all entries of X.
Convex subdifferential of the regularizer at X.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Entrywise sparsity induced by the matrix l1 norm.

source_refs.locator: 3.3.1 Nonsmooth Models of the Objective Function p. 225

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(X=(X_{ij})\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), the entrywise-sparse matrix regularizer with weight \(\lambda\ge0\) is
\[
R_{\mathrm{ent}}(X)=\lambda\lVert X\rVert_{1,\mathrm{ent}}:=\lambda\sum_{i=1}^{m}\sum_{j=1}^{n}|X_{ij}|.
\]
It is convex and, when \(\lambda>0\), is a norm. Its subdifferential consists of matrices \(G\) satisfying \(G_{ij}=\lambda\operatorname{sign}(X_{ij})\) when \(X_{ij}\ne0\), and \(G_{ij}\in[-\lambda,\lambda]\) when \(X_{ij}=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The entrywise l1 penalty sums absolute matrix entries, is convex, and promotes zeros at individually selected positions.
knowledge_statements.title: Entrywise-Sparse Matrix Penalties

source_witnesses.locator: 3.3.1 Nonsmooth Models of the Objective Function p. 225

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact proximal evaluation of the entrywise matrix l1 penalty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(R(X)=\lambda\sum_{i,j}|X_{ij}|\) and \(\gamma>0\), \[\bigl(\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma R}(Z)\bigr)_{ij}=\operatorname{sign}(Z_{ij})(|Z_{ij}|-\gamma\lambda)_+.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The proximal map independently soft-thresholds every matrix entry.
knowledge_statements.title: Entrywise Soft Thresholding

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual norm and conjugate of the entrywise matrix l1 penalty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(J(X)=\sum_{i,j}|X_{ij}|\), \[J^\circ(Y)=\max_{i,j}|Y_{ij}|.\] Hence, for \(\lambda>0\), \[(\lambda J)^*(Y)=\delta_{\{Y:\max_{i,j}|Y_{ij}|\le\lambda\}}(Y).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The dual of the entrywise matrix l1 norm is the maximum-absolute-entry norm.
knowledge_statements.title: Entrywise Infinity Duality

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal G\) be a partition of \(\{1,\ldots,m\}\times\{1,\ldots,n\}\) into nonempty blocks. For weights \(w_g>0\) and \(\lambda\ge0\), define
\[
R_{\mathrm{blk}}(X)=\lambda\sum_{g\in\mathcal G}w_g\lVert X_g\rVert_2,
\qquad X\in\mathbb R^{m\times n},
\]
where \(X_g\) is the vector of entries indexed by \(g\). The regularizer is convex and, for \(\lambda>0\), is a norm. Its nonsmoothness at \(X_g=0\) supports blockwise sparsity under suitable optimization models.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A weighted sum of Euclidean norms of disjoint entry blocks is convex and favors matrices whose nonzero entries occur in a small number of prescribed blocks.
knowledge_statements.title: Block-Sparse Matrix Penalties

source_witnesses.locator: 3.3.1 Nonsmooth Models of the Objective Function p. 225

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact proximal map for disjoint block penalties.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(R(X)=\lambda\sum_{g\in\mathcal G}w_g\|X_g\|_2\) and \(\gamma>0\), \[\bigl(\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma R}(Z)\bigr)_g=\left(1-\frac{\gamma\lambda w_g}{\|Z_g\|_2}\right)_+Z_g,\] with value zero when \(Z_g=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The proximal map independently shrinks each block and deletes blocks below their weighted thresholds.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual geometry and blockwise certificate for a partitioned group norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(J(X)=\sum_{g\in\mathcal G}w_g\|X_g\|_2\), \[J^\circ(Y)=\max_{g\in\mathcal G}\frac{\|Y_g\|_2}{w_g}.\] Moreover, \(G\in\partial J(X)\) exactly when \[G_g=w_gX_g/\|X_g\|_2\quad(X_g\ne0),\qquad \|G_g\|_2\le w_g\quad(X_g=0).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The dual block norm is a weighted block maximum, and the subgradient separates over active and zero blocks.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal G\) is a partition into nonempty blocks.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: J^\circ(Y)=\max_g\|Y_g\|_2/w_g\text{ and }\partial J(X)\text{ has the displayed block form}.
knowledge_statements.title: Dual Norm and Block Subdifferential

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Rank Is Not a Convex Spectral Penalty
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary motivating convex singular-value surrogates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A=\operatorname{diag}(1,0)\) and \(B=\operatorname{diag}(0,1)\). Then \(\operatorname{rank}(A)=\operatorname{rank}(B)=1\), while \[\operatorname{rank}\left(\frac{A+B}{2}\right)=2>\frac{\operatorname{rank}(A)+\operatorname{rank}(B)}2.\] Hence matrix rank is not convex, although it is a spectral function counting nonzero singular values.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rank directly measures low-dimensional structure but is nonconvex, motivating convex singular-value surrogates such as nuclear norm.
knowledge_statements.title: Rank Is Not a Convex Spectral Penalty
