children.title: Product-Space Lifts
children.top_down_role: Lifted representations that place component variables in a Cartesian product space.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Block-Separable Calculus on a Product Space
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conjugate and proximal separability exposed by Cartesian-product lifting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y=\prod_{i=1}^mY_i\) have its canonical product inner product and let \(R(z)=\sum_{i=1}^m r_i(z_i)\), where \(r_i\in\Gamma_0(Y_i)\). Then \(R\in\Gamma_0(Y)\), \(R^*(y)=\sum_{i=1}^m r_i^*(y_i)\), and for \(\lambda>0\), \[\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda R}(z)=\bigl(\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda r_i}(z_i)\bigr)_{i=1}^m.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A separable function on a Cartesian product has a block-separable conjugate and proximal mapping.
assumptions_latex: Each \(Y_i\) is a finite-dimensional Hilbert space and \(r_i\in\Gamma_0(Y_i)\).
The canonical unweighted product metric is used.

notation.meaning: Block-separable function on the product space.

knowledge_statements.title: Block-Separable Calculus on a Product Space
Product-Space Lifts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separable product-space reformulation of a finite sum of composite terms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X,Y_1,\ldots,Y_m\) be finite-dimensional real vector spaces, let \(F:X\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\), let \(A_i:X\to Y_i\) be affine, and let \(r_i:Y_i\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\). With \(Y=\prod_{i=1}^mY_i\), the problem
\[
\inf_{x\in X}\left(F(x)+\sum_{i=1}^m r_i(A_i x)\right)
\]
has the exact lift
\[
\inf_{x\in X,\,z\in Y}\left\{F(x)+\sum_{i=1}^m r_i(z_i):z_i=A_i x\ \text{for all }i\right\}.
\]
Feasible lifted points project to the original point \(x\), and every original point has the unique compatible block vector \(z=(A_1x,\ldots,A_mx)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each composite term receives its own product-space block, linked to the original variable by an affine equality; projection and canonical lifting preserve objectives and minimizers.
assumptions_latex: \(m\) is finite and every \(Y_i\) is finite-dimensional.
All sums use extended-real arithmetic without undefined combinations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The original and product-space formulations have equal infima and corresponding minimizers under \(z_i=A_i x\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The product-space representation is mathematically precise and fits the terminal container, but it has no cited source or inspectable locator.

children.title: Consensus Variable Lifts
children.top_down_role: Replicated-variable representations coupled through a shared consensus structure.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual geometry of the product-space consensus constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D:=\{(x_1,\ldots,x_m)\in(\mathbb R^n)^m:x_1=\cdots=x_m\}\). Under the standard product inner product, \[D^\perp=\left\{(u_1,\ldots,u_m):\sum_{i=1}^m u_i=0\right\},\qquad \delta_D^*=\delta_{D^\perp}.\] Thus consensus-normal multiplier vectors are exactly the zero-sum vectors.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The orthogonal complement of consensus consists exactly of zero-sum local multipliers, and the consensus indicator conjugates to its indicator.
assumptions_latex: The product space uses the standard sum inner product.
knowledge_statements.title: Consensus Subspace Orthogonal Complement

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sparse edge-based representation of equality consensus among finitely many variable copies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a finite undirected graph on \(V=\{1,\ldots,m\}\), let \(x_i\in\mathbb R^n\), and let \(B\) be an oriented vertex-edge incidence matrix. If G is connected, then \[x_i=x_j\quad\forall\{i,j\}\in E\] is equivalent to \(x_i=z\) for every i and some \(z\), and equivalently to \[(B^\top\otimes I_n)x=0.\] Its nullspace is \(\{\mathbf1_m\otimes z:z\in\mathbb R^n\}\). If G is disconnected, edge equalities impose consensus only within each connected component.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Global consensus can be enforced by edge equalities on any connected graph; disconnected graphs yield only componentwise consensus.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For connected G, \(\ker(B^\top\otimes I_n)=\{\mathbf1_m\otimes z:z\in\mathbb R^n\}\).
knowledge_statements.title: Connected-Graph Consensus Constraints
Consensus Variable Lifts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consensus reformulation obtained by replicating a shared decision variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) be a finite-dimensional real vector space and let \(f_i:X\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) for \(i=1,\ldots,m\). The shared-variable problem
\[
\inf_{x\in X}\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x)
\]
is equivalent to
\[
\inf_{z,x_1,\ldots,x_m\in X}\left\{\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x_i):x_i=z\ \text{for all }i\right\}.
\]
The diagonal embedding \(x\mapsto(x,\ldots,x)\) maps every original feasible point to a consensus-feasible point with the same objective. Conversely, every consensus-feasible tuple has \(x_1=\cdots=x_m=z\), so projection onto \(z\) preserves objective values and minimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replicate the shared variable for separate components and impose equality to one consensus variable. The diagonal embedding and projection preserve feasible objectives and minimizers.
assumptions_latex: The sum contains no undefined extended-real combination.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The consensus representation is mathematically precise and correctly classified, but no source or locator supports it.

children.title: Lift Equivalence Structure
children.top_down_role: Relationships between lifted feasible points, original variables, and equivalent objective values.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Equal Values Do Not Ensure Optimizer Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp boundary between equality of optimal values and exact recovery of optimizer sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C=\{0,1\}\), \(f(0)=0\), \(f(1)=1\), \(D=C\times\{0\}\), and \(g(0,0)=g(1,0)=0\). Then \(\inf_Dg=\inf_Cf=0\), but \(\operatorname{proj}_X\operatorname*{argmin}_Dg=\{0,1\}\neq\{0\}=\operatorname*{argmin}_Cf\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equality of infima permits spurious lifted minimizers and therefore is weaker than exact lift equivalence.
knowledge_statements.title: Equal Values Do Not Ensure Optimizer Correspondence

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fiberwise Value-Function Criterion for Exact Lifts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise exactness after eliminating auxiliary variables, including the attainment condition needed for optimizer lifting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq X\), \(D\subseteq X\times Z\), and \(h(x)=\inf\{g(x,z):(x,z)\in D\}\), with \(h(x)=+\infty\) for an empty fiber. The lift is pointwise objective-equivalent exactly when \(h=f+\delta_C\) on \(X\). In that case \(\inf_D g=\inf_C f\), and every lifted minimizer projects to an original minimizer. If the fiber infimum is attained for every \(x\in\operatorname*{argmin}_C f\), then \(\operatorname{proj}_X\operatorname*{argmin}_D g=\operatorname*{argmin}_C f\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eliminating the auxiliary variable must recover the original extended-valued objective. Lifting every original minimizer additionally requires attainment in its auxiliary fiber.
assumptions_latex: The infimum of an empty fiber is \(+\infty\).
Fiber attainment is required only for lifting original minimizers.

notation.meaning: Lifted objective after elimination of the auxiliary variable.
Extended-valued indicator of the original feasible set.

knowledge_statements.title: Fiberwise Value-Function Criterion for Exact Lifts
Lift Equivalence Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact equivalence criterion for objective-preserving lifted formulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\inf_{x\in C}f(x)\) and \(L=\inf_{(x,z)\in D}g(x,z)\), where \(C\subseteq X\) and \(D\subseteq X\times Z\). Suppose that for every \(x\in C\) there exists \(z\) with \((x,z)\in D\) and \(g(x,z)=f(x)\), while every \((x,z)\in D\) satisfies \(x\in C\) and \(g(x,z)=f(x)\). Then \(P=L\). Moreover, projection of any lifted minimizer is an original minimizer, and every original minimizer admits a lifted minimizer. Thus the two formulations are equivalent in value and in their optimizer sets after projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lift is exact when every original point has an objective-preserving lift and every lifted point projects to an original point with the same objective.
assumptions_latex: The lift and projection conditions preserve the objective exactly.
Infima and minimizers use extended-real conventions.

notation.meaning: Projection onto the original variable space.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The exact-lift property and projected optimizer equality follow from the stated hypotheses and fit this leaf, but the record lacks source evidence.

children.title: Polyhedral Regularizer Representations
children.top_down_role: Linear and piecewise-linear representations of polyhedral penalties.

knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral Regularizer Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite max-affine representation of proper closed polyhedral convex penalties.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A proper closed convex function \(r:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) is polyhedral if and only if there exist a nonempty polyhedron \(P=\{x:Bx\le d\}\), vectors \(a_1,\ldots,a_m\in\mathbb R^n\), and scalars \(b_1,\ldots,b_m\in\mathbb R\) such that
\[
r(x)=\max_{1\le i\le m}(a_i^{\mathsf T}x+b_i)+\delta_P(x).
\]
Consequently, \(r(x)\le t\) is represented exactly by the linear inequalities \(Bx\le d\) and \(a_i^{\mathsf T}x+b_i\le t\) for all \(i\). Hence adding a polyhedral regularizer to a linearly representable model preserves linear representability after an epigraph lift.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every proper closed polyhedral convex penalty is max-affine on a polyhedral domain, so its epigraph is described by finitely many linear inequalities.
assumptions_latex: \(r:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) is proper, closed, and convex.
The maximum contains finitely many affine functions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r\) is polyhedral exactly when it has the displayed max-affine-plus-indicator representation.

notation.meaning: Effective polyhedral domain of the representation.

children.title: Second-Order-Cone Regularizer Representations
children.top_down_role: Conic representations of Euclidean, group, and related norm structures.

knowledge_statements.title: Second-Order-Cone Regularizer Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Second-order-cone epigraph for weighted sums of Euclidean group norms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G_j:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^{p_j}\) be linear and let \(w_j\ge0\) for \(j=1,\ldots,m\). For
\[
r(x)=\sum_{j=1}^m w_j\lVert G_jx\rVert_2,
\]
the epigraph condition \(r(x)\le\tau\) holds if and only if there exist \(t_1,\ldots,t_m\ge0\) such that
\[
(G_jx,t_j)\in\mathcal Q^{p_j+1}\ \text{for every }j,
\qquad
\sum_{j=1}^m w_jt_j\le\tau,
\]
where \(\mathcal Q^{p+1}=\{(u,t):\lVert u\rVert_2\le t\}\). Thus Euclidean, group-lasso, and block-norm penalties possess exact second-order-cone lifts.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A weighted sum of Euclidean group norms has an exact lift using one Lorentz-cone constraint per group and one linear inequality coupling their epigraph variables.
assumptions_latex: Each \(G_j\) is linear between finite-dimensional Euclidean spaces.
The number of groups is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r(x)\le\tau\) is equivalent to the displayed system of second-order-cone and linear constraints.

notation.meaning: The Lorentz or second-order cone in \(\mathbb R^p\times\mathbb R\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The second-order-cone epigraph formulation is correct, including for zero weights, and its knowledge kind fits the leaf. No source or locator is supplied.

children.title: Semidefinite Regularizer Representations
children.top_down_role: Matrix-cone representations of spectral and atomic structures.

knowledge_statements.title: Semidefinite Regularizer Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semidefinite epigraph representation of the matrix nuclear norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a real matrix \(X\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), its nuclear norm has the semidefinite representation
\[
\lVert X\rVert_*=\frac{1}{2}\inf_{U\in\mathbb S^m,\,V\in\mathbb S^n}
\left\{\operatorname{tr}(U)+\operatorname{tr}(V):
\begin{pmatrix}U&X\\X^{\mathsf T}&V\end{pmatrix}\succeq0\right\}.
\]
Equivalently, \(\lVert X\rVert_*\le t\) if and only if there exist \(U\in\mathbb S^m\) and \(V\in\mathbb S^n\) satisfying the displayed positive-semidefinite constraint and \(\operatorname{tr}(U)+\operatorname{tr}(V)\le2t\). Therefore nuclear-norm regularization admits an exact matrix-cone lift.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The nuclear norm is the minimum half-sum of two traces subject to a block positive-semidefinite constraint, yielding an exact semidefinite epigraph lift.
assumptions_latex: Positive semidefiniteness uses the usual Loewner order.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The nuclear norm and its epigraph equal the displayed semidefinite representations.

notation.meaning: Sum of the singular values of \(X\).
Space of real symmetric \(k\times k\) matrices.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact semidefinite epigraph representation of the rectangular matrix operator norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(X\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) and \(t\in\mathbb R\), \[\lVert X\rVert_2\le t\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \begin{pmatrix}tI_m&X\\X^{\mathsf T}&tI_n\end{pmatrix}\succeq0.\] Consequently, spectral-norm regularization and spectral-norm constraints admit direct semidefinite representations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rectangular matrix has spectral norm at most a scalar exactly when the associated symmetric block matrix is positive semidefinite.
assumptions_latex: \(\lVert X\rVert_2\) denotes the largest singular value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lVert X\rVert_2\le t\) if and only if \(\begin{pmatrix}tI_m&X\\X^{\mathsf T}&tI_n\end{pmatrix}\succeq0\).

children.title: Value Oracle Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Access contracts returning component objective values.

knowledge_statements.title: Value Oracle Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact scalar-value access for a smooth objective component.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(D\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) and let \(f:D\to\mathbb R\). An exact value oracle for \(f\) is an interface \(\mathcal O_f^{\mathrm{val}}\) whose admissible queries are points \(x\in D\) and whose response satisfies
\[
\mathcal O_f^{\mathrm{val}}(x)=f(x).
\]
The interface supplies no derivative information unless this is separately specified. If queries outside \(D\) are permitted operationally, the interface must return a distinguished domain-error response rather than a numerical value purported to equal \(f(x)\). Oracle complexity counts each admissible evaluation request as one value-oracle call.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A value oracle accepts a point in the component’s domain and returns its exact scalar value, with derivative access treated as a separate capability.
assumptions_latex: \(D\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is the declared query domain.
The oracle is exact and deterministic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every admissible query \(x\in D\), \(\mathcal O_f^{\mathrm{val}}(x)=f(x)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The exact deterministic value-oracle definition fits the interface leaf, but the record provides no source for the definition or its call-count convention.

children.title: Gradient Oracle Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Access contracts returning first-order derivative information for smooth components.

knowledge_statements.title: Gradient Oracle Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact first-derivative access for a differentiable smooth component.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(D\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be open and let \(f:D\to\mathbb R\) be differentiable. An exact gradient oracle for \(f\) is an interface \(\mathcal O_f^{\mathrm{grad}}\) whose admissible queries are points \(x\in D\) and whose response satisfies
\[
\mathcal O_f^{\mathrm{grad}}(x)=\nabla f(x)\in\mathbb R^n.
\]
The returned vector represents the derivative under the declared Euclidean inner product. The interface need not return \(f(x)\); value access is a distinct capability unless a joint interface is specified. Oracle complexity counts each query as one gradient-oracle call.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A gradient oracle returns the exact gradient at every admissible point; it does not implicitly provide the function value unless the interface says so.
assumptions_latex: The Euclidean inner product fixes the gradient representation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The gradient-oracle definition is internally consistent and correctly separated from value access, but it lacks a source and locator.

children.title: Joint Value–Gradient Access
children.top_down_role: Interfaces providing coordinated value and gradient information from a single component query.

knowledge_statements.title: Joint Value–Gradient Access
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Atomic access to a consistent value-gradient pair at one query point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(D\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be open and let \(f:D\to\mathbb R\) be differentiable. A joint value-gradient oracle is an interface \(\mathcal O_f^{\mathrm{vg}}\) satisfying
\[
\mathcal O_f^{\mathrm{vg}}(x)=\bigl(f(x),\nabla f(x)\bigr)
\qquad\text{for every }x\in D.
\]
Both components of the response correspond to the same query and the same realization of \(f\). One joint call may be counted separately from one value call plus one gradient call; the chosen oracle-cost convention must therefore state whether joint access has unit cost or decomposed cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A joint oracle returns a mutually consistent function value and gradient for the same query, with its call cost specified by the computational model.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The joint value-gradient interface is precise and fits the leaf, but neither its definition nor the cost-model statement has cited support.

children.title: Subgradient Oracles
children.top_down_role: Access interfaces for nonsmooth components without tractable proximal structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Subgradient Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact first-order oracle access for a proper convex nonsmooth component.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper and convex. An exact subgradient oracle is an interface \(\mathcal O_f^{\mathrm{sub}}\) defined on a declared set \(D\subseteq\operatorname{dom}f\) such that every response \(g=\mathcal O_f^{\mathrm{sub}}(x)\) satisfies
\[
f(y)\ge f(x)+\langle g,y-x\rangle
\qquad\text{for every }y\in\mathbb R^n.
\]
Equivalently, \(g\in\partial f(x)\). If \(\partial f(x)\) contains several vectors, the interface may return any one of them according to its declared deterministic or stochastic selection rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A subgradient oracle returns a vector defining a global affine lower support to the convex function at the queried point.

source_refs.locator: 8.1 From Gradient Descent to Subgradient Descent p. 195

source_witnesses.locator: 8.1 From Gradient Descent to Subgradient Descent p. 195

knowledge_statements.statement_title: A Proper Closed Convex Function May Lack a Boundary Subgradient
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of universal subgradient-oracle access at an effective-domain boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define \(f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) by
\[
f(x)=\begin{cases}-\sqrt{1-x^2},&|x|\le1,\\+\infty,&|x|>1.\end{cases}
\]
Then \(f\) is proper, closed, and convex, but \(\partial f(1)=\varnothing\). Therefore an exact subgradient oracle cannot generally declare every point of \(\operatorname{dom}f\) admissible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proper closed convex function can have no finite subgradient at a boundary point, so domain-wide exact oracle access is not automatic.
knowledge_statements.title: A Proper Closed Convex Function May Lack a Boundary Subgradient

children.title: Proximal Oracles
children.top_down_role: Exact or certified approximate access through proximal subproblems.

knowledge_statements.title: Proximal Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact or residual-certified approximate access to a convex proximal subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(r:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper, closed, and convex. For \(\lambda>0\), an exact proximal oracle returns
\[
p=\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda r}(x)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{u\in\mathbb R^n}\left\{r(u)+\frac{1}{2\lambda}\lVert u-x\rVert_2^2\right\}.
\]
A residual-certified \(\delta\)-approximate response consists of \((p,v)\) with \(v\in\partial r(p)\) and
\[
\lVert p-x+\lambda v\rVert_2\le\delta.
\]
The case \(\delta=0\) is exact. The certificate is checkable whenever membership \(v\in\partial r(p)\) is itself verifiable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proximal oracle solves a strongly convex regularized subproblem; an approximate response can be certified by a subgradient and a bounded optimality residual.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The exact response is \(\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda r}(x)\); a certified approximate response obeys \(v\in\partial r(p)\) and \(\lVert p-x+\lambda v\rVert_2\le\delta\).

children.title: Linear-Minimization Oracles
children.top_down_role: Access interfaces for atomic, gauge, and constrained geometries.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Failure of Exact Linear-Minimization Access Without Attainment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Attainment boundary for an exact point-returning linear-minimization oracle.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C=(0,1)\subset\mathbb R\) and \(d=1\). Then \(\inf_{s\in C}ds=0\), but \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{s\in C}ds=\varnothing\). Thus a finite linear infimum need not admit an exact point-valued response; nonempty compact sets in finite dimensions guarantee attainment, whereas boundedness alone does not.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On the open interval (0,1), minimizing the identity has finite value zero but no minimizer.
knowledge_statements.title: Failure of Exact Linear-Minimization Access Without Attainment

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive-accuracy variant and its lower-bound certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For nonempty \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), query \(d\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(\varepsilon\ge0\), an additive \(\varepsilon\)-accurate response is \(\widehat s\in C\) satisfying
\[
\langle d,\widehat s\rangle\le \inf_{s\in C}\langle d,s\rangle+\varepsilon.
\]
If a validated bound \(L\le\inf_{s\in C}\langle d,s\rangle\) is also returned, feasibility of \(\widehat s\) and \(\langle d,\widehat s\rangle-L\le\varepsilon\) certify this accuracy. For \(\varepsilon=0\), such a response is an exact minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inexact LMO returns a feasible point within an additive tolerance; a valid lower bound makes the tolerance verifiable.
assumptions_latex: For certification, \(L\le\inf_{s\in C}\langle d,s\rangle\) is validated independently.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat s\) is additively \(\varepsilon\)-optimal; the displayed upper-minus-lower bound certifies this claim.

notation.meaning: Validated lower bound on the queried linear optimum.

knowledge_statements.title: Additively Inexact Linear-Minimization Oracle

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Support-function and exposed-face representation of an LMO query.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For nonempty \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), let \(\sigma_C(z)=\sup_{s\in C}\langle z,s\rangle\). In the extended-real sense,
\[
\inf_{s\in C}\langle d,s\rangle=-\sigma_C(-d)
=-\sigma_{\operatorname{conv}C}(-d).
\]
If the infimum is attained, its minimizers are
\[
C\cap\operatorname*{argmax}_{s\in\operatorname{conv}C}\langle-d,s\rangle.
\]
Hence they are the points of \(C\) lying in the exposed face of \(\operatorname{conv}C\) selected by \(-d\); convexification preserves the oracle value but can enlarge the returned solution set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Linear minimization is support-function evaluation in the opposite direction, and attained solutions lie in the corresponding exposed face of the convex hull.
assumptions_latex: Attainment is required only for the minimizer-set statement.
review_flags: revised_builder_claim: exposed-face wording corrected for nonconvex C
knowledge_statements.title: Support-Function Representation of Linear Minimization

assumptions_latex: The feasible region \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is nonempty and compact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The oracle returns some \(s(d)\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{s\in C}\langle d,s\rangle\), optionally together with the value \(\langle d,s(d)\rangle\).

notation.meaning: linear objective supplied to the oracle

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard definition of a linear-minimization oracle
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact Euclidean linear-minimization interface over a compact feasible region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A linear-minimization oracle for a nonempty compact set \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is a map that, for every query \(d\in\mathbb{R}^n\), returns a point \(s(d)\in C\) satisfying
\[
\langle d,s(d)\rangle=\min_{s\in C}\langle d,s\rangle.
\]
The interface may also return the minimum value. If \(C=\operatorname{conv}(\mathcal A)\) for an atomic set \(\mathcal A\), an optimal output can be chosen from \(\mathcal A\) whenever the minimum is attained there. For a gauge unit ball, the same query exposes a supporting atom or face.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A linear-minimization oracle returns a feasible point minimizing a queried linear functional; for atomic convex hulls, an optimal atom may be returned.
knowledge_statements.title: Linear-Minimization Oracles

children.title: Proximal Evaluation Structures
children.top_down_role: Regularizer structures that reduce proximal evaluation to recognized computational primitives.

children.title: Decomposable Proximal Evaluation
children.top_down_role: Coordinatewise and blockwise decomposition of proximal problems.

children.title: Coordinate-Separable Proximal Evaluation
children.top_down_role: Proximal evaluation decomposed into independent scalar or coordinate subproblems.

assumptions_latex: Each \(r_i:\mathbb{R}\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(v\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \(\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma r}(v)_i=\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma r_i}(v_i)\) for all \(i\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: direct separability of the Euclidean proximal objective
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Euclidean proximal evaluation for a sum of scalar coordinate functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(r:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) have the coordinate-separable form \(r(x)=\sum_{i=1}^n r_i(x_i)\), where every \(r_i\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex. For \(\gamma>0\) and \(v\in\mathbb{R}^n\),
\[
\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma r}(v)
=\bigl(\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma r_1}(v_1),\ldots,
\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma r_n}(v_n)\bigr),
\]
where \(\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma r_i}(v_i)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{t\in\mathbb{R}}\{r_i(t)+(t-v_i)^2/(2\gamma)\}\). Thus one proximal query decomposes into \(n\) independent scalar queries.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The proximal map of a coordinatewise sum is obtained by applying each scalar proximal map independently to the corresponding coordinate.
knowledge_statements.title: Coordinate-Separable Proximal Evaluation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The coordinatewise proximal representation is correctly scoped and stated, but the record supplies no source with a specific locator.

children.title: Blockwise Proximal Evaluation
children.top_down_role: Proximal evaluation decomposed across prescribed groups or variable blocks.

assumptions_latex: The space decomposes orthogonally as \(H=H_1\oplus\cdots\oplus H_m\).
Each \(r_j:H_j\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: product-space separability of the Euclidean proximal objective
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Independent proximal evaluation across orthogonal variable blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let the Hilbert space be the orthogonal product \(H=H_1\oplus\cdots\oplus H_m\), and let \(r(x)=\sum_{j=1}^m r_j(x_j)\), with each \(r_j:H_j\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex. For \(\gamma>0\) and \(v=(v_1,\ldots,v_m)\in H\),
\[
\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma r}(v)
=\bigl(\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma r_1}(v_1),\ldots,
\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma r_m}(v_m)\bigr).
\]
Consequently, the full proximal evaluation consists of independent blockwise evaluations and may be executed in parallel.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an orthogonal block decomposition and a block-separable regularizer, the full proximal map is the tuple of independent block proximal maps.
knowledge_statements.title: Blockwise Proximal Evaluation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The blockwise proximal representation and its hypotheses fit the leaf, but no inspectable supporting citation is provided.

children.title: Coupled-Block Failure Boundary
children.top_down_role: Cross-block dependencies that prevent direct decomposition of the proximal evaluation.

knowledge_statements.title: Coupled-Block Failure Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A cross-block term destroys independent blockwise proximal evaluation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Blockwise proximal decomposition generally fails when the regularizer couples distinct blocks. For example, take \(r(x_1,x_2)=\lambda(x_1-x_2)^2/2\) with \(\lambda>0\). For \(\gamma>0\) and \(v=(a,-a)\) with \(a\ne0\), direct minimization gives
\[
\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma r}(a,-a)
=\left(\frac{a}{1+2\gamma\lambda},-\frac{a}{1+2\gamma\lambda}\right).
\]
Each output coordinate depends on the cross-block coupling. Hence the coordinate or block product formula is unavailable unless the coupling is removed, absorbed into a compatible metric, or handled by an auxiliary splitting method.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cross-block quadratic changes both coordinates jointly, so its proximal map cannot be evaluated as independent coordinate or block proximal maps.
assumptions_latex: The coupling strength and stepsize satisfy \(\lambda>0\) and \(\gamma>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The proximal output is \((a/(1+2\gamma\lambda),-a/(1+2\gamma\lambda))\), so independent coordinate evaluation is invalid.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: explicit coupled quadratic proximal calculation

children.title: Projection-Based Proximal Evaluation
children.top_down_role: Indicator, norm-ball, cone, and epigraph projection interfaces.

assumptions_latex: The set \(C\) is nonempty, closed, and convex in a Hilbert space \(H\).
The indicator is \(\delta_C(x)=0\) on \(C\) and \(+\infty\) otherwise.

notation.meaning: indicator function of the feasible set
metric projection onto the feasible set

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Indicator proximal maps as metric projections onto closed convex sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\) be a nonempty closed convex subset of a Hilbert space \(H\), and define its indicator by \(\delta_C(x)=0\) for \(x\in C\) and \(\delta_C(x)=+\infty\) otherwise. For every \(\gamma>0\) and \(v\in H\),
\[
\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma\delta_C}(v)
=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}\frac12\lVert x-v\rVert^2
=P_C(v).
\]
Thus a proximal oracle for an indicator is exactly a projection oracle. This interface applies to convex norm balls, closed convex cones, and closed convex epigraphs whenever their metric projections are computable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The proximal map of a closed convex set's indicator is its metric projection, covering projection interfaces for balls, cones, and epigraphs.
knowledge_statements.title: Projection-Based Proximal Evaluation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The indicator-projection identity is correctly scoped and the property kind fits, but the record has no inspectable citation.

children.title: Sparsity Thresholding Interface Family
children.top_down_role: Thresholding structures associated with sparse and grouped penalties.

children.title: Scalar Thresholding Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Thresholding primitives acting independently on scalar coefficients.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinate-dependent scalar thresholds for a weighted l1 penalty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(r(x)=\sum_{i=1}^n\lambda_i|x_i|\), where \(\lambda_i\ge0\). For every \(\gamma>0\),
\[
(\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma r}(v))_i=S_{\gamma\lambda_i}(v_i)=\operatorname{sign}(v_i)(|v_i|-\gamma\lambda_i)_+.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A weighted l1 proximal map soft-thresholds each coordinate using its own weight.
knowledge_statements.title: Weighted Coordinatewise Soft Thresholding

knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-sided threshold interface for a nonnegative scalar with a linear penalty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(r(t)=\lambda t+\delta_{[0,+\infty)}(t)\), where \(\lambda\ge0\). For every \(\gamma>0\) and \(v\in\mathbb R\),
\[
\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma r}(v)=\max\{v-\gamma\lambda,0\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonnegative coefficient with a linear penalty is evaluated by subtracting the threshold and clipping at zero.

notation.meaning: extended-valued indicator of the nonnegative half-line

knowledge_statements.title: Nonnegative Scalar Soft Thresholding

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar threshold-and-rescale interface for absolute-value and quadratic penalties.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(r(t)=\lambda_1|t|+\frac{\lambda_2}{2}t^2\), where \(\lambda_1,\lambda_2\ge0\). For every \(\gamma>0\),
\[
\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma r}(v)=\frac{1}{1+\gamma\lambda_2}S_{\gamma\lambda_1}(v).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Elastic-net proximal evaluation soft-thresholds the scalar and then applies quadratic rescaling.
knowledge_statements.title: Elastic-Net Scalar Thresholding

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The proximal map is coordinatewise soft thresholding: \((\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma r}(v))_i=\operatorname{sign}(v_i)\max\{|v_i|-\gamma\lambda,0\}\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard proximal formula for the l1 norm
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Soft-threshold interface for the weighted scalar absolute-value penalty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(r(x)=\lambda\lVert x\rVert_1\) on \(\mathbb{R}^n\), with \(\lambda\ge0\), the Euclidean proximal map at stepsize \(\gamma>0\) is evaluated coordinatewise by soft thresholding:
\[
\bigl(\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma r}(v)\bigr)_i
=S_{\gamma\lambda}(v_i)
=\operatorname{sign}(v_i)\max\{|v_i|-\gamma\lambda,0\},
\qquad i=1,\ldots,n.
\]
The convention \(\operatorname{sign}(0)=0\) makes the interface single-valued. Coordinates at or below the threshold are returned as zero, while larger magnitudes are reduced by exactly \(\gamma\lambda\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The proximal map of the l1 penalty applies soft thresholding independently: small coordinates become zero and larger ones shrink by the threshold.
knowledge_statements.title: Scalar Thresholding Interfaces

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The soft-thresholding representation is mathematically precise and fits the scalar-interface leaf, but no source or locator is supplied.

children.title: Group Thresholding Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Thresholding primitives acting jointly on vector or block magnitudes.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed proximal interface for disjoint sparse-group penalties.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G_1,\ldots,G_m\) partition the coordinates and let \(r(x)=\alpha\lVert x\rVert_1+\sum_{j=1}^m\beta_j\lVert x_{G_j}\rVert_2\), where \(\alpha,\beta_j\ge0\). For \(\gamma>0\), set \(w_{G_j}=S_{\gamma\alpha}(v_{G_j})\) coordinatewise. Then
\[
(\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma r}(v))_{G_j}=\left(1-\frac{\gamma\beta_j}{\lVert w_{G_j}\rVert_2}\right)_+w_{G_j},
\]
with zero output when \(w_{G_j}=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a disjoint sparse-group penalty, first soft-threshold every coordinate and then apply radial group shrinkage to each resulting block.
review_flags: zero intermediate block convention stated explicitly
knowledge_statements.title: Sparse-Group Block Thresholding

assumptions_latex: The index sets \(G_1,\ldots,G_m\) form a partition of the coordinates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each block satisfies \((\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma r}(v))_{G_j}=(1-\gamma\lambda_j/\lVert v_{G_j}\rVert_2)_+v_{G_j}\), with zero output when \(v_{G_j}=0\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard proximal formula for a sum of disjoint group norms
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Block soft thresholding for disjoint Euclidean group penalties.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G_1,\ldots,G_m\) partition the coordinates and let \(r(x)=\sum_{j=1}^m\lambda_j\lVert x_{G_j}\rVert_2\), where \(\lambda_j\ge0\). For \(\gamma>0\), the proximal map is evaluated independently on each group:
\[
\bigl(\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma r}(v)\bigr)_{G_j}
=\left(1-\frac{\gamma\lambda_j}{\lVert v_{G_j}\rVert_2}\right)_+v_{G_j}.
\]
The right-hand side is defined as zero when \(v_{G_j}=0\). A group is removed when \(\lVert v_{G_j}\rVert_2\le\gamma\lambda_j\); otherwise its direction is preserved and its norm is reduced by \(\gamma\lambda_j\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For disjoint group-norm penalties, each group is either set to zero or radially shrunk while preserving its direction.
knowledge_statements.title: Group Thresholding Interfaces

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The disjoint-group thresholding formula is correctly delimited and scoped, but it lacks an inspectable authoritative citation.

children.title: Thresholding Tie Regimes
children.top_down_role: Boundary cases involving zero blocks, equal magnitudes, or nonunique active structures.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Equal-Magnitude Ties in Hard Support Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonunique active supports in Euclidean projection onto a cardinality set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(1\le k<n\) and \(C_k=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:\lVert x\rVert_0\le k\}\). Euclidean projections of \(v\) onto \(C_k\) retain coordinates on a set of at most \(k\) largest magnitudes. If \(|v|_{[k]}>|v|_{[k+1]}\), the projection is unique. If \(|v|_{[k]}=|v|_{[k+1]}>0\), distinct selections among coordinates tied across the cutoff give distinct projections.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hard top-k selection is unique under a strict cutoff gap and set-valued when equal nonzero magnitudes straddle the cutoff.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: |v|_{[k]}>|v|_{[k+1]}\Rightarrow P_{C_k}(v)\text{ is unique};\quad |v|_{[k]}=|v|_{[k+1]}>0\Rightarrow P_{C_k}(v)\text{ is nonunique}.

notation.meaning: set of vectors with at most k nonzero coordinates

review_flags: tie convention is not part of the projection set
knowledge_statements.title: Equal-Magnitude Ties in Hard Support Selection

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Soft-Threshold Equality Is Unique but Nondifferentiable
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary behavior of the convex scalar soft-threshold map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\tau>0\), let \(S_\tau(v)=\operatorname{sign}(v)(|v|-\tau)_+\). Then \(S_\tau(\tau)=S_\tau(-\tau)=0\), so the proximal output remains unique at equality, but \(S_\tau\) is not differentiable at either \(v=\tau\) or \(v=-\tau\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Soft thresholding remains single-valued at equality but has a kink at each threshold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S_\tau(\pm\tau)=0\text{ uniquely, and }S_\tau\text{ is nondifferentiable at }\pm\tau.
knowledge_statements.title: Soft-Threshold Equality Is Unique but Nondifferentiable

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Group-Threshold Equality Is Unique but Nondifferentiable
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Activation boundary of Euclidean block soft thresholding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\tau>0\), define \(T_\tau(v)=(1-\tau/\lVert v\rVert_2)_+v\), with \(T_\tau(0)=0\). If \(\lVert v\rVert_2=\tau\), then \(T_\tau(v)=0\) uniquely. Nevertheless, \(T_\tau\) is not Fréchet differentiable at such \(v\), because inward radial perturbations remain on the zero branch while outward radial perturbations enter the active branch.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a group threshold, block shrinkage has a unique zero output but changes branch and is not differentiable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T_\tau(v)=0\text{ uniquely, but }T_\tau\text{ is not Fréchet differentiable at }v.
review_flags: boundary statement for convex group shrinkage
knowledge_statements.title: Group-Threshold Equality Is Unique but Nondifferentiable

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At \(|v|=\sqrt{2\gamma\lambda}\), \(\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma r}(v)=\{0,v\}\), so any single-valued hard-threshold interface requires a tie rule.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: explicit comparison of the zero and nonzero hard-threshold candidates
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Set-valued tie boundary for nonconvex hard thresholding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the scalar counting penalty \(r(x)=\lambda\mathbf{1}_{\{x\ne0\}}\), with \(\lambda>0\), the proximal minimizers at stepsize \(\gamma>0\) satisfy
\[
\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma r}(v)=
\begin{cases}
\{0\},&|v|<\sqrt{2\gamma\lambda},\\
\{0,v\},&|v|=\sqrt{2\gamma\lambda},\\
\{v\},&|v|>\sqrt{2\gamma\lambda}.
\end{cases}
\]
Thus hard thresholding is set-valued at exact equality. An implementation returning one point must specify a deterministic tie convention, such as preferring zero or preserving the input; that convention is algorithmic and is not part of the proximal argmin set itself.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hard thresholding has two minimizers exactly at its threshold, so a single-valued implementation must explicitly choose a tie convention.
knowledge_statements.title: Thresholding Tie Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The nonconvex tie regime and failure-boundary kind fit the terminal container, but the set-valued formula has no supporting source with a locator.

children.title: Spectral Proximal Evaluation
children.top_down_role: Reduction of matrix proximal problems to eigenvalue or singular-value operations.

knowledge_statements.title: Spectral Proximal Evaluation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Singular-value reduction for convex unitarily invariant functions on real matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(m,n\in\mathbb N\), let \(q=\min\{m,n\}\), and let \(\phi:\mathbb R^q\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, convex, and absolutely symmetric. Define \(F:\mathbb R^{m\times n}\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) by \(F(X)=\phi(\sigma(X))\), where \(\sigma(X)\in\mathbb R_+^q\) is the singular-value vector. If \(Y=U\operatorname{Diag}(s)V^{\mathsf T}\) is a singular-value decomposition with \(s=\sigma(Y)\), then for every \(\gamma>0\),
\[
\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma F}(Y)
=U\operatorname{Diag}\bigl(\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma\phi}(s)\bigr)V^{\mathsf T}.
\]
Hence spectral proximal evaluation reduces to a singular-value decomposition, a vector proximal evaluation, and reconstruction with the input singular vectors.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a convex unitarily invariant function on real matrices, its proximal map is obtained by applying the associated absolutely symmetric vector proximal map to the input singular values and retaining the input singular vectors.
assumptions_latex: The matrix dimensions satisfy \(m,n\in\mathbb N\) and \(q=\min\{m,n\}\).
The function \(\phi:\mathbb R^q\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, convex, and absolutely symmetric.
The matrix function is \(F(X)=\phi(\sigma(X))\) on \(\mathbb R^{m\times n}\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard proximal calculus for convex unitarily invariant functions

children.title: Orthogonal Transform Interfaces

assumptions_latex: The linear map \(Q:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) is orthogonal, so \(Q^{\mathsf T}Q=QQ^{\mathsf T}=I\).
The function \(g:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.

notation.meaning: transpose and inverse of the orthogonal transform

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: change-of-variables identity for orthogonal transforms
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact transform-domain proximal evaluation under an orthogonal change of coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Q:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) be orthogonal and let \(g:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex. For every \(\gamma>0\) and \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\),
\[
\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma(g\circ Q)}(x)
=Q^{\mathsf T}\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma g}(Qx).
\]
Thus the interface consists of a forward orthogonal transform, one proximal evaluation for \(g\) in transform coordinates, and the inverse transform. No metric correction is required because \(Q\) preserves Euclidean distances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an orthogonal transform, evaluate the transformed penalty's proximal map by transforming forward, applying the base proximal map, and transforming back.
knowledge_statements.title: Orthogonal Transform Interfaces

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The orthogonal change-of-coordinates formula is correctly stated and its representation kind fits, but no inspectable source is cited.

children.title: Tight-Frame Transform Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Evaluation structures induced by redundant transforms satisfying a tight-frame relation.

assumptions_latex: The bounded linear map \(L:H\to G\) satisfies \(LL^*=cI_G\) for some \(c>0\).
The function \(g:G\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard composition-proximal identity under a scaled coisometry
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed-form composition rule for a transform satisfying \(LL^*=cI\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H\) and \(G\) be real Hilbert spaces, let \(L:H\to G\) be bounded and satisfy the tight-frame relation \(LL^*=cI_G\) for some \(c>0\), and let \(g:G\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex. Then for every \(\gamma>0\) and \(x\in H\),
\[
\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma(g\circ L)}(x)
=x+\frac1cL^*\bigl(\operatorname{prox}_{c\gamma g}(Lx)-Lx\bigr).
\]
The evaluation uses one forward transform, one proximal query for \(g\), one adjoint transform, and a scaled correction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A tight-frame transform permits a closed proximal formula using one forward transform, one base proximal evaluation, and one adjoint correction.
knowledge_statements.title: Tight-Frame Transform Interfaces

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The scaled-coisometry proximal formula is appropriately scoped to the tight-frame interface, but it lacks a source with a specific theorem, proposition, section, or page locator.

children.title: Non-Tight Transform Boundary

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No scalar \(c>0\) makes the tight-frame shortcut equal \(\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma(g\circ L)}\) for every input.
