knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of the scalar tight-frame correction for unequal transform singular values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(L=\operatorname{Diag}(1,2)\) and \(g(z)=\lVert z\rVert_1\). Then \(g(Lx)=|x_1|+2|x_2|\), so
\[
\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma(g\circ L)}(x)
=\bigl(S_\gamma(x_1),S_{2\gamma}(x_2)\bigr).
\]
Because \(LL^{\mathsf T}=\operatorname{Diag}(1,4)\), no scalar \(c>0\) satisfies \(LL^{\mathsf T}=cI\). Correspondingly, the proposed tight-frame expression \(x+c^{-1}L^{\mathsf T}(\operatorname{prox}_{c\gamma g}(Lx)-Lx)\) would require \(c=1\) to reproduce the first-coordinate threshold and \(c=4\) to reproduce the second-coordinate threshold. It therefore cannot be valid for all inputs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A transform with unequal singular values needs different coordinate corrections, so no single tight-frame constant yields the usual closed proximal formula.
knowledge_statements.title: Non-Tight Transform Boundary

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The diagonal example correctly illustrates failure of a single scalar tight-frame correction and the failure-boundary kind fits, but no inspectable citation supports the claim.

children.title: General Linear-Transform Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Transformed regularizers requiring lifting, dualization, or splitting.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Primal-Dual Optimality Certificate for Transformed Proximal Evaluation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact certificate under the qualified dual interface.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Under the assumptions of the transformed-proximal dual interface, a pair \((x,y)\in X\times Y\) is primal-dual optimal if and only if
\[
y\in\partial g(Ax),\qquad x-v+\gamma A^*y=0.
\]
Equivalently, \(Ax\in\partial g^*(y)\) and \(x=v-\gamma A^*y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A transformed proximal point is certified by a dual subgradient whose adjoint balances the proximal displacement.
assumptions_latex: The assumptions and relative-interior qualification of the transformed-proximal dual interface hold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (x,y)\text{ is primal-dual optimal}\iff y\in\partial g(Ax)\text{ and }x-v+\gamma A^*y=0.
review_flags: certificate depends on the stated qualification
knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Dual Optimality Certificate for Transformed Proximal Evaluation

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dual Interface for a Linear-Transform Proximal Problem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Qualified Fenchel dual of general transformed-component proximal evaluation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X,Y\) be finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces, let \(A:X\to Y\) be linear, let \(g:Y\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, closed, and convex, and suppose \(\operatorname{ran}A\cap\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}g)\ne\varnothing\). For \(\gamma>0\),
\[
\min_x\left\{g(Ax)+\frac{1}{2\gamma}\lVert x-v\rVert^2\right\}
=
\max_y\left\{\langle Av,y\rangle-g^*(y)-\frac{\gamma}{2}\lVert A^*y\rVert^2\right\}.
\]
The dual maximum is attained, and every primal-dual solution satisfies \(x=v-\gamma A^*y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under a relative-interior qualification, a transformed proximal problem has an attained quadratic Fenchel dual and an adjoint primal-recovery formula.
assumptions_latex: \(X,Y\) are finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces and \(A:X\to Y\) is linear.
knowledge_statements.title: Dual Interface for a Linear-Transform Proximal Problem
General Linear-Transform Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lifted representation of a proximal evaluation for a convex function composed with a general linear map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) and \(Y\) be finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces, let \(A:X\to Y\) be linear, and let \(g:Y\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, closed, and convex. For \(\gamma>0\), evaluation of the transformed-component proximal map is the convex program
\[\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma(g\circ A)}(v)=\underset{x\in X}{\operatorname{argmin}}\left\{g(Ax)+\frac{1}{2\gamma}\lVert x-v\rVert^2\right\}.\]
Equivalently, it admits the lifted interface
\[\underset{x\in X,\,z\in Y}{\operatorname{minimize}}\quad g(z)+\frac{1}{2\gamma}\lVert x-v\rVert^2\quad\text{subject to}\quad z=Ax.\]
Thus a general linear transform normally requires an inner solve, dualization, or operator splitting rather than a primitive call to \(\operatorname{prox}_{g}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The proximal map of a regularizer after a general linear transformation is a strongly convex constrained problem obtained by introducing a variable equal to the transformed argument.
assumptions_latex: \(X,Y\) are finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces and \(A:X\to Y\) is linear.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma(g\circ A)}(v)\) equals the \(x\)-component of the stated lifted problem.

notation.meaning: Proximal map of the function h with parameter gamma.
Lifted variable constrained to equal Ax.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard lifting identity obtained by substituting z=Ax in the proximal minimization
A directly relevant proximal-splitting source and exact locator are required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The lifting identity is mathematically standard and fits the representation container, but no inspectable source supports either the identity or the broader claim about inner solves, dualization, or splitting.

children.title: Nonlinear Composition Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Composition structures governed by specialized calculus or inner models.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar example showing that convexity of both functions does not alone preserve convexity under composition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F(x)=x^2\) and \(g(t)=-t\). Both \(F\) and \(g\) are convex, but \(g\) is decreasing and \((g\circ F)(x)=-x^2\) is not convex. Thus convex inner components and a convex outer function are insufficient without compatible monotonicity or another composition rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two convex functions can have a nonconvex composition when the outer function has the wrong monotonicity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F\text{ and }g\text{ are convex, but }g\circ F\text{ is not convex}.
knowledge_statements.title: Failure Without Outer Monotonicity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order oracle interface for differentiable inner and outer mappings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) be differentiable at \(x\), and let \(g:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R\) be differentiable at \(F(x)\). Then \[\nabla(g\circ F)(x)=DF(x)^*\nabla g(F(x)).\] Value-and-gradient evaluation therefore requires \(F(x)\), the outer value and gradient at \(F(x)\), and an adjoint-Jacobian product; the full Jacobian need not be formed when that product is directly available.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A smooth nonlinear composition is evaluated using the inner value, outer gradient, and one adjoint-Jacobian product.

notation.meaning: adjoint-Jacobian product at x applied to v

knowledge_statements.title: Smooth Nonlinear Composition Evaluation Interface

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convexity rule for a convex outer function applied to convex scalar inner components.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be convex, let \(F=(F_1,\ldots,F_m):C\to\mathbb R^m\) have convex components, and let \(g:\mathbb R^m\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be convex and coordinatewise nondecreasing on a convex upper set containing \(F(C)+\mathbb R_+^m\). If the composition is well defined and proper, then \(g\circ F\) is convex on \(C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex coordinatewise-nondecreasing outer function preserves convexity when applied to convex inner components.
assumptions_latex: \(g\) is convex and coordinatewise nondecreasing on a convex upper set containing \(F(C)+\mathbb R_+^m\).
knowledge_statements.title: Coordinatewise-Monotone Nonlinear Composition Rule

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Qualified vector-valued nonlinear subgradient interface under globally finite convex data.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let each \(F_i:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be finite and convex, and let \(g:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R\) be finite, convex, and coordinatewise nondecreasing. For \(F=(F_1,\ldots,F_m)\), \[\partial(g\circ F)(x)=\bigcup_{y\in\partial g(F(x))}\left\{\sum_{i=1}^m y_i u_i:\ u_i\in\partial F_i(x)\right\}.\] Every such \(y\) is componentwise nonnegative. Thus nonsmooth evaluation requires an outer subgradient and compatible inner subgradients, while the finiteness assumptions avoid extended-domain chain-rule qualifications.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For finite convex monotone compositions, composite subgradients are nonnegative outer-weighted sums of inner subgradients.
assumptions_latex: Each \(F_i:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) is finite and convex.
\(g:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R\) is finite, convex, and coordinatewise nondecreasing.

notation.meaning: outer subgradient at the inner value
subgradient of the ith inner component

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Valued Nonsmooth Composition Subdifferential
Nonlinear Composition Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convexity and first-order evaluation interface for a scalar convex outer function composed with a differentiable inner map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) be a finite-dimensional Hilbert space, let \(F:X\to\mathbb{R}^m\) be differentiable, and let \(g:\mathbb{R}^m\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and convex. If every component \(F_i\) is convex and \(g\) is coordinatewise nondecreasing on \(F(X)\), then \(g\circ F\) is convex. At any \(x\) where the convex-composition chain rule is valid, its subdifferential is
\[\partial(g\circ F)(x)=DF(x)^*\partial g(F(x)).\]
Consequently, a first-order composition interface must provide \(F(x)\), the adjoint-Jacobian action \(DF(x)^*y\), and an outer subgradient \(y\in\partial g(F(x))\); absent these conditions, convexity or the equality may fail.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonlinear convex composition can be evaluated through inner values, adjoint-Jacobian products, and outer subgradients when monotonicity, componentwise convexity, and chain-rule qualification hold.
assumptions_latex: \(F_i\) is convex for each component and \(F\) is differentiable.
\(g\) is proper, convex, and coordinatewise nondecreasing on \(F(X)\).
A standard convex-composition chain-rule qualification holds at \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g\circ F\) is convex and \(\partial(g\circ F)(x)=DF(x)^*\partial g(F(x))\).

notation.meaning: Adjoint of the derivative of F at x.

source_refs.locator: 1.1 The World of Nonlinear Optimization p. 3

review_flags: The exact chain-rule qualification and formula require confirmation against a dedicated convex-analysis locator.

source_witnesses.locator: 1.1 The World of Nonlinear Optimization p. 3

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited introductory page is not a reliable locator for this nonlinear convex-composition chain rule. The exact monotonicity domain and chain-rule qualification must be stated from a dedicated convex-analysis source before the displayed equality is reliable.

children.title: Evaluation Accuracy-Regime Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: Distinctions among direct, decomposed, inner-solved, and approximate component evaluation.

children.title: Direct Primitive Evaluation Family
children.top_down_role: Components reducible to standard scalar, block, projection, or spectral primitives.

children.title: Closed-Form Scalar Evaluation
children.top_down_role: Direct evaluation through standard scalar primitives.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical closed-form scalar proximal evaluation for the absolute-value penalty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(h(t)=\alpha|t|\), \(\alpha\ge0\), and \(\gamma>0\),
\[
\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma h}(v)=\operatorname{sign}(v)\max\{|v|-\gamma\alpha,0\}.
\]
Consequently, for \(H(x)=\alpha\|x\|_1\), this formula is applied independently to every coordinate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The proximal map of a scaled absolute value is soft thresholding, and the scaled l1 proximal map applies it coordinatewise.
knowledge_statements.title: Soft-Threshold Scalar Primitive

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical closed-form scalar proximal evaluation for a convex quadratic penalty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For
\[
h(s)=\frac a2s^2+bs+c,
\qquad a\ge0,
\]
and \(\gamma>0\),
\[
\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma h}(v)=\frac{v-\gamma b}{1+\gamma a}.
\]
A coordinate-separable sum of such scalar quadratics is therefore evaluated by independent affine rescalings.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A scalar convex quadratic has an affine closed-form proximal map.
knowledge_statements.title: Affine-Quadratic Scalar Primitive
Closed-Form Scalar Evaluation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinatewise reduction when a separable scalar proximal primitive has an explicit formula.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(h:\mathbb{R}\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, closed, and convex, and define \(H(x)=\sum_{i=1}^n h(x_i)\). For \(\gamma>0\), the proximal evaluation separates as
\[\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma H}(v)_i=\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma h}(v_i),\qquad i=1,\ldots,n.\]
If the scalar minimizer
\[p_\gamma(t)=\underset{s\in\mathbb{R}}{\operatorname{argmin}}\left\{h(s)+\frac{(s-t)^2}{2\gamma}\right\}\]
has an explicit formula, then \(\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma H}(v)=(p_\gamma(v_1),\ldots,p_\gamma(v_n))\) is a direct closed-form scalar evaluation, requiring no coupled optimization subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A separable regularizer with a closed-form scalar proximal map is evaluated by applying that scalar formula independently to every coordinate.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: separability of the proximal minimization yields independent scalar problems
A directly relevant proximal-operator source and locator are required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The coordinatewise proximal decomposition is standard and the representation kind fits the leaf, but the record supplies no source with a specific locator.

children.title: Direct Block Evaluation
children.top_down_role: Direct evaluation through standard vector or grouped-block primitives.

knowledge_statements.title: Direct Block Evaluation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Blockwise decomposition of a proximal primitive over an orthogonal product space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X=X_1\times\cdots\times X_m\) be a finite-dimensional Hilbert product space with \(\lVert x\rVert^2=\sum_{j=1}^m\lVert x_j\rVert_j^2\). Let \(H(x)=\sum_{j=1}^m h_j(x_j)\), where every \(h_j:X_j\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, closed, and convex. Then for every \(\gamma>0\) and \(v\in X\),
\[\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma H}(v)=\bigl(\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma h_1}(v_1),\ldots,\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma h_m}(v_m)\bigr).\]
Hence the component oracle may evaluate each block independently, and parallel block evaluation produces the exact proximal point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an additively block-separable regularizer and product norm, the exact proximal map is the tuple of independent block proximal maps.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) has the stated orthogonal product norm.
Each \(h_j\) is proper, closed, and convex.

notation.meaning: Regularizer acting only on block j.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: additive separability and the product norm separate the proximal objective by blocks
A directly relevant proximal-operator source and locator are required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The block-separable proximal property is mathematically precise and appropriately classified as a property, but it lacks an inspectable source and locator.

children.title: Direct Projection Evaluation
children.top_down_role: Direct evaluation reducible to projection onto a tractable convex set.

knowledge_statements.title: Direct Projection Evaluation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projection as the proximal primitive of a closed convex set indicator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\) be a nonempty closed convex subset of a finite-dimensional Hilbert space \(X\), and let \(\delta_C(x)=0\) for \(x\in C\) and \(\delta_C(x)=+\infty\) otherwise. For every \(v\in X\) and \(\gamma>0\),
\[\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma\delta_C}(v)=\underset{x\in C}{\operatorname{argmin}}\;\frac12\lVert x-v\rVert^2=P_C(v).\]
The minimizer exists and is unique. Therefore, whenever \(P_C\) is available as a primitive, the indicator component is evaluated directly by one projection call, independently of \(\gamma\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The proximal map of a closed convex set’s indicator is its unique metric projection, so an indicator component can use a projection oracle directly.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq X\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma\delta_C}(v)=P_C(v)\), with a unique value for every \(v\in X\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the indicator restricts the proximal minimization exactly to C
A directly relevant convex-analysis source and exact locator are required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The projection representation is standard and correctly scoped, including existence and uniqueness, but no authoritative source with an exact locator is supplied.

children.title: Direct Spectral Evaluation
children.top_down_role: Direct evaluation through eigenvalue or singular-value primitives.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct proximal evaluation of a rectangular unitarily invariant convex function through singular values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(q=\min\{m,n\}\), let \(f:\mathbb{R}^q\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, closed, convex, and absolutely symmetric, and define \(F(X)=f(\sigma(X))\) on \(\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\). If \(V=U\operatorname{Diag}(\sigma(V))W^{\mathsf T}\) is a thin singular-value decomposition, then for every \(\gamma>0\),
\[\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma F}(V)=U\operatorname{Diag}\!\left(\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma f}(\sigma(V))\right)W^{\mathsf T}.\]
The resulting matrix is independent of the choice of singular-vector bases within repeated-singular-value subspaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rectangular unitarily invariant proximal problem reduces to the vector proximal problem on singular values, followed by reconstruction in the same singular subspaces.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, closed, convex, and absolutely symmetric.
\(F(X)=f(\sigma(X))\), and the proximal matrix geometry is Frobenius.

notation.meaning: Vector of singular values of X in nonincreasing order.
Left and right singular-vector matrices in a thin SVD of V.
Minimum of the two matrix dimensions.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: proximal calculus for unitarily invariant convex matrix functions
knowledge_statements.title: Singular-Value Proximal Reduction
Direct Spectral Evaluation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Eigenvalue reduction for the proximal map of an orthogonally invariant convex matrix function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, closed, convex, and invariant under coordinate permutations, and define \(F(X)=f(\lambda(X))\) on real symmetric matrices. If \(V=Q\operatorname{Diag}(\lambda(V))Q^{\mathsf T}\), then for every \(\gamma>0\),
\[\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma F}(V)=Q\operatorname{Diag}\!\left(\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma f}(\lambda(V))\right)Q^{\mathsf T}.\]
Thus direct spectral evaluation consists of an eigendecomposition, evaluation of the vector proximal primitive on the eigenvalues, and reconstruction using the same eigenvectors. Repeated eigenvalues do not affect the resulting matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The proximal map of an orthogonally invariant convex matrix function is obtained by applying the corresponding vector proximal map to the eigenvalues.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, closed, convex, and permutation invariant.

notation.meaning: Vector of eigenvalues of the symmetric matrix X in a fixed order.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard spectral proximal calculus for orthogonally invariant convex functions
A matrix-analysis source with an exact spectral proximal theorem locator is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The spectral proximal formula fits the representation container, but this specialized matrix-calculus claim requires an exact theorem or section locator.

children.title: Inner-Optimization Evaluation
children.top_down_role: Components whose oracle requires a subsidiary optimization problem.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact value evaluation need not provide an exact feasible optimizer when the subsidiary infimum is unattained.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Z=(0,\infty)\) and define \(h=\inf_{z\in Z}z\). Then \(h=0\), but every feasible \(z\) has upper value \(U=z>0\). Thus the finite exact value can be approached arbitrarily closely, while no feasible inner point attains it. An interface requiring an exact optimizing witness therefore needs an attainment hypothesis in addition to knowledge of the infimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite inner infimum may be unattained, so arbitrarily accurate feasible evaluations need not yield an exact optimizing witness.

notation.meaning: Open feasible set of the subsidiary problem.
Objective value of a returned feasible point.

knowledge_statements.title: Unattained Inner Infimum Boundary

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Primal–Dual Certificate for Convex Inner Evaluation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Computable lower and upper bounds for a convex subsidiary problem obtained from Lagrange duality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix \(x\) and consider
\[h(x)=\inf_z\{\Phi(x,z):g_i(x,z)\le0\ (i=1,\ldots,p),\ Az=b\}.\]
For fixed \(x\), assume the objective and inequality functions are proper closed convex in \(z\), the equality constraint is affine, the value is finite, and there is a point in the relative interior of their common domain satisfying \(Az=b\) and every nonaffine inequality strictly. Define
\[d_x(\lambda,\nu)=\inf_z\left(\Phi(x,z)+\sum_{i=1}^p\lambda_i g_i(x,z)+\langle\nu,Az-b\rangle\right).\]
For every primal-feasible \(\widehat z\), every \(\lambda\ge0\), and every \(\nu\),
\[d_x(\lambda,\nu)\le h(x)\le U:=\Phi(x,\widehat z),\qquad 0\le U-h(x)\le U-d_x(\lambda,
u).\]
Under the stated Slater qualification, \(h(x)=\sup_{\lambda\ge0,\nu}d_x(\lambda,
u)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A primal-feasible point and dual multipliers give a certified evaluation interval; under a Slater qualification, the best dual lower bound equals the inner value.
assumptions_latex: For fixed \(x\), \(\Phi(x,\cdot)\) and \(g_i(x,\cdot)\) are proper closed convex functions, and \(Az=b\) is affine.
The inner value is finite and the stated relative-interior Slater condition holds.
\(\widehat z\) is primal feasible, \(\lambda\ge0\), and \(U=\Phi(x,\widehat z)<+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\(d_x(\lambda,\nu)\le h(x)\le U\), the gap \(U-d_x(\lambda,
u)\) bounds evaluation error, and the optimal dual bound equals \(h(x)\).

notation.meaning: Lagrange dual function for the inner problem at x.
Upper value supplied by a primal-feasible inner point.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: weak duality gives the interval and finite-dimensional Slater regularity gives zero duality gap
knowledge_statements.title: Primal–Dual Certificate for Convex Inner Evaluation
Inner-Optimization Evaluation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Component evaluation represented as a parameterized subsidiary convex optimization problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) and \(Z\) be finite-dimensional spaces, let \(Z(x)\subseteq Z\) be nonempty, and define the component value function
\[h(x)=\inf_{z\in Z(x)}\Phi(x,z).\]
An inner-optimization evaluation at \(x\) returns a feasible \(\widehat z\in Z(x)\), the upper value \(U=\Phi(x,\widehat z)\), and, when certification is required, a lower bound \(L\le h(x)\). The reported value \(\widehat h=U\) then satisfies
\[0\le \widehat h-h(x)\le U-L.\]
Exact evaluation occurs when an optimizer is attained and \(U=L\); otherwise the computable gap \(U-L\) controls the evaluation accuracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inner-optimization oracle evaluates a value function by solving a parameterized subproblem and can bound its error using feasible upper and valid lower values.
assumptions_latex: \(Z(x)\) is nonempty at the queried point.
\(L\) is a valid lower bound on \(h(x)\).

notation.meaning: Feasible set of the inner problem at x.
Certified upper and lower values for the inner optimum.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: weak duality or any valid lower bound combined with a feasible upper value yields the displayed gap certificate
A source treating certified evaluation of parameterized value functions is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The upper-minus-lower-bound certificate is valid as stated, but the scope describes a convex subsidiary problem without imposing convexity assumptions. A source is also required for the proposed evaluation interface.

children.title: Certified Inexact Evaluation
children.top_down_role: Approximate component evaluation accompanied by computable accuracy information.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic enclosure contract for approximate scalar component values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:D\to\mathbb R\). A certified inexact value evaluation at \(x\in D\) returns validated bounds \(\ell\le f(x)\le u\) and may report an estimate \(\widehat f\in[\ell,u]\). Then
\[
|\widehat f-f(x)|\le\max\{\widehat f-\ell,u-\widehat f\}.
\]
For the midpoint \(\widehat f=(\ell+u)/2\), the error is at most \((u-\ell)/2\). A single validated lower or upper bound certifies only the corresponding one-sided error.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A certified approximate value comes with a validated interval containing the exact value, from which an absolute-error bound is computable.
assumptions_latex: \(\ell\le f(x)\le u\) is a validated enclosure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The enclosure provides a computable absolute-error bound for \(\widehat f\).

notation.meaning: Validated enclosure of the exact value.

knowledge_statements.title: Certified Inexact Value Evaluation

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Unverified Termination Is Not an Accuracy Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between approximate output and certified inexact evaluation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(v^*=\inf_z Q(z)\) be finite. A feasible trial point \(\widehat z\) gives only \(v^*\le Q(\widehat z)\). Without a validated lower bound \(L\le v^*\), a residual-to-error theorem whose assumptions have been verified, or another rigorous enclosure, solver termination, small successive-iterate changes, or a nominally small residual do not by themselves imply a prescribed bound on \(Q(\widehat z)-v^*\). Such output is approximate but not certified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Termination or a heuristic residual is not an accuracy certificate unless validated bounds or a theorem convert it into a rigorous error estimate.
assumptions_latex: \(\widehat z\) is feasible for the inner problem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Feasibility alone gives \(v^*\le Q(\widehat z)\) but no nontrivial certified upper bound on \(Q(\widehat z)-v^*\).
knowledge_statements.title: Unverified Termination Is Not an Accuracy Certificate
Certified Inexact Evaluation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal-lower-bound certificate for an approximate proximal component evaluation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(h:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, closed, and convex, let \(v\in X\), and let \(\gamma>0\). Define
\[Q_v(x)=h(x)+\frac{1}{2\gamma}\lVert x-v\rVert^2.\]
A certified inexact proximal evaluation consists of \(\widehat x\in\operatorname{dom}h\) and a computable lower bound \(L\le\inf_x Q_v(x)\). If
\[Q_v(\widehat x)-L\le\varepsilon,\]
then \(Q_v(\widehat x)-\inf_xQ_v(x)\le\varepsilon\). Moreover, strong convexity gives
\[\lVert\widehat x-\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma h}(v)\rVert\le\sqrt{2\gamma\varepsilon}.\]
Thus the pair \((\widehat x,L)\) provides verifiable objective and pointwise accuracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible approximate proximal point and a valid lower bound certify objective error at most epsilon and distance at most the square root of twice gamma epsilon.

notation.meaning: Computable lower bound on the proximal objective optimum.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the objective-gap certificate and strong-convexity growth inequality imply the bounds
A directly relevant source for certified inexact proximal evaluation is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The objective-gap and distance bounds are standard consequences of strong convexity and the certificate kind fits the leaf, but X is not declared to be a Hilbert space and no source with an exact locator is supplied.

children.title: Composite Optimality-Residual Certificate System
children.top_down_role: Exact optimality representations and computable certificate families attached to composite structure.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Optimality conditions and proximal-gradient composite model
Subgradients, optimality conditions, and Fenchel duality

children.title: Exact Composite Optimality
children.top_down_role: Equivalent structural interfaces for exact optimality.

children.title: Composite Fermat-Rule Family
children.top_down_role: Optimality through aggregate subdifferential structure.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A composite minimizer with no cancelling pair of summand subgradients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In \(\mathbb{R}^2\), let \(C=\{(x,y):y\geq x^2\}\), \(D=\{(x,y):y\leq-x^2\}\), \(f(x,y)=x+\delta_C(x,y)\), and \(g=\delta_D\). Then \(C\cap D=\{(0,0)\}\), so \((0,0)\) minimizes \(f+g\) and \(0\in\partial(f+g)(0,0)\). However, \[\partial f(0,0)+\partial g(0,0)=\{(1,t):t\in\mathbb{R}\},\] which does not contain zero. The relative-interior qualification fails.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without a sum-rule qualification, a composite minimizer need not admit cancelling summand subgradients.
knowledge_statements.title: Failure of Unqualified Summand Decomposition

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Aggregate and Decomposed Composite Fermat Rules
knowledge_statements.scope_note: General convex composite optimality and its qualified summand decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f,g\in\Gamma_0(X)\) on a finite-dimensional Hilbert space and let \(x^\star\in\operatorname{dom}f\cap\operatorname{dom}g\). Then \[x^\star\in\operatorname*{argmin}(f+g)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad0\in\partial(f+g)(x^\star).\] If additionally \(\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}f)\cap\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}g)\neq\varnothing\), this is equivalent to the existence of \(u\in\partial f(x^\star)\) and \(v\in\partial g(x^\star)\) with \(u+v=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Composite optimality is always zero aggregate subgradient; decomposition into cancelling summand subgradients requires an exact sum rule.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Separated Stationarity Can Fail Without a Sum Rule
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure boundary for decomposing constrained Fermat optimality into an objective subgradient and a feasible-set normal.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=\{(u,v)\in\mathbb R^2:v\ge u^2\}\), \(C=\mathbb R\times\{0\}\), \(F(u,v)=-u+\delta_D(u,v)\), and \(x^\star=(0,0)\). Then \(C\cap\operatorname{dom}F=\{x^\star\}\), but \(0\notin\partial F(x^\star)+N_C(x^\star)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Separated Stationarity Can Fail Without a Sum Rule
Normal-Cone Optimality Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact constrained convex optimality expressed through the normal cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\) be a nonempty closed convex subset of a finite-dimensional Hilbert space \(X\), and let \(F:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, closed, and convex. Suppose the subdifferential sum rule applies to \(F+\delta_C\) at \(x^\star\in C\cap\operatorname{dom}F\). Then
\[x^\star\in\underset{x\in C}{\operatorname{argmin}}F(x)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad0\in\partial F(x^\star)+N_C(x^\star),\]
where
\[N_C(x^\star)=\{n\in X:\langle n,y-x^\star\rangle\le0\ \text{for all }y\in C\}.\]
Thus optimality is certified by \(s+n=0\) with \(s\in\partial F(x^\star)\) and \(n\in N_C(x^\star)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Constrained convex optimality is equivalent, under the subdifferential sum rule, to balancing an objective subgradient with a normal vector to the feasible set.
assumptions_latex: The subdifferential sum rule for \(F+\delta_C\) holds at \(x^\star\).

notation.meaning: Convex-analytic normal cone to C at x.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: apply the convex Fermat rule and a qualified subdifferential sum rule to F plus the indicator of C
A convex-analysis source with the exact normal-cone optimality theorem and qualification is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The qualified normal-cone optimality equivalence is correct and fits a theorem container, but it lacks a convex-analysis source specifying the sum-rule qualification and result.

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible point minimizes a convex function exactly when every feasible chord direction has nonnegative one-sided directional derivative.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, let \(F\) be proper, closed, and convex, and suppose the sum rule for \(F+\delta_C\) holds at \(x^\star\in C\cap\operatorname{dom}F\). F\text{ is proper, closed, and convex}

knowledge_statements.title: Selected-Subgradient Variational Inequality
Variational-Inequality Optimality Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Differentiable constrained convex optimality expressed as a variational inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\) be a nonempty closed convex subset of a finite-dimensional Hilbert space \(X\), and let \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\) be convex and differentiable on an open set containing \(C\). For \(x^\star\in C\),
\[x^\star\in\underset{x\in C}{\operatorname{argmin}}f(x)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\langle\nabla f(x^\star),x-x^\star\rangle\ge0\quad\text{for every }x\in C.\]
The right-hand condition is the variational-inequality interface for constrained minimization. It supplies an exact certificate using only feasibility, the gradient at the candidate, and inner products against feasible directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible point minimizes a differentiable convex function over a convex set exactly when its gradient has nonnegative inner product with every feasible displacement.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is convex and differentiable on an open neighborhood of \(C\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Qualified equivalence among constrained minimization, a normal-cone inclusion, and a subgradient variational inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subset X\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, let \(h\in\Gamma_0(X)\), and suppose \(\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}h)\cap\operatorname{ri}C\neq\varnothing\). For \(x^\star\in C\cap\operatorname{dom}h\), the following are equivalent: \[(i)\ x^\star\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}h(x);\qquad (ii)\ \exists s^\star\in\partial h(x^\star):0\in s^\star+N_C(x^\star);\] \[(iii)\ \exists s^\star\in\partial h(x^\star):\langle s^\star,x-x^\star\rangle\geq0\quad\forall x\in C.\] The equivalence of (ii) and (iii) is the defining normal-cone inequality; the qualification is needed for necessity of the separated subgradient-normal witness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the convex sum-rule qualification, constrained minimization, a subgradient-normal inclusion, and a subgradient variational inequality are equivalent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^\star\in\arg\min_C h\iff\exists s^\star\in\partial h(x^\star):-s^\star\in N_C(x^\star)\iff\langle s^\star,x-x^\star\rangle\geq0\ \forall x\in C.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonsmooth Constraint-Interface Correspondence
Constraint-Interface Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence between normal-cone inclusion and variational-inequality forms of smooth constrained convex optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\) be a nonempty closed convex subset of a finite-dimensional Hilbert space \(X\), let \(f\) be convex and differentiable on a neighborhood of \(C\), and let \(x^\star\in C\). By the definition of the convex normal cone,
\[-\nabla f(x^\star)\in N_C(x^\star)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\langle\nabla f(x^\star),x-x^\star\rangle\ge0\quad\text{for every }x\in C.\]
Equivalently,
\[0\in\nabla f(x^\star)+N_C(x^\star)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\operatorname{VI}(\nabla f,C)\text{ holds at }x^\star.\]
Both interfaces therefore certify the same constrained minimizer, while exposing different oracle operations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The normal-cone inclusion and gradient variational inequality are equivalent descriptions of the same smooth convex constrained optimality condition.

notation.meaning: Normal cone to C at the candidate.
Variational inequality induced by the gradient on C.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: substituting the normal-cone definition gives the variational inequality algebraically
A convex-analysis source explicitly linking the two constrained optimality interfaces is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The equivalence follows from the stated normal-cone convention, but it is a correspondence or representation rather than a duality. It also lacks an authoritative source with an exact locator.

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Point Optimality Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Euclidean proximal fixed-point representation for an unconstrained convex composite objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be convex and differentiable, let \(g:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, closed, and convex, and set \(F=f+g\). For \(\gamma>0\), define \(T_\gamma(x)=\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma g}(x-\gamma\nabla f(x))\). Then, for every \(x^\star\in\operatorname{dom}g\), \[x^\star\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}F(x)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x^\star=T_\gamma(x^\star).\] This equivalence holds for every positive \(\gamma\); no Lipschitz-gradient assumption is required for the optimality representation itself.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A point minimizes the convex composite objective exactly when it is a fixed point of every positive-step proximal-gradient operator.
assumptions_latex: f\text{ is convex and differentiable on }\mathbb{R}^n

knowledge_statements.title: Saddle-Point Optimality Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex–concave saddle representation of a linearly composed convex objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) and \(h:\mathbb{R}^m\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, closed, convex functions, and let \(K:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) be linear. Define \(L(x,y)=f(x)+\langle Kx,y\rangle-h^*(y)\). A pair \((x^\star,y^\star)\) is a saddle point precisely when \[L(x^\star,y)\le L(x^\star,y^\star)\le L(x,y^\star)\quad\text{for all }(x,y)\in\operatorname{dom}f\times\operatorname{dom}h^*.\] Such a pair simultaneously attains the primal problem \(\min_x f(x)+h(Kx)\) and its Fenchel dual \(\max_y -f^*(-K^*y)-h^*(y)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A saddle pair satisfies the two-sided Lagrangian inequality and simultaneously solves the linearly composed primal problem and its Fenchel dual.
assumptions_latex: f,h\text{ are proper, closed, and convex}

knowledge_statements.title: KKT Optimality Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Subdifferential KKT system for a linearly composed convex objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(L(x,y)=f(x)+\langle Kx,y\rangle-h^*(y)\), the convex composite KKT interface associates \((x^\star,y^\star)\) with the coupled inclusions \[0\in\partial f(x^\star)+K^*y^\star,\qquad 0\in\partial h^*(y^\star)-Kx^\star.\] Equivalently, \(-K^*y^\star\in\partial f(x^\star)\) and \(Kx^\star\in\partial h^*(y^\star)\), the latter being equivalent to \(y^\star\in\partial h(Kx^\star)\). Any pair satisfying these inclusions is primal-dual optimal and has zero Fenchel duality gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Composite KKT optimality is expressed by two coupled subgradient inclusions linking the primal variable, dual variable, and linear map.
assumptions_latex: f,h\text{ are proper, closed, and convex}

knowledge_statements.title: Interface Equivalence Conditions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Qualification ensuring equivalence of primal optimality, KKT solvability, and saddle-point optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\) and \(h\) be proper, closed, convex functions on finite-dimensional spaces, let \(K\) be linear, and suppose \(K(\operatorname{ri}\operatorname{dom}f)\cap\operatorname{ri}\operatorname{dom}h\ne\varnothing\). If the primal minimum of \(f(x)+h(Kx)\) is attained, then a point \(x^\star\) is primal optimal if and only if there exists \(y^\star\) satisfying \[0\in\partial f(x^\star)+K^*y^\star,\qquad Kx^\star\in\partial h^*(y^\star).\] Moreover, this KKT system holds if and only if \((x^\star,y^\star)\) is a saddle point of \(L(x,y)=f(x)+\langle Kx,y\rangle-h^*(y)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under a relative-interior qualification and primal attainment, primal optimality, existence of a KKT multiplier, and saddle-point optimality are equivalent.
assumptions_latex: f,h\text{ are proper, closed, and convex on finite-dimensional spaces}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^\star\text{ is primal optimal}\iff\exists y^\star\text{ satisfying KKT}\iff(x^\star,y^\star)\text{ is a saddle point}

knowledge_statements.title: Subdifferential Residuals
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distance-to-subdifferential certificate for exact composite optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f,g:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, closed, convex functions satisfying \(\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}f)\cap\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}g)\ne\varnothing\). For \(x\in\operatorname{dom}f\cap\operatorname{dom}g\), define \[r_{\partial}(x)=\operatorname{dist}\bigl(0,\partial f(x)+\partial g(x)\bigr).\] The subdifferential sum rule gives \(\partial(f+g)(x)=\partial f(x)+\partial g(x)\), and therefore \[r_{\partial}(x)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad 0\in\partial(f+g)(x)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x\in\operatorname*{argmin}(f+g).\] Thus the zero residual is an exact, directly verifiable optimality certificate whenever the displayed subdifferentials are available.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The distance from zero to the summed subdifferentials vanishes exactly at composite minimizers, provided the convex subdifferential sum rule applies.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of uniform objective and distance guarantees from a small subdifferential residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(F_a(t)=a|t|\), \(a>0\), the unique minimizer is \(0\), while for every \(t\neq0\), \[\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial F_a(t))=a,\qquad F_a(t)-F_a(0)=a|t|.\] Thus an arbitrarily small fixed residual can coexist with arbitrarily large distance and objective gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A small subdifferential residual alone can coexist with arbitrarily large distance and objective error.
assumptions_latex: Only proper, closed, convex functions with attained minima are assumed.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distance and objective guarantees under strong convexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be proper, closed, and \(\mu\)-strongly convex with \(\mu>0\), and let \(x^\star\) be its unique minimizer. For \(r(x)=\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial F(x))\), \[\|x-x^\star\|\leq\frac{r(x)}{\mu},\qquad 0\leq F(x)-F(x^\star)\leq\frac{r(x)^2}{2\mu}.\] Under an exact sum rule, \(r(x)=\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x)+\partial g(x))\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong convexity converts a subdifferential residual into explicit distance and objective-gap guarantees.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is proper, closed, and \(\mu\)-strongly convex for \(\mu>0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Euclidean Composite Gradient Mapping
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard Euclidean proximal-gradient residual and its exact zero condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be convex and differentiable and let \(g\in\Gamma_0(\mathbb{R}^n)\). For \(\gamma>0\), define \[p_\gamma(x)=\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma g}(x-\gamma\nabla f(x)),\qquad G_\gamma(x)=\gamma^{-1}(x-p_\gamma(x)).\] The vector \(G_\gamma(x)\) is the Euclidean composite gradient mapping. Its norm is a residual, and \[G_\gamma(x)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad 0\in\nabla f(x)+\partial g(x)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x\in\operatorname*{argmin}(f+g).\] A Lipschitz-gradient condition may be imposed for descent or complexity estimates, but not for this zero-residual equivalence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The proximal-gradient displacement divided by the step size is zero exactly at minimizers of the convex composite objective.
assumptions_latex: f\text{ is convex and differentiable on }\mathbb{R}^n

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conversion of the gradient mapping into a true composite subgradient at the new point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(p=p_\gamma(x)\) and suppose \(
abla f\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz. Proximal optimality gives \[G_\gamma(x)-
abla f(x)\in\partial g(p).\] Therefore \[v_p:=G_\gamma(x)+
abla f(p)-
abla f(x)\in\partial(f+g)(p),\qquad \|v_p\|\leq(1+\gamma L)\|G_\gamma(x)\|.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A small Euclidean gradient mapping produces a controlled true composite subgradient at the proximal-gradient point.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: One-Step Composite Descent Bound and Sharp Stepsize Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Descent expressed directly through the Euclidean composite gradient mapping.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=f+g\), \(p=p_\gamma(x)\), and suppose \(\nabla f\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz. Then \[F(p)\leq F(x)-\gamma\left(1-\frac{L\gamma}{2}\right)\|G_\gamma(x)\|^2.\] Hence \(0<\gamma\leq1/L\) gives \(F(p)\leq F(x)-\frac\gamma2\|G_\gamma(x)\|^2\). The positive-descent boundary cannot be extended beyond \(2/L\) uniformly: for \(g=0\) and \(f(t)=\frac L2t^2\), one has \(p=(1-\gamma L)t\), and \(F(p)>F(t)\) whenever \(\gamma L>2\) and \(t\neq0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A smoothness-compatible step makes the squared gradient-mapping norm certify one-step descent; steps beyond two over the smoothness constant can increase the objective.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Spectral Equivalence of Metric Residual Conventions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Comparison of metric-scaled residual, metric displacement, and Euclidean magnitude.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(mI\preceq H\preceq MI\), \(0<m\leq M\), and \(d=x-p_{\gamma,H}(x)\), then \[\|R_{\gamma,H}(x)\|_{H^{-1}}=\gamma^{-1}\|d\|_H\] and \[\frac{\sqrt m}{\gamma}\|d\|_2\leq\|R_{\gamma,H}(x)\|_{H^{-1}}\leq\frac{\sqrt M}{\gamma}\|d\|_2.\] Thus residual magnitudes from different metrics are not uniformly comparable without declared spectral bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eigenvalue bounds quantify how the dual-metric residual compares with the proximal displacement.

notation.meaning: lower and upper spectral bounds for the metric

knowledge_statements.title: Spectral Equivalence of Metric Residual Conventions

knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order representation of the scaled metric residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(p=p_{\gamma,H}(x)\). Its optimality condition is \[0\in\partial g(p)+
abla f(x)+\gamma^{-1}H(p-x),\] and therefore \[R_{\gamma,H}(x)=\gamma^{-1}H(x-p)\in
abla f(x)+\partial g(p).\] If \(
abla f\) is \(L_H\)-Lipschitz from the \(H\)-norm to the \(H^{-1}\)-norm, then \[\operatorname{dist}_{H^{-1}}(0,\partial(f+g)(p))\leq(1+\gamma L_H)\|R_{\gamma,H}(x)\|_{H^{-1}}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The metric-scaled displacement is a mixed-point first-order witness, and metric smoothness controls a true subgradient at the new point.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is convex and differentiable; \(g\) is proper, closed, and convex.
For the quantitative bound, \(\nabla f\) is \(L_H\)-Lipschitz in the stated metric pair.

knowledge_statements.title: Variable-Metric Step Optimality Witness
Variable-Metric Composite Residuals
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scaled proximal-gradient residual induced by a positive-definite metric.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) be symmetric positive definite. For convex differentiable \(f\), proper closed convex \(g\), and \(\gamma>0\), define \[p_{\gamma,H}(x)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{u}\left\{g(u)+\langle\nabla f(x),u-x\rangle+\frac{1}{2\gamma}\lVert u-x\rVert_H^2\right\},\qquad R_{\gamma,H}(x)=\gamma^{-1}H(x-p_{\gamma,H}(x)).\] Then \[R_{\gamma,H}(x)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad 0\in\nabla f(x)+\partial g(x)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x\in\operatorname*{argmin}(f+g).\] The scalar \(\lVert R_{\gamma,H}(x)\rVert_{H^{-1}}\) is the corresponding dual-metric residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive-definite metric scales the proximal displacement; the resulting residual vanishes exactly at composite minimizers.
assumptions_latex: f\text{ is convex and differentiable},\quad g\in\Gamma_0(\mathbb{R}^n)

children.title: Bregman Composite Residuals
children.top_down_role: Residuals adapted to non-Euclidean reference geometry.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Comparison under uniform curvature bounds for the reference geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(p=p_\gamma^\phi(x)\) and \(R_\gamma^\phi(x)=\gamma^{-1}(
abla\phi(x)-
abla\phi(p))\). If \(\phi\) is \(m\)-strongly convex and \(
abla\phi\) is \(M\)-Lipschitz, with respect to \(\|\cdot\|\), on a convex set containing \(x\) and \(p\), then \[ rac{m}{\gamma}\|x-p\|\leq\|R_\gamma^\phi(x)\|_*\leq rac{M}{\gamma}\|x-p\|.\] Hence Legendre geometry alone gives no uniform equivalence between primal displacement and mirror-coordinate magnitude.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lower and upper curvature bounds make primal Bregman displacement and mirror-coordinate residual quantitatively comparable.
assumptions_latex: \(\phi\) is \(m\)-strongly convex on the relevant convex set.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mixed-point first-order witness supplied by an attained Bregman proximal-gradient step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(p=p_\gamma^\phi(x)\) attain the Bregman proximal-gradient subproblem, and suppose its convex first-order condition applies. Then there exists \(s_p\in\partial g(p)\) such that \[0=s_p+
abla f(x)+\gamma^{-1}(
abla\phi(p)-
abla\phi(x)).\] Consequently, \[R_\gamma^\phi(x)=\gamma^{-1}(
abla\phi(x)-
abla\phi(p))=
abla f(x)+s_p\in
abla f(x)+\partial g(p).\] This is a mixed-point witness; it is not generally an element of \(\partial(f+g)(p)\) until \(
abla f(x)\) is related to \(

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The mirror-coordinate displacement equals the old smooth gradient plus a nonsmooth subgradient at the new Bregman point.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(\phi\) are differentiable at the displayed points.

abla f(x),u-xangle+\gamma^{-1}D_\phi(u,x)ight\}\] exists in \(\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}\phi)\), and define \(R_\gamma^\phi(x)=\gamma^{-1}(

children.title: Primal–Dual Certificate Families

children.title: Fenchel-Gap Certificates
children.top_down_role: Gap certificates for conjugate composite models.

knowledge_statements.title: Fenchel-Gap Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Computable primal–dual gap for a linearly composed Fenchel pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the primal problem \(P^\star=\inf_x\{f(x)+h(Kx)\}\) and dual problem \(D^\star=\sup_y\{-f^*(-K^*y)-h^*(y)\}\), define at any finite-valued pair \((x,y)\) \[\mathcal G_F(x,y)=f(x)+h(Kx)+f^*(-K^*y)+h^*(y).\] Fenchel–Young inequalities imply \(\mathcal G_F(x,y)\ge0\). Moreover, \(\mathcal G_F(x,y)=0\) if and only if \(-K^*y\in\partial f(x)\) and \(y\in\partial h(Kx)\). Hence \(\mathcal G_F(x,y)\le\varepsilon\) certifies a primal–dual objective gap of at most \(\varepsilon\), while zero certifies exact primal-dual optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The sum of primal and conjugate dual objectives is nonnegative and certifies exact optimality when it vanishes.
assumptions_latex: f,h\text{ are proper, closed, and convex}

source_refs.locator: 4 Duality and Optimality Conditions p. 67

source_witnesses.locator: 4 Duality and Optimality Conditions p. 67

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective-accuracy consequences of a finite Fenchel primal-dual gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p(x)=f(x)+h(Kx)\), \(d(y)=-f^*(-K^*y)-h^*(y)\), \(P^\star=\inf p\), and \(D^\star=\sup d\). If these values are finite at the displayed witnesses, then \[0\le p(x)-P^\star\le p(x)-d(y)=\mathcal G_F(x,y),\qquad 0\le D^\star-d(y)\le\mathcal G_F(x,y).\] Thus \(\mathcal G_F(x,y)\le\varepsilon\) certifies both inequalities without requiring strong duality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite Fenchel gap upper-bounds the primal and dual witnesses' respective objective errors by weak duality, even without strong duality.
assumptions_latex: f,h\text{ are proper, closed, and convex}
knowledge_statements.title: Fenchel-Gap One-Sided Error Bounds

children.title: Saddle-Gap Certificates
children.top_down_role: Gap certificates for saddle-representable objectives.

knowledge_statements.title: Saddle-Gap Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Restricted primal–dual gap certificate for a convex–concave saddle problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) and \(Y\) be nonempty convex sets, let \(L:X\times Y\to\mathbb{R}\) be convex in its first argument and concave in its second, and let \(\varepsilon\ge 0\). Define the saddle gap \[\mathcal G_L(x,y)=\sup_{v\in Y}L(x,v)-\inf_{u\in X}L(u,y).\] Whenever both displayed values are finite, \(\mathcal G_L(x,y)\ge0\). If \(\mathcal G_L(x,y)\le\varepsilon\), then \[L(x,v)-L(u,y)\le\varepsilon\quad\text{for all }(u,v)\in X\times Y.\] In particular, \(\mathcal G_L(x,y)=0\) if and only if \((x,y)\) is a saddle point of \(L\) on \(X\times Y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For any nonnegative tolerance, the supremum-minus-infimum saddle gap bounds every saddle inequality; zero gap is equivalent to a saddle point.
assumptions_latex: L(\cdot,y)\text{ is convex and }L(x,\cdot)\text{ is concave}

children.title: Polar-Set Certificates
children.top_down_role: Certificates expressed through polar sets for gauge or atomic structures.

knowledge_statements.title: Polar-Set Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Support-function certificate for membership in the polar of a convex set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty, closed, convex, and contain the origin. Its polar is \[C^\circ=\{z\in\mathbb{R}^n:\langle z,x\rangle\le1\text{ for every }x\in C\}.\] With the support function \(\sigma_C(z)=\sup_{x\in C}\langle z,x\rangle\), one has \[z\in C^\circ\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\sigma_C(z)\le1.\] Thus any verifiable upper bound \(U\ge\sigma_C(z)\) with \(U\le1\) certifies polar membership; conversely, an \(x\in C\) satisfying \(\langle z,x\rangle>1\) certifies nonmembership.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Polar membership is certified by a support-function bound at most one; a point of the original set violating the bound certifies nonmembership.
assumptions_latex: C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\text{ is nonempty, closed, and convex}

children.title: Dual-Norm Certificates
children.top_down_role: Certificates expressed through dual-norm bounds for norm-regularized structures.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Norm Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual-norm and complementarity certificate for a scaled norm subgradient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\lVert\cdot\rVert\) be a norm on \(\mathbb{R}^n\), let \(\lVert\cdot\rVert_*\) be its dual norm, and let \(\lambda>0\). For \(x,z\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \[z\in\partial\bigl(\lambda\lVert\cdot\rVert\bigr)(x)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \lVert z\rVert_*\le\lambda\ \text{ and }\ \langle z,x\rangle=\lambda\lVert x\rVert.\] Accordingly, the dual-norm inequality certifies dual feasibility and the equality certifies complementarity. At \(x=0\), the equality is automatic, so \(\lVert z\rVert_*\le\lambda\) alone exactly certifies subgradient membership.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A scaled-norm subgradient is certified by dual-norm feasibility plus equality in Hölder’s inequality; at zero only dual feasibility remains.

source_refs.locator: 3.2 Properties of the Subdifferential Set p. 39

source_witnesses.locator: 3.2 Properties of the Subdifferential Set p. 39

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dual-Norm Optimality Certificate for Norm-Regularized Objectives
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Specialization of the dual-norm subgradient test to a differentiable convex loss plus a norm penalty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\ell:\mathbb R^n	o\mathbb R\) be convex and differentiable, let \(\|\cdot\|\) be a norm with dual norm \(\|\cdot\|_*\), and let \(\lambda>0\). Then \[x^\star\in\operatorname*{argmin}_x\{\ell(x)+\lambda\|x\|\}\iff \|
abla\ell(x^\star)\|_*\le\lambda\ 	ext{ and }\ \langle-
abla\ell(x^\star),x^\starangle=\lambda\|x^\star\|.\] In particular, \(0\) is optimal if and only if \(\|
abla\ell(0)\|_*\le\lambda\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimality for a differentiable convex loss plus a norm penalty is certified by dual-norm feasibility and Hölder equality; at zero it reduces to a dual-norm threshold.

notation.meaning: Gradient of the differentiable convex loss.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Norm Optimality Certificate for Norm-Regularized Objectives

children.title: Gauge-Polar Certificates
children.top_down_role: Certificates specialized to gauge geometry and its polar representation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional first-order certificate for a differentiable convex loss plus a proper closed gauge.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\gamma_C\) be a proper closed convex gauge and define its polar gauge by \(\gamma_C^\circ(z)=\sup\{\langle z,u\rangle:\gamma_C(u)\le1\}\). For convex differentiable \(f\), \(\lambda>0\), and \(x\in\operatorname{dom}\gamma_C\), set \(z=-\nabla f(x)\). Then \[x\in\operatorname*{argmin}_u\{f(u)+\lambda\gamma_C(u)\}\] if and only if \[\gamma_C^\circ(z)\le\lambda,\qquad \langle z,x\rangle=\lambda\gamma_C(x).\] Equivalently, \(z\in\lambda\partial\gamma_C(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimality for a differentiable loss plus a gauge is certified by polar feasibility and saturation of the gauge-polar pairing.
assumptions_latex: \(\gamma_C\) is a proper closed convex gauge
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x\text{ is optimal}\iff \gamma_C^\circ(-\nabla f(x))\le\lambda\text{ and }\langle-\nabla f(x),x\rangle=\lambda\gamma_C(x).
knowledge_statements.title: Gauge-Polar Optimality Certificate

assumptions_latex: \(E\) is a finite-dimensional real inner-product space.
\(C\subset E\) is closed and convex with \(0\in C\), and its gauge \(\gamma_C\) is proper.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\) minimizes \(f+\lambda\gamma_C\) exactly when the displayed polar inequalities and complementarity equality hold.

notation.meaning: polar gauge, defined as the support over the gauge unit ball

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional first-order certificate for a differentiable loss plus a convex gauge.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define \(\gamma_C(x)=\inf\{t>0:x\in tC\}\) and \(\gamma_C^\circ(z)=\sup\{\langle z,u\rangle:\gamma_C(u)\leq 1\}\). For any \(x\in\operatorname{dom}\gamma_C\), set \(z=-\nabla f(x)\). Then \(z\) is a gauge-polar optimality certificate for \(x\) precisely when
\[\gamma_C^\circ(z)\leq\lambda\quad\text{and}\quad \langle z,x\rangle=\lambda\gamma_C(x).\]
Equivalently, \(z\in\lambda\partial\gamma_C(x)\), so \(0\in\nabla f(x)+\lambda\partial\gamma_C(x)\). By convexity, this condition is equivalent to global optimality of \(x\) for \(\min_u f(u)+\lambda\gamma_C(u)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A point is optimal for a loss plus gauge penalty exactly when its negative gradient lies in the scaled polar ball and saturates the gauge-polar pairing.
knowledge_statements.title: Gauge-Polar Certificates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate is mathematically standard and fits the leaf, but no source or inspectable locator supports the gauge-polar subdifferential characterization.

children.title: Sparsity Screening Certificates
children.top_down_role: Polar or dual-norm certificates used to validate sparsity structure.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantifier-correct safe screening for l1-regularized convex optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal X^\star\) be the optimizer set of \(f(x)+\lambda\|x\|_1\), where \(f\) is convex and differentiable and \(\lambda>0\). Suppose a certified set \(Z\) contains \(-\nabla f(x^\star)\) for every \(x^\star\in\mathcal X^\star\). Then \[\sup_{z\in Z}|z_i|<\lambda\quad\Longrightarrow\quad x_i^\star=0\quad\text{for every }x^\star\in\mathcal X^\star.\] Containment of only one optimizer's dual vector certifies only that optimizer; an uncertified region or a non-strict bound does not justify safe elimination.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A coordinate is safely removable for all optimizers only when a certified region contains every compatible optimal negative gradient and remains strictly inside that coordinate's dual boundary.

notation.meaning: certified region containing all compatible optimal negative gradients

knowledge_statements.title: Safe-Region Coordinate Screening

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Gap-Safe Ball Screening for the Lasso
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete coordinate screening using a primal-dual-gap ball.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(P(x)=\tfrac12\|Ax-b\|_2^2+\lambda\|x\|_1\), define \[D(\theta)=\tfrac12\|b\|_2^2-\tfrac{\lambda^2}{2}\|\theta-b/\lambda\|_2^2,\qquad \|A^T\theta\|_\infty\le1.\] Given a primal point \(x\) and dual-feasible \(\theta\), let \(G=P(x)-D(\theta)\) and \(r=\sqrt{2G}/\lambda\). The unique dual optimum \(\theta^\star\) lies in \(B(\theta,r)\). Hence, for column \(a_i\) of \(A\), \[|a_i^T\theta|+\|a_i\|_2r<1\quad\Longrightarrow\quad x_i^\star=0\] for every primal optimum \(x^\star\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Lasso coordinate is safely eliminated when its maximum possible optimal dual correlation over the gap-derived ball is strictly below one.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is evaluated from a primal point and a dual-feasible point

notation.meaning: ith column of the design matrix

knowledge_statements.title: Gap-Safe Ball Screening for the Lasso

assumptions_latex: \(Z\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is a certified set containing \(z^\star=-\nabla f(x^\star)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\sup_{z\in Z}|z_i|<\lambda\), then every compatible optimizer satisfies \(x_i^\star=0\).

notation.meaning: safe set containing the unknown optimal dual vector

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safe coordinate screening for the convex ℓ1-regularized problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The optimality condition gives \(z^\star\in\lambda\partial\lVert x^\star\rVert_1\). Hence, for each coordinate \(i\), nonzero \(x_i^\star\) requires \(|z_i^\star|=\lambda\), whereas \(|z_i^\star|<\lambda\) forces \(x_i^\star=0\). Consequently, any computable safe set \(Z\) satisfying \(z^\star\in Z\) yields the screening certificate
\[\sup_{z\in Z}|z_i|<\lambda\quad\Longrightarrow\quad x_i^\star=0.\]
The implication is safe only when containment of \(z^\star\) in \(Z\) is itself certified; an estimated set without that guarantee does not justify eliminating the coordinate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A coordinate can be safely removed when a certified region for the optimal dual vector stays strictly inside that coordinate’s ℓ∞ boundary.
knowledge_statements.title: Sparsity Screening Certificates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed implication certifies the selected optimizer only. Safe removal for every optimizer requires Z to contain every compatible optimal dual vector or an appropriate uniqueness assumption. A source is also absent.

children.title: Spectral Certificates
children.top_down_role: Dual-geometric certificates for matrix and low-rank regularizers.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual-saturation and singular-subspace forms of nuclear-norm optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^{m\times n}\to\mathbb R\) be convex and differentiable, \(\lambda>0\), and let \(X=U\Sigma V^T\) be a compact SVD when \(X\ne0\). With \(Z=-\nabla f(X)\), the following are equivalent: \[(i)\quad X\in\operatorname*{argmin}_Y\{f(Y)+\lambda\|Y\|_*\};\] \[(ii)\quad \|Z\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\lambda,\qquad \langle Z,X\rangle_F=\lambda\|X\|_*;\] \[(iii)\quad Z=\lambda(UV^T+W),\quad U^TW=0,\quad WV=0,\quad\|W\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le1.\] At \(X=0\), the certificate reduces to \(\|Z\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\lambda\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nuclear-norm optimality is equivalently certified by operator-norm feasibility and dual saturation, or by exact matching on active singular spaces with a bounded orthogonal remainder.
assumptions_latex: The SVD form is used for \(X\ne0\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: X\text{ is optimal}\iff Z\in\lambda\partial\|X\|_*\iff\text{the displayed spectral conditions hold}.
knowledge_statements.title: Equivalent Nuclear-Norm Spectral Certificates

assumptions_latex: \(\lambda>0\), and the regularizer is the nuclear norm \(\lVert\cdot\rVert_*\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X\) is optimal exactly when \(Z=-\nabla f(X)\) satisfies \(\lVert Z\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\leq\lambda\) and \(\langle Z,X\rangle_F=\lambda\lVert X\rVert_*\).

notation.meaning: nuclear norm, the sum of singular values
operator norm, the largest singular value

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nuclear-norm optimality certificate expressed through the dual operator norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Set \(Z=-
abla f(X)\). Because the nuclear and operator norms are dual, \(Z\in\lambda\partial\lVert XVert_*\) holds exactly when
\[\lVert ZVert_{\mathrm{op}}\leq\lambda\quad	ext{and}\quad \langle Z,Xangle_F=\lambda\lVert XVert_*.\]
Therefore these two spectral conditions are equivalent to \(0\in
abla f(X)+\lambda\partial\lVert XVert_*\), and hence certify that \(X\) globally minimizes \(f(U)+\lambda\lVert UVert_*\). When \(X
eq0\), the equality additionally requires saturation of the operator-nuclear norm inequality on the singular subspaces active in \(X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For nuclear-norm regularization, the negative gradient certifies optimality when its operator norm is bounded and its pairing with the candidate saturates duality.
knowledge_statements.title: Spectral Certificates

children.title: Approximate-Solution Reporting
children.top_down_role: Distinct reporting interfaces for value, stationarity, feasibility, and dual quality.

children.title: Objective-Quality Reporting
children.top_down_role: Approximation described through objective values and bounds.

assumptions_latex: \(x\in\operatorname{dom}F\), and \(L\) is a certified lower bound on \(p^\star\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Absolute objective-quality certificate from a candidate value and a valid lower bound.

source_refs.locator: 3.1.9 Basic Elements of Primal-Dual Methods p. 191

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define the reported objective-quality gap by \(\Delta_{\mathrm{obj}}(x;L)=F(x)-L\). Since \(L\leq p^\star\leq F(x)\), one has
\[0\leq F(x)-p^\star\leq\Delta_{\mathrm{obj}}(x;L).\]
Thus \(\Delta_{\mathrm{obj}}(x;L)\leq\varepsilon\) is a verifiable absolute \(\varepsilon\)-objective certificate. The report must identify both \(F(x)\) and the provenance of \(L\); a candidate objective value alone supplies an upper bound but does not quantify suboptimality. A relative report may divide the gap by a declared positive scale, but it must retain the absolute gap and scaling convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Report the candidate objective and a certified lower bound; their difference upper-bounds the candidate’s objective suboptimality.
knowledge_statements.title: Objective-Quality Reporting

source_witnesses.locator: 3.1.9 Basic Elements of Primal-Dual Methods p. 191

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Objective Accuracy Does Not Imply Iterate or Stationarity Accuracy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limits of an objective-value certificate without conditioning assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Even when \(F\) is proper, closed, convex, and attains \(p^\star\), a bound \(F(x)-p^\star\leq\varepsilon\) need not control \(\operatorname{dist}(x,\operatorname{argmin}F)\) or the subdifferential residual. Indeed, for \(F_a(t)=a|t|\), \(a>0\), and \(t=M>0\), one has \[F_a(M)-F_a(0)=aM,\qquad \operatorname{dist}(M,\operatorname{argmin}F_a)=M,\qquad \operatorname{dist}(0,\partial F_a(M))=a.\] Choosing \(a=\varepsilon/M\) keeps the objective gap equal to \(\varepsilon\) while the distance becomes arbitrarily large and the stationarity residual convention varies with the scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A small objective gap alone gives neither iterate accuracy nor a uniform stationarity guarantee; conversions require growth or conditioning assumptions.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is proper, closed, convex, and has a minimizer.
No growth, error-bound, strong-convexity, or uniform scaling assumption is imposed.
knowledge_statements.title: Objective Accuracy Does Not Imply Iterate or Stationarity Accuracy

children.title: Stationarity Reporting
children.top_down_role: Approximation described through composite residuals.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Stationarity Thresholds Require Declared Geometry and Conditioning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interpretive boundary for approximate stationarity reports.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A report \(\|R(x)\|\leq\varepsilon\) must declare the residual map, norm, scaling, and any stepsize or metric parameters. Exact vanishing may characterize optimality, but small subdifferential or proximal-gradient-type residuals do not uniformly imply objective or iterate accuracy over unconditioned convex problem classes. For \(F_a(t)=a|t|\) and \(t=M>0\), \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial F_a(M))=a\) while \(F_a(M)-F_a(0)=aM\) and the distance to the minimizer is \(M\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stationarity tolerance is meaningful only with its residual geometry, and it does not automatically certify objective or iterate accuracy.
assumptions_latex: The residual convention and its zero-set interpretation are declared.
No error-bound, growth, or uniform conditioning hypothesis is imposed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \|R(x)\|\leq\varepsilon\text{ alone is not a uniform objective-gap or distance-to-solution certificate over unconditioned convex classes}.
knowledge_statements.title: Stationarity Thresholds Require Declared Geometry and Conditioning

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lVert G_\eta(x)\rVert\leq\varepsilon\) is a composite stationarity report, and \(G_\eta(x)=0\) is equivalent to optimality.

notation.meaning: proximal map of the scaled nonsmooth component
positive stepsize used in the residual

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proximal-gradient residual for unconstrained convex composite minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define
\[G_\eta(x)=\eta^{-1}\bigl(x-\operatorname{prox}_{\eta g}(x-\eta\nabla f(x))\bigr).\]
The scalar \(\lVert G_\eta(x)\rVert\) is a computable composite stationarity residual at the declared stepsize \(\eta\). A report \(\lVert G_\eta(x)\rVert\leq\varepsilon\) therefore states \(\varepsilon\)-stationarity in this residual convention. Moreover,
\[G_\eta(x)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad 0\in\nabla f(x)+\partial g(x),\]
and, by convexity, this is equivalent to global optimality. Residual magnitudes obtained with different stepsizes or norms are not directly comparable unless the report also specifies those conventions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Composite stationarity is reported by the norm of a declared proximal-gradient mapping; zero residual is exactly the convex optimality condition.
knowledge_statements.title: Stationarity Reporting

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proximal-gradient residual and zero-residual equivalence are correctly stated for the declared convex composite setting, but no source or locator is supplied.

children.title: Feasibility Residual Reporting

assumptions_latex: \(A:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) is linear, \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), and \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is nonempty and closed.
The norms used for equality residuals and distances are declared.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact feasibility is equivalent to \(r_{\mathrm{eq}}(x)=r_C(x)=0\); approximate feasibility is reported by explicit bounds on both residuals.

notation.meaning: distance induced by the declared norm

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual convention for equality constraints and closed-set membership.

source_refs.locator: 2.3.1 Geometry of the primal and dual problems p. 53

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the feasibility requirements \(Ax=b\) and \(x\in C\), define
\[r_{\mathrm{eq}}(x)=\lVert Ax-b\rVert,\qquad r_C(x)=\operatorname{dist}(x,C)=\inf_{u\in C}\lVert x-u\rVert.\]
A feasibility-residual report consists of the ordered pair \((r_{\mathrm{eq}}(x),r_C(x))\), together with the norms and any scaling used. The point is exactly feasible if and only if both entries vanish. Given tolerances \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{eq}},\varepsilon_C\geq0\), it is approximately feasible in this convention when \(r_{\mathrm{eq}}(x)\leq\varepsilon_{\mathrm{eq}}\) and \(r_C(x)\leq\varepsilon_C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Report equality violation and distance to the constraint set separately, with declared norms and scales; both vanish exactly at feasible points.
knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility Residual Reporting

children.top_down_role: Reporting conventions for primal–dual or saddle-gap quantities.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal–Dual Gap Reporting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fenchel primal-dual gap for a linearly composed convex objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the primal problem \(\inf_x P(x)\), where \(P(x)=f(Ax)+g(x)\), define the dual value \(D(y)=-f^*(y)-g^*(-A^\top y)\). The reported primal-dual gap is
\[G(x,y)=P(x)-D(y)=f(Ax)+g(x)+f^*(y)+g^*(-A^\top y).\]
Fenchel inequalities imply \(G(x,y)\geq0\). If \(p^\star\) is the primal infimum, weak duality gives \(D(y)\leq p^\star\leq P(x)\), and hence \(0\leq P(x)-p^\star\leq G(x,y)\). Thus \(G(x,y)\leq\varepsilon\) certifies at most \(\varepsilon\) objective suboptimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a Fenchel primal-dual pair, subtract the dual value from the primal value; this nonnegative gap certifies objective accuracy by weak duality.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^m\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) and \(g:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) are proper, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The reported gap is nonnegative and upper-bounds primal suboptimality whenever the dual value is a valid lower bound.

source_refs.locator: 3.1.9 Basic Elements of Primal-Dual Methods p. 191

source_witnesses.locator: 3.1.9 Basic Elements of Primal-Dual Methods p. 191

children.title: Joint Tolerance Interpretation
children.top_down_role: Interpretation of simultaneous feasibility and gap tolerances.

assumptions_latex: A primal-dual formulation supplies nonnegative primal residual \(r_p\), dual residual \(r_d\), and gap \(G\).
All norms, normalizations, and objective scaling conventions are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Joint acceptance means \(r_p\leq\varepsilon_p\), \(r_d\leq\varepsilon_d\), and \(G\leq\varepsilon_g\), with no tolerance substituting for another.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Componentwise interpretation of feasibility, dual residual, and gap tolerances.

source_refs.locator: 3.1.9 Basic Elements of Primal-Dual Methods p. 191

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A joint tolerance report accepts a candidate pair only when
\[r_p\leq\varepsilon_p,\qquad r_d\leq\varepsilon_d,\qquad G\leq\varepsilon_g.\]
Each inequality has a distinct interpretation: \(r_p\) controls primal feasibility, \(r_d\) controls dual feasibility or stationarity, and \(G\) controls objective separation when it is formed from valid primal and dual bounds. A small gap cannot compensate for excessive infeasibility, and small residuals alone need not imply a small objective gap without additional conditioning or error-bound assumptions. Any aggregate stopping rule must therefore preserve, or make recoverable, the three componentwise bounds and their normalization conventions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A joint certificate must meet separate primal-residual, dual-residual, and gap tolerances; success in one component does not replace another.
knowledge_statements.title: Joint Tolerance Interpretation

source_witnesses.locator: 3.1.9 Basic Elements of Primal-Dual Methods p. 191

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent scalar encoding of componentwise joint tolerances when all denominators are positive.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(r_p,r_d,G\ge0\) and \(\varepsilon_p,\varepsilon_d,\varepsilon_g>0\). Define
\[R_{\max}=\max\left\{\frac{r_p}{\varepsilon_p},\frac{r_d}{\varepsilon_d},\frac{G}{\varepsilon_g}\right\}.\]
Then
\[R_{\max}\le1\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad r_p\le\varepsilon_p,\;r_d\le\varepsilon_d,\;G\le\varepsilon_g.\]
Zero tolerances must remain exact componentwise tests rather than denominators.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The maximum of the tolerance-normalized components exactly encodes joint acceptance when positive normalizations are declared; zero tolerances remain separate exact tests.
assumptions_latex: Residual, gap, norm, and scaling conventions are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_{\max}\le1\) if and only if all three componentwise tolerance inequalities hold.
knowledge_statements.title: Normalized Maximum Joint Test
